translations.idiomatic: (Clan great-grandson Hui; Hui's son Longzhi; Hui's younger brother Su; clan younger cousin Shu)

sentences.zh: 崔逞，字叔祖，清河東武城人，魏中尉琰之五世孫也。

translations.literal: Cui Cheng, styled Shuzu, was a man of Dongwucheng in Qinghe, fifth-generation descendant of Wei Commandant of Justice Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Cheng, styled Shuzu, came from Dongwucheng in Qinghe — fifth in descent from Yan, Commandant of Justice under Wei.

sentences.zh: 曾祖諒，晉中書令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Liang was Jin Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Liang had been Jin Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 祖遇，仕石氏，為特進。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yu served the Shi clan as Special Grand Master.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yu served the Later Zhao as Special Grand Master.

sentences.zh: 父瑜，黃門郎。

translations.literal: His father Yu was a Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu held office as Gentleman at the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 逞少好學，有文才。

translations.literal: Cheng from youth loved learning and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Cheng loved books and showed real literary gift.

sentences.zh: 仕慕容痈，補著作郎，撰《燕記》。

translations.literal: He served Murong Jun, was made Aide in the Bureau of Writings, and compiled the Records of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Murong Jun he became Aide in the Bureau of Writings and compiled the Records of Yan.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 痈滅，苻堅以為齊郡太守。

translations.literal: When Jun fell, Fu Jian made him Administrator of Qi commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun's state collapsed, Fu Jian appointed him Administrator of Qi.

sentences.zh: 堅敗，仕晉，曆清河、平原二郡太守。

translations.literal: After Fu Jian's defeat he entered Jin service and successively governed Qinghe and Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Jian's ruin he entered Jin service and in turn governed Qinghe and Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 為翟遼所虜，以為中書令。

translations.literal: Captured by Zhai Liao, he was made Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Zhai Liao took him captive and made him Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 慕容垂滅翟釗，以為秘書監。

translations.literal: When Murong Chui destroyed Zhai Zhao, he was made Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Chui destroyed Zhai Zhao, he became Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 慕容寶東走和龍，為留台吏部尚書。

translations.literal: When Murong Bao fled east to Helong, Cheng remained at the rear capital as Minister of the Civil Service.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Bao fled east to Helong, Cheng stayed behind as Minister of the Civil Service.

sentences.zh: 及慕容驎立，逞攜妻子歸魏。

translations.literal: When Murong Lin acceded, Cheng brought wife and children and returned to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: When Murong Lin took the throne, Cheng brought wife and children home to Wei.

sentences.zh: 張袞先稱美之，由是道武禮遇甚厚。

translations.literal: Zhang Gun had praised him first; hence Daowu treated him with great favor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gun had praised him first, and Daowu therefore favored him richly.

sentences.zh: 拜尚書，錄三十六曹，別給吏屬，居門下省。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of the Secretariat, recorded the affairs of the thirty-six bureaus, was given separate clerks, and dwelt in the Gate Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Minister of the Secretariat, oversaw all thirty-six bureaus with his own clerks, and lodged in the Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 尋除御史中丞。

translations.literal: Soon after he was made Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became Imperial Censor.

sentences.zh: 道武攻中山，未克，六軍乏糧，問計於逞。

translations.literal: Daowu besieged Zhongshan without taking it; the six armies lacked grain and he asked Cheng for counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu besieged Zhongshan without success; the armies ran short of grain, and he asked Cheng's counsel.

sentences.zh: 逞曰：「飛鴞食葚而改音，《詩》稱其事，可取以助糧。

translations.literal: Cheng said: "When the flying owl eats mulberries its cry changes — the Odes praise the matter; mulberries may be taken to supplement grain.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng said, "The flying owl eats mulberries and its cry changes — the Odes mark the thing. Mulberries could help feed the army."

sentences.zh: 」帝雖銜其侮慢，然兵既須食，乃聽人以葚當租。

translations.literal: " Though the Emperor resented his insolence, the troops needed food, and he allowed mulberries to be taken in lieu of rent.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor bridled at the insolence, yet the troops needed food — so mulberries were accepted in place of rent.

sentences.zh: 逞又言：「可使軍人及時自取，過時則落盡。

translations.literal: Cheng added: "Soldiers could gather them in season; after the season they fall and are gone."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng added that soldiers should gather them in season, "for afterward they drop and are wasted."

sentences.zh: 」帝怒曰：「內賊未平，兵人安可解甲收葚乎！

translations.literal: The Emperor raged: "With rebels within not yet subdued, how may soldiers doff armor to pick mulberries!"
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flared: "Rebels within are not yet crushed — shall soldiers strip armor to pick mulberries?"

sentences.zh: 」以中山未拔，故不加罪。

translations.literal: Because Zhongshan was still untaken, he did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongshan still held out, so no punishment followed.

sentences.zh: 及姚興侵晉，襄陽戍將郗恢馳使乞師于常山王遵，書云「賢兄武步中原」。

translations.literal: When Yao Xing invaded Jin, the garrison commander of Xiangyang, Xi Hui, sent a swift messenger begging troops from the Prince of Changshan, Zun; the letter read, "Your worthy elder brother strides in martial glory through the Central Plains."
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Xing struck Jin, Xi Hui at Xiangyang sent a rider begging aid from Prince of Changshan Zun; the letter said, "Your worthy elder brother strides in arms through the Central Plains."

sentences.zh: 道武以為悖君臣之體，敕逞與張袞為遵書答使，亦貶其主號以報之。

translations.literal: Daowu judged this a breach of the bond between ruler and subject and ordered Cheng and Zhang Gun to draft Zun's reply to the envoy, also demoting the addressee's sovereign title in the response.
translations.idiomatic: Daowu called this a breach of ruler and subject and ordered Cheng and Gun to draft Zun's reply — and to demote the Jin ruler's title in it.

sentences.zh: 逞、袞為書，乃云「貴主」。

translations.literal: Cheng and Gun wrote the letter and used only "Your exalted lord."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng and Gun wrote back with merely "Your exalted lord."

sentences.zh: 帝怒其失旨，黜袞，遂賜逞死。

translations.literal: The Emperor, furious at missing the point, demoted Gun and had Cheng put to death.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor, furious they had missed his intent, demoted Gun and sentenced Cheng to death.

sentences.zh: 後晉荊州刺史司馬休之等數十人為桓玄所逐，皆將來奔。

translations.literal: Later Jin's Inspector of Jingzhou, Sima Xiuzhi, and several dozen others driven out by Huan Xuan were all coming to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Later Sima Xiuzhi, Inspector of Jingzhou, and dozens more expelled by Huan Xuan were all fleeing north to surrender.

sentences.zh: 至陳留，聞逞被殺，分為二輩：一奔長安，一奔廣固。

translations.literal: At Chenliu they heard Cheng had been killed and split into two bands: one fled to Chang'an, one to Guanggu.
translations.idiomatic: At Chenliu they heard Cheng was dead and split: one band ran to Chang'an, one to Guanggu.

sentences.zh: 帝聞深悔，自是士人有過，多見優容。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard, he deeply regretted it; thereafter when scholars erred they were often treated leniently.
translations.idiomatic: The news filled the Emperor with bitter regret; thereafter scholars who stumbled were usually spared harshly.

sentences.zh: 逞子毅、禕、嚴、頤。

translations.literal: Cheng's sons were Yi, Wei, Yan, and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's sons were Yi, Wei, Yan, and Yi.

sentences.zh: 初，逞之內徙，終慮不免，乃使其妻張氏與四子歸慕容德於廣固，獨與小子頤在代京。

translations.literal: At first, when Cheng moved inward, he always feared he would not escape harm; he sent his wife Lady Zhang and four sons back to Murong De at Guanggu, keeping only his youngest, Yi, at Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng first moved inward he feared he could not escape ruin; he sent Lady Zhang and four sons to Murong De at Guanggu and kept only young Yi at Dai.

sentences.zh: 及逞死，亦以此為譴。

translations.literal: When Cheng died, this too was held against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng died, even that was counted against him.

sentences.zh: 頤字太沖，散騎常侍，賜爵清河侯。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Taichong, was Regular Attendant at the Secretariat and enfeoffed as Marquis of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Taichong, became Regular Attendant at the Secretariat and Marquis of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 太武聞宋以其兄諲為冀州刺史，乃曰：「義隆用其兄，我豈無冀州地邪？

translations.literal: Taiwu heard that Song had made his elder brother Shen Inspector of Ji and said: "Yilong employs his brother — do I lack land in Ji?"
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu heard Song had made his brother Shen Inspector of Ji and said, "Yilong uses his brother — have I no Ji province?"

sentences.zh: 」乃以頤為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: " He thereupon made Yi Inspector of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He promptly made Yi Inspector of Ji.

sentences.zh: 入為大鴻臚，持節策拜楊難當為南秦王。

translations.literal: He entered court as Grand Herald and, bearing credentials, invested Yang Nandang as King of Southern Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Grand Herald and, with credentials, invested Yang Nandang as King of Southern Qin.

sentences.zh: 奉使數返，光揚朝命，太武善之。

translations.literal: On missions he returned again and again, spreading the court's renown; Taiwu was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: On repeated embassies he bore the court's dignity abroad; Taiwu approved.

sentences.zh: 後與方士韋文秀詣王屋山造金丹，不就。

translations.literal: Later he went with the adept Wei Wenxiu to Mount Wangwu to compound the golden elixir, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Later he went with adept Wei Wenxiu to Mount Wangwu to seek the golden elixir and failed.

sentences.zh: 真君初，卒。

translations.literal: At the start of the Zhenjun era he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the opening of the Zhenjun era.

sentences.zh: 始崔浩與頤及榮陽太守模等，年皆相次。

translations.literal: At first Cui Hao, Yi, and Mo, Administrator of Xingyang, were nearly the same age.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hao, Yi, and Mo of Xingyang were nearly of an age.

sentences.zh: 浩為長，次模，次頤。

translations.literal: Hao was eldest, then Mo, then Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Hao was eldest, Mo next, Yi last.

sentences.zh: 三人別祖，而模、頤為親。

translations.literal: The three traced to different ancestors, but Mo and Yi were close kin.
translations.idiomatic: They sprang from different lines, yet Mo and Yi were close kin.

sentences.zh: 浩恃其家世魏、晉公卿，常侮模、頤。

translations.literal: Hao relied on his family's generations of Wei and Jin high office and often insulted Mo and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Hao leaned on generations of Wei and Jin grandees and often belittled Mo and Yi.

sentences.zh: 浩不信佛道，模深所歸向，雖糞壤中，禮拜形像。

translations.literal: Hao did not believe in Buddhism; Mo was deeply devoted — even in filth he would bow to images.
translations.idiomatic: Hao scorned the Buddha; Mo was devout and would bow to images even in filth.

sentences.zh: 浩大笑曰：「持此頭顱，不淨處跪是胡神也！

translations.literal: Hao laughed loudly: "To kneel in unclean places with that head of yours — to these barbarian gods!"
translations.idiomatic: Hao laughed: "You kneel your head in filth before barbarian gods!"

sentences.zh: 」模嘗謂人曰：「桃簡可欺我，何容輕我周兒也！

translations.literal: " Mo once told others: "Taojian may deceive me — how dare he slight my Zhou'er!"
translations.idiomatic: Mo once said, "Taojian may fool me — how dare he slight my Zhou'er!"

sentences.zh: 」浩小名桃簡，頤小名周兒。

translations.literal: " Hao's childhood name was Taojian; Yi's was Zhou'er.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's pet name was Taojian; Yi's was Zhou'er.

sentences.zh: 太武頗聞之，故浩誅時，二家獲免。

translations.literal: Taiwu heard much of this; hence when Hao was executed both their houses were spared.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwu heard of it; when Hao was executed both families were spared.

sentences.zh: 頤五子。

translations.literal: Yi had five sons.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had five sons.

sentences.zh: 少子睿以交通境外，伏誅。

translations.literal: The youngest, Rui, was executed for trafficking with foreign lands.
translations.idiomatic: The youngest, Rui, was executed for dealing with outsiders.

sentences.zh: 自逞之死，至睿之誅，三世，積五十餘年，在北一門盡矣。

translations.literal: From Cheng's death to Rui's execution, three generations and more than fifty years — the northern branch of the house was ended.
translations.idiomatic: From Cheng's death to Rui's execution three generations and fifty years passed — the northern line was extinguished.

sentences.zh: 彧字文若，頤兄禕之孫也。

translations.literal: Yu, styled Wenruo, was grandson of Wei's son through Yi's elder brother Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, styled Wenruo, was grandson of Wei, son of Yi's elder brother Wei.

sentences.zh: 父勳之，字甯國，位大司馬、外兵郎，贈通直郎。

translations.literal: His father Xunzhi, styled Ningguo, held Grand Marshal and Outer Troops Officer, posthumously made Direct Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xunzhi, styled Ningguo, reached Grand Marshal and Outer Troops Officer and was posthumously made Direct Attendant.

sentences.zh: 彧與兄相如俱自宋入魏。

translations.literal: Yu and his elder brother Xiangru both came from Song into Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yu and elder brother Xiangru both entered Wei from Song.

sentences.zh: 相如以才學知名，早卒。

translations.literal: Xiangru was known for talent and learning and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangru was famed for learning and died young.

sentences.zh: 彧少逢隱沙門，教以《素問》、《甲乙》，遂善醫術。

translations.literal: Yu in youth met a recluse monk who taught him the Plain Questions and the A and B Canon of Acupuncture; he became skilled in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Yu met a recluse monk who taught the Plain Questions and the A–B Canon; he mastered medicine.

sentences.zh: 中山王英子略曾病，王顯等不能療。

translations.literal: The son of Prince of Zhongshan Ying, Zilue, once fell ill; Wang Xian and others could not cure him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying's son Zilue fell ill; Wang Xian and others could not heal him.

sentences.zh: 彧針之，抽針即愈，後位冀州別駕。

translations.literal: Yu needled him; at withdrawal of the needle he recovered — later he was Aide of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Yu needled him; the needle scarcely left before he was well — later he became Aide of Ji.

sentences.zh: 性仁恕，見疹者，喜與療之。

translations.literal: By nature he was kind and forgiving; seeing the afflicted, he delighted to treat them.
translations.idiomatic: Kind by nature, he delighted to treat whoever was sick.

sentences.zh: 廣教門生，令多救療。

translations.literal: He widely taught disciples and had many save lives through treatment.
translations.idiomatic: He taught many pupils and sent them out to heal.

sentences.zh: 其弟子清河趙約、勃海郝文法之徒，咸亦有名。

translations.literal: Among his pupils, Zhao Yue of Qinghe and Hao Wenfa of Bohai and others also won names.
translations.idiomatic: Pupils such as Zhao Yue of Qinghe and Hao Wenfa of Bohai won names in turn.

sentences.zh: 彧子景哲，豪率，亦以醫術知名。

translations.literal: Yu's son Jingzhe was bold and open — also famed in medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's son Jingzhe was bold and open, likewise famed in medicine.

sentences.zh: 仕魏，太中大夫、司徒長史。

translations.literal: Serving Wei, he was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Chief Clerk of the Minister of State.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei he was Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Chief Clerk to the Minister of State.

sentences.zh: 景哲子冏，字法峻，幼好學，泛覽經傅，多伎藝，尤工相術。

translations.literal: Jingzhe's son Jiong, styled Fajun, from youth loved learning, ranged through classics and commentaries, had many arts, and was especially skilled in physiognomy.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhe's son Jiong, styled Fajun, loved learning from youth, ranged the classics, mastered many arts, and excelled at physiognomy.

sentences.zh: 仕魏為司空參軍。

translations.literal: In Wei he was Aide to the Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei he served as Aide to the Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，為尚藥典禦。

translations.literal: At the start of Qi Tianbao he was Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi Tianbao's opening he became Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 曆高陽太守、太子家令。

translations.literal: He successively was Administrator of Gaoyang and Household Master of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was in turn Administrator of Gaoyang and Household Master of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 武平中，為散騎常侍、假儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the Wuping era he was Regular Attendant and Acting Commissioner with Protocol Equal to the Three Dukes.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping he was Regular Attendant with acting protocol equal to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 從幸晉陽，嘗謂中書侍郎李德林曰：「比日看高相王以下文武官人相表，俱盡其事，口不忍言。

translations.literal: On an imperial visit to Jinyang he once told Secretariat Vice Director Li Delin: "These days I have read the physiognomies of civil and military officers down from the High Chancellor — all to the end of their fate; I cannot bear to speak it."
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyang he told Li Delin, "I have read the faces of every officer down from the High Chancellor — each to the end of his fate; I cannot speak it aloud."

sentences.zh: 唯弟一人更應富貴，當在他國，不在本朝，吾不及見也。

translations.literal: "Only my younger brother should grow richer still — in another state, not this court; I shall not live to see it."
translations.idiomatic: Only my brother will grow richer still — in another realm, not this one; I shall not see it."

sentences.zh: 」其精如此。

translations.literal: " Such was his precision.
translations.idiomatic: So keen was his art.

sentences.zh: 冏性廉謹，恭儉自修，所得俸秩，必分親故。

translations.literal: Jiong was frugal and careful, cultivated modesty, and always shared salary with kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was frugal and careful, cultivated humility, and divided every stipend among kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 終鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: He ended as Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 臨終，誡其二子曰：「夫恭儉福之輿，傲侈禍之機。

translations.literal: On his deathbed he admonished his two sons: "Modesty and thrift are the carriage of blessing; pride and extravagance the engine of disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Dying, he told his sons, "Modesty and thrift are the carriage of blessing; pride and waste the engine of ruin."

sentences.zh: 乘福輿者浸以康休，蹈禍機者忽而傾覆，汝其誡歟！

translations.literal: "Those who ride the carriage of blessing grow ever healthier; those who tread the engine of disaster topple in a moment — take heed!"
translations.idiomatic: Those who ride blessing grow ever sound; those who tread ruin topple in a breath — heed me!"

sentences.zh: 吾沒後，斂以時服，祭無牢餼，棺足周屍，瘞不洩露而已。

translations.literal: "After I am gone, bury me in seasonable dress; offer no sacrificial beasts; let the coffin only enclose the corpse and the grave not leak — that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Bury me in proper season's dress; no sacrificial beasts; a coffin that only wraps the corpse; a grave that does not gape — no more."

sentences.zh: 」及卒，長子修遵父命。

translations.literal: " When he died, the eldest son Xiu followed his command.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, eldest son Xiu obeyed.

sentences.zh: 景哲弟景鳳，字鸞叔，位尚藥典禦。

translations.literal: Jingzhe's younger brother Jingfeng, styled Luanshu, was Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhe's brother Jingfeng, styled Luanshu, was Director of the Imperial Pharmacy.

sentences.zh: 休字惠盛。

translations.literal: Xiu, styled Huisheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu, styled Huisheng.

sentences.zh: 曾祖諲，仕宋位青、冀二州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shen served Song as Inspector of Qing and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Shen served Song as Inspector of Qing and Ji.

sentences.zh: 祖靈和，宋員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Linghe was Song Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Linghe was Song Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 父宗伯，始還魏，追贈清河太守。

translations.literal: His father Zongbo first returned to Wei and was posthumously made Administrator of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Father Zongbo first came home to Wei and was posthumously made Administrator of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 休少孤貧，矯然自立。

translations.literal: Xiu in youth was orphaned and poor yet stood upright by sheer will.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor in youth, Xiu stood upright by will alone.

sentences.zh: 舉秀才，入京師，與宋弁、邢巒雅相知友。

translations.literal: Recommended as a cultivated talent, he entered the capital and became close friends with Song Bian and Xing Luan.
translations.idiomatic: As a cultivated talent he entered the capital and grew intimate with Song Bian and Xing Luan.

sentences.zh: 尚書王嶷欽其人望，為長子娉休姊，贍以財貨，由是少振。

translations.literal: Minister Wang Yi admired his reputation, married his eldest son to Xiu's sister, and supported him with goods — thus he briefly revived.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi of the Secretariat admired him, married his heir to Xiu's sister, and supplied goods so his fortunes briefly rose.

sentences.zh: 孝文納休妹為嬪。

translations.literal: Xiaowen took Xiu's sister as a consort.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowen took Xiu's sister into the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 頻遷兼給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Regular Attendant at the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose repeatedly to Acting Regular Attendant at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 休勤學，公事軍旅之隙，手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Xiu studied hard; in the gaps of public business and campaigns his hand never left the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: He studied relentlessly; between office and campaign his hand never left a scroll.

sentences.zh: 禮遇亞于宋弁、郭祚。

translations.literal: His honors stood just below Song Bian and Guo Zuo.
translations.idiomatic: Court favor ranked him just below Bian and Zuo.

sentences.zh: 孝文南伐，以北海王詳為尚書僕射，統留台事，以休為尚書左丞。

translations.literal: On Xiaowen's southern campaign, Prince of Beihai Xiang was made Vice Director of the Secretariat to command the rear capital; Xiu was made Left Assistant Director.
translations.idiomatic: On Xiaowen's southern expedition, Prince Xiang of Beihai commanded the rear capital; Xiu became Left Assistant Director.

sentences.zh: 詔以北海年少，百揆務殷，便以委休。

translations.literal: An edict said Beihai was young and the hundred offices' business heavy — authority was therefore entrusted to Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: An edict said the prince was young and business crushing — power was lodged with Xiu.

sentences.zh: 轉長史，兼給事黃門侍郎，參定禮儀。

translations.literal: He was made Chief Clerk, also Acting Regular Attendant, and helped fix ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He became Chief Clerk and Acting Regular Attendant and helped settle ritual.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗閱故府，得舊冠，題曰：「南部尚書崔逞制」。

translations.literal: The Emperor once examined the old storehouse, found an ancient cap, and read the inscription: "Made by Southern Minister Cui Cheng."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor once searched the old treasury, found an ancient cap inscribed, "Made by Southern Minister Cui Cheng."

sentences.zh: 顧謂休曰：「此卿家舊事也。

translations.literal: He turned to Xiu and said: "This is an old story of your house."
translations.idiomatic: He turned to Xiu: "That is your family's antiquity."

sentences.zh: 」後從駕南行。

translations.literal: " Later he followed the imperial progress south.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 及還，幸彭城，泛舟泗水，詔在侍筵，觀者榮之。

translations.literal: On the return the court visited Pengcheng and drifted on the Si; an edict placed him at the feast — onlookers counted it glory.
translations.idiomatic: On the return the court visited Pengcheng and boated the Si; Xiu was ordered to the banquet — the crowd envied him.

sentences.zh: 宣武初，休以祖父未葬，弟夤又亡，固求出為勃海太守。

translations.literal: At the start of Xuanwu's reign Xiu, because grandfather and father were still unburied and his younger brother Yin had died, firmly begged to go out as Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Xuanwu's reign, with forebears unburied and brother Yin dead, Xiu begged leave to govern Bohai.

sentences.zh: 性嚴明，雅長政體。

translations.literal: His nature was stern and bright; he excelled in the substance of government.
translations.idiomatic: Stern and clear by nature, he excelled at the substance of rule.

sentences.zh: 下車先戮豪猾數人，奸盜莫不禽翦。

translations.literal: On taking office he first executed several powerful ruffians; robbers and thieves were none not seized and cut down.
translations.idiomatic: Taking office he first killed several powerful bullies; thieves were hunted to the last.

sentences.zh: 清身率下，部內安之。

translations.literal: He kept himself pure and led those below; the commandery was settled.
translations.idiomatic: He kept himself pure and led subordinates; the district grew calm.

sentences.zh: 時大儒張吾貴名盛山東，弟子恆千餘人，所在多不見容。

translations.literal: The great scholar Zhang Wugui then had fame throughout the east; his disciples always numbered more than a thousand, and in many places he was not welcomed.
translations.idiomatic: The savant Zhang Wugui was famed across the east with a thousand pupils, yet often unwelcome where he went.

sentences.zh: 休招延禮接，使肄業而還，儒者稱為口實。

translations.literal: Xiu received and honored him, had him complete his studies and return — scholars made it a byword.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu welcomed him, let him finish study and return — scholars told the tale ever after.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部郎中，遷散騎常侍，權兼選任，多所拔擢。

translations.literal: He entered as Director in the Ministry of the Civil Service, was promoted Regular Attendant, and while holding concurrent selection authority advanced many men.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the Ministry of the Civil Service, rose to Regular Attendant, and while holding selection advanced many men.

sentences.zh: 廣平王懷數引談宴。

translations.literal: Prince of Guangping Huai often invited him to talk and feast.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Huai of Guangping often drew him to talk and feast.

sentences.zh: 以與諸王交遊，免官。

translations.literal: Because he associated with princes he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Friendship with princes cost him his post.

sentences.zh: 後為司徒右長史，公平清潔，甚得時譽。

translations.literal: Later he was Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of State — fair, clean, and much praised in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Right Chief Clerk of the Minister of State — fair, clean, widely praised.

sentences.zh: 曆幽、青二州刺史，皆以清白稱，二州懷其德澤。

translations.literal: He successively governed You and Qing, in both known for purity; the two provinces cherished his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He governed You and Qing in turn, both times famed for purity; both provinces cherished him.

sentences.zh: 入為度支、七兵、殿中三尚書。

translations.literal: He entered as Minister of Revenue, of the Seven Armies, and of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He entered as Minister of Revenue, of the Seven Armies, and of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 休久在台閣，明習典故，每朝廷疑議，咸取正焉。

translations.literal: Xiu long served in the terrace offices and knew precedents well; whenever the court doubted, his word settled it.
translations.idiomatic: Long in the terraces, he knew precedent; whenever the court wavered, his word settled it.

sentences.zh: 諸公咸謂崔尚書下意處不可異也。

translations.literal: The great lords all said that where Minister Cui inclined, one could not differ.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees said that where Minister Cui inclined, none might differ.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書右僕射，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Vice Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous name Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died, was posthumously Vice Director with the name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 休少而謙退，事母孝謹。

translations.literal: Xiu from youth was modest and served his mother with filial care.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was modest and served his mother with filial care.

sentences.zh: 及為尚書，子仲文娶丞相高陽王雍女，女適領軍元叉庶長子舒，挾恃二家，志氣微改，陵藉同列。

translations.literal: When he became Minister, his son Zhongwen married the daughter of Chancellor Prince of Gaoyang Yong; the daughter married Shu's eldest son by a concubine of the Commander-in-Chief Yuan Cha — leaning on both houses, his spirit shifted slightly and he trod upon colleagues.
translations.idiomatic: As Minister, son Zhongwen married Chancellor Prince Yong's daughter; that daughter wed Yuan Cha's commander's eldest by a concubine — leaning on both houses, Xiu's temper shifted and he trampled colleagues.

sentences.zh: 尚書令李崇、左僕射蕭寶夤、右僕射元欽皆以此憚下之。

translations.literal: Minister of State Li Chong, Left Vice Director Xiao Baoyin, and Right Vice Director Yuan Qin all therefore feared and yielded.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chong, Xiao Baoyin, and Yuan Qin all feared him and yielded.

sentences.zh: 始休母房氏欲以休女妻其外孫邢氏，休乃違母情，以妻叉子，議者非之。

translations.literal: At first Xiu's mother, Lady Fang, wished to marry Xiu's daughter to her grandson of the Xing clan; Xiu went against her wish and gave the girl to Cha's son — critics faulted him.
translations.idiomatic: Mother Lady Fang wished Xiu's daughter for a Xing grandson; Xiu defied her and gave her to Cha's son — critics faulted him.

sentences.zh: 子甗。

translations.literal: His son Lin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Lin.

sentences.zh: 甗字長儒，狀貌偉麗，善於容止。

translations.literal: Lin, styled Changru, had a grand form and fine bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, styled Changru, had a grand form and fine bearing.

sentences.zh: 少知名。

translations.literal: From youth he was known.
translations.idiomatic: He was known from youth.

sentences.zh: 為魏宣武挽郎。

translations.literal: He was a mourning officer for Emperor Xuanwu of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: He served as mourning officer for Wei Emperor Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 釋褐太學博士，累遷散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: On first office he was Erudite of the Imperial University and rose to Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: First office was Erudite of the Imperial University; he rose to Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 坐事免歸鄉里。

translations.literal: Because of an affair he was dismissed and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: An affair dismissed him home.

sentences.zh: 冀部豪傑之起，爭召甗兄弟，甗中立無所就。

translations.literal: When heroes of Ji rose, all contended to summon the Lin brothers; Lin stood neutral and joined none.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji heroes rose, all summoned the Lin brothers; Lin stood neutral.

sentences.zh: 高敖曹以三百騎劫取之，以為師友。

translations.literal: Gao Aocao with three hundred horsemen seized him and made him a friend and teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Aocao seized him with three hundred horse and made him friend and teacher.

sentences.zh: 齊神武至信都，以為開府諮議參軍，曆給事黃門侍郎、衛將軍。

translations.literal: When Qi Shenwu reached Xindu he made him Counselor of the Opening Office and successively Regular Attendant and Defender-General.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu reached Xindu he made Lin Opening Office Counselor, then Regular Attendant and Defender-General.

sentences.zh: 神武入洛，議定廢立。

translations.literal: When Shenwu entered Luoyang they debated deposing and enthroning.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenwu entered Luoyang they debated whom to enthrone.

sentences.zh: 太僕綦俊盛言節閔帝賢明，可主社稷。

translations.literal: Grand Master of the Stud Qi Jun loudly praised Emperor Jiemin as worthy and fit to rule the altars.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Master of the Stud Qi Jun praised Jiemin as worthy to rule the realm.

sentences.zh: 甗作色而前曰：「若其賢明，自可待我高王。

translations.literal: Lin flushed and stepped forward: "If he were worthy, he could wait on our High King."
translations.idiomatic: Lin flushed and stepped forward: "If worthy, let him wait on our High King."

sentences.zh: 既為逆胡所立，何得猶作天子？

translations.literal: " Once set up by rebellious barbarians, how may he still be Son of Heaven?"
translations.idiomatic: Once raised by rebel barbarians, how is he still Son of Heaven?"

sentences.zh: 若從俊言，王師何名義舉？

translations.literal: " If we follow Jun's words, under what righteous name does the King's army march?"
translations.idiomatic: Follow Jun and what righteous name has the King's army?"

sentences.zh: 由是節閔及中興主皆廢。

translations.literal: Thus Jiemin and the Zhongxing ruler were both deposed.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Jiemin and the Zhongxing ruler were both deposed.

sentences.zh: 更立平陽王，是為孝武。

translations.literal: They enthroned the Prince of Pingyang — this is Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: They enthroned Prince of Pingyang — Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 以建義功，封武城縣公。

translations.literal: For merit in raising the righteous banner he was enfeoffed Duke of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: For raising the righteous banner he was made Duke of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 甗恃預義旗，頗自矜縱。

translations.literal: Lin, relying on his place in the righteous army, was rather proud and unrestrained.
translations.idiomatic: Counting on the righteous banner, Lin grew proud and loose.

sentences.zh: 尋以貪污為御史糾劾，逃還鄉里。

translations.literal: Soon he was impeached by the censorate for corruption and fled home.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the censorate impeached him for graft and he fled home.

sentences.zh: 時清河多盜，齊文襄以石愷為太守，令得專殺。

translations.literal: Qinghe then had many bandits; Qi Wenxiang made Shi Kai administrator with power to kill at will.
translations.idiomatic: Qinghe swarmed with bandits; Wenxiang made Shi Kai administrator with power to kill at will.

sentences.zh: 愷經甗宅，謂少年曰：「諸郎輩莫作賊，太守打殺人！

translations.literal: Passing Lin's house, Kai told the youths: "Young sirs, do not be bandits — the Administrator kills people!"
translations.idiomatic: Passing Lin's gate Kai told the youths, "Do not be thieves — the Administrator kills!"

sentences.zh: 」甗顧曰：「何不答府君：下官家作賊，止捉一天子牽臂下殿，捉一天子推上殿。

translations.literal: " Lin looked back: "Why not answer the Lord: 'In our house we make bandits — we only seize one Son of Heaven by the arm and lead him down from the hall, seize another and push him up."
translations.idiomatic: Lin called back, "Tell the Lord: 'We make bandits — we only seize one Son of Heaven by the arm down the steps and push another up."

sentences.zh: 不作偷驢摸犢賊。

translations.literal: " We do not steal asses or grope calves."
translations.idiomatic: We do not steal donkeys or grope calves.'"

sentences.zh: 」及遇赦出，復為黃門。

translations.literal: When amnesty came he was released and again became Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Amnesty freed him; he returned to the Yellow Gate.

sentences.zh: 天平中，授徐州刺史，給廣宗部曲三百，清河部曲千。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was made Inspector of Xuzhou, given three hundred households of Guangzong and a thousand of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping he was Inspector of Xuzhou with three hundred Guangzong households and a thousand of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 甗性暴慢。

translations.literal: Lin was violent and arrogant by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Lin was violent and arrogant.

sentences.zh: 寵妾馮氏，長且姣，家人號曰成母，朝士邢子才等多奸之。

translations.literal: His favored concubine Lady Feng was tall and beautiful; the household called her Mother Cheng; courtiers such as Xing Zicai often lay with her.
translations.idiomatic: Concubine Feng was tall and fair; servants called her Mother Cheng; Xing Zicai and others often slept with her.

sentences.zh: 至是假其威勢，恣情取受，風政不立。

translations.literal: Now he borrowed her power, took as he pleased, and government lost its edge.
translations.idiomatic: Now he borrowed her power, took what he wished, and rule grew slack.

sentences.zh: 初，甗為常侍，求人修起居注，或曰：「魏收可。

translations.literal: At first, as Regular Attendant, Lin sought someone to compile the imperial diary; some said: "Wei Shou will do."
translations.idiomatic: As Regular Attendant he sought a diarist; some said Wei Shou would serve.

sentences.zh: 」甗曰：「收輕薄徒耳。

translations.literal: " Lin said: "Shou is a frivolous fellow."
translations.idiomatic: Lin said, "Shou is a frivolous wretch."

sentences.zh: 」更引祖鴻勳為之。

translations.literal: " He brought in Zu Hongxun instead.
translations.idiomatic: He took Zu Hongxun instead.

sentences.zh: 又欲陷收不孝之罪，乃以盧元明代收為中書郎。

translations.literal: He also wished to trap Shou with the crime of unfilial conduct and therefore had Lu Yuanming replace Shou as Secretariat Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He tried to trap Shou with unfilial conduct and had Lu Yuanming replace him at the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 由是收銜之。

translations.literal: Hence Shou bore a grudge.
translations.idiomatic: Shou nursed a grudge.

sentences.zh: 及收聘梁，過徐州，甗備刺史鹵簿迎之，使人相聞收曰：「勿怪儀衛多，稽古力也。

translations.literal: When Shou went on embassy to Liang and passed Xuzhou, Lin prepared the inspector's full guard to meet him and sent word: "Do not wonder at the many guards — that is the scholar's antiquarian pride."
translations.idiomatic: When Shou went on embassy to Liang and passed Xuzhou, Lin met him with the inspector's full guard and said, "Do not wonder at the escort — a scholar's antiquarian pride."

sentences.zh: 」收語蹇，急報曰：「崔徐州建義之勳，何稽古之有？

translations.literal: " Shou stumbled in speech and shot back: "Inspector Cui's merit in raising the righteous banner — what antiquarianism is in that?"
translations.idiomatic: Shou stumbled and shot back, "What antiquarianism in Inspector Cui's righteous-banner merit?"

sentences.zh: 」甗自以門伐素高，特不平此言。

translations.literal: Lin, trusting his pedigree, was especially displeased at these words.
translations.idiomatic: Lin, trusting his pedigree, burned at the reply.

sentences.zh: 收乘宿憾，故以此挫之。

translations.literal: Shou, riding an old grievance, therefore used this to humiliate him.
translations.idiomatic: Shou, riding old spite, meant to humble him.

sentences.zh: 罷徐州，除秘書監，以母憂去官。

translations.literal: Dismissed from Xuzhou, he was made Supervisor of the Secretariat and left office for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Xuzhou he became Supervisor of the Secretariat, then left for mourning.

sentences.zh: 服終，兼太常卿，轉七兵尚書、清河邑中正。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was concurrently Minister of Ceremonies, then Minister of the Seven Armies and Rectifier of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning done, he was Minister of Ceremonies, then Minister of the Seven Armies and Rectifier of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 甗有文學，偉風貌，寡言辭，端嶷如神，以簡貴自處。

translations.literal: Lin had literature, a grand presence, few words, an upright awe like a spirit's — he held himself aloof and noble.
translations.idiomatic: Lin had letters, a grand presence, few words, upright awe like a god — he held himself rare.

sentences.zh: 齊神武言：「崔甗應作令僕，恨其精神太遒。

translations.literal: Qi Shenwu said: "Cui Lin should be Vice Director — pity his spirit is too fierce."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu said, "Lin should be Vice Director — pity his spirit is too fierce."

sentences.zh: 趙郡李渾將聘梁，名輩畢萃，詩酒正謹，甗後到，一坐無復談話。

translations.literal: Li Hun of Zhao was to go on embassy to Liang; the famous gathered, wine and verse in proper order — Lin arrived late and the whole bench fell silent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hun of Zhao was to embassy Liang; the famous gathered with wine and verse — Lin came late and the hall went mute.

sentences.zh: 鄭伯猷歎曰：「身長八尺，面如刻畫，謦欬為洪鐘饗，胸中貯千卷書，使人那得不畏服！」

translations.literal: Zheng Boyou sighed: "Eight feet tall, face carved as if chiseled, cough and breath like a great bell sounding, a thousand volumes stored in the breast — how could one not fear and submit!"
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Boyou sighed, "Eight feet, face chiseled, cough like a bell, a thousand volumes in the breast — who would not submit?"

sentences.zh: 甗以籍地自矜，常與蕭祗、明少遐等高宴終日，獨無言。

translations.literal: Lin, proud of his register, often feasted to the day's end with Xiao Zhi, Ming Shaoxia, and others — alone speechless.
translations.idiomatic: Proud of his register, Lin feasted all day with Xiao Zhi and Ming Shaoxia — and said nothing.

sentences.zh: 少遐晚謂甗曰：「驚風飄白日，忽然落西山。

translations.literal: Late, Shaoxia told Lin: "The startled wind blows the white sun; suddenly it falls beyond the western hills."
translations.idiomatic: Late, Shaoxia told Lin, "Startled wind blows the white sun; suddenly it falls beyond the western hills."

sentences.zh: 」甗亦無言，直曰「爾」。

translations.literal: " Lin also said nothing — only "You."
translations.idiomatic: Lin said nothing — only "You."

sentences.zh: 每謂盧元明曰：「天下盛門唯我與爾，博崔、趙李何事者哉！

translations.literal: He often told Lu Yuanming: "The great houses under Heaven are only you and I — what are Broad Cui and Zhao Li?"
translations.idiomatic: He told Lu Yuanming, "Under Heaven only you and I are great houses — what are Broad Cui and Zhao Li?"

sentences.zh: 」崔暹聞而銜之。

translations.literal: " Cui Xuan heard and bore resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan heard and resented it.

sentences.zh: 神武葬後，甗又竊言：「黃頷小兒堪當重任不？

translations.literal: After Shenwu's burial Lin again whispered: "Can that yellow-chinned boy bear heavy duty?"
translations.idiomatic: After Shenwu's burial Lin whispered, "Can that yellow-chinned boy bear great weight?"

sentences.zh: 」暹外兄李慎以告暹。

translations.literal: Xuan's cousin by marriage Li Shen told Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan's cousin Li Shen told Xuan.

sentences.zh: 暹啟文襄，絕甗朝謁。

translations.literal: Xuan reported to Wenxiang and cut off Lin's court attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan reported to Wenxiang and barred Lin from court.

sentences.zh: 甗要拜道左，文襄發怒曰：「黃頷兒何足拜也！

translations.literal: Lin wished to bow by the roadside; Wenxiang raged: "What is a yellow-chinned boy worth bowing to!"
translations.idiomatic: Lin tried to bow by the road; Wenxiang raged, "What is a yellow-chinned boy worth bowing to!"

sentences.zh: 」於是鎖甗赴晉陽，訊之，不服。

translations.literal: " He thereupon chained Lin and sent him to Jinyang for interrogation; Lin would not confess.
translations.idiomatic: He chained Lin to Jinyang; Lin would not confess.

sentences.zh: 暹引邢子才為證，子才執無此言。

translations.literal: Xuan called Xing Zicai as witness; Zicai held that there was no such speech.
translations.idiomatic: Xuan called Xing Zicai; Zicai swore there was no such speech.

sentences.zh: 甗在禁謂邢曰：「卿知我意屬太丘不？

translations.literal: Imprisoned, Lin told Xing: "Do you know my heart is set on Taqiu?"
translations.idiomatic: Imprisoned, Lin told Xing, "Do you know my heart is set on Taqiu?"

sentences.zh: 」邢出，告甗子贍曰：「尊公意，正應欲結姻陳元康。

translations.literal: " Xing left and told Lin's son Zhan: "Your father's intent is surely to ally by marriage with Chen Yuankang."
translations.idiomatic: Xing left and told son Zhan, "Your father's intent is marriage with Chen Yuankang."

sentences.zh: 」贍有新生女，乃許妻元康子。

translations.literal: " Zhan had a newborn daughter and promised her to Yuankang's son.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan had a newborn daughter and betrothed her to Yuankang's son.

sentences.zh: 元康為言于文襄曰：「崔甗名望素重，不可以私語殺之。

translations.literal: Yuankang spoke to Wenxiang: "Cui Lin's name and standing are always weighty — he cannot be killed for private words."
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang told Wenxiang, "Lin's name is weighty — kill him not for a private whisper."

sentences.zh: 」文襄曰：「若免其性命，當徙之遐裔。

translations.literal: Wenxiang said: "If his life is spared, he should be moved to the far border."
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang said, "Spare him and move him to the far marches."

sentences.zh: 」元康曰：「甗若在邊，或將外叛。

translations.literal: Yuankang said: "If Lin is on the frontier he may rebel outward."
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang said, "On the frontier Lin may rebel outward."

sentences.zh: 以英賢資寇敵，非所宜也。

translations.literal: " To supply a worthy foe to the enemy is not fitting."
translations.idiomatic: To arm the enemy with a worthy man is not fitting."

sentences.zh: 」文襄曰：「既有季珪之罪，還令輸作可乎？

translations.literal: Wenxiang said: "Since he has Jigui's crime, may he be sent to labor instead?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang said, "Since he has Jigui's crime, send him to labor?"

sentences.zh: 」元康曰：「元康常讀《崔琰傳》，追恨魏武不弘。

translations.literal: Yuankang said: "I have often read the biography of Cui Yan and regret that Wei Wu was not magnanimous."
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang said, "I have read Cui Yan's biography and regret Wei Wu's want of magnanimity."

sentences.zh: 甗若在作所而殞，後世豈道公不殺也？

translations.literal: " If Lin dies in the works, will later ages not say you killed him?"
translations.idiomatic: If Lin dies in the works, will later ages not say you killed him?"

sentences.zh: 」文襄曰：「然則奈何？

translations.literal: Wenxiang said: "Then what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang said, "Then what is to be done?"

sentences.zh: 」元康曰：「甗合死。

translations.literal: Yuankang said: "Lin deserves death — the court and countryside all know it."
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang said, "Lin deserves death — court and countryside know it."

sentences.zh: 朝野皆知。

translations.literal: The court and countryside all know it.
translations.idiomatic: All know it.

sentences.zh: 公誠能以寬濟猛，特輕其罰，則仁德彌著，天下歸心。

translations.literal: " If you can indeed use lenience to temper severity and especially lighten his punishment, benevolence will shine the more and the realm will turn its heart."
translations.idiomatic: If you temper severity with lenience and lighten his punishment, benevolence will blaze and hearts will turn."

sentences.zh: 」段孝先亦言甗勳舊，乃舍之。

translations.literal: Duan Xiaoxian also spoke of Lin's old merit — and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Xiaoxian spoke of old merit — and Lin was released.

sentences.zh: 甗進謁奉謝，文襄猶怒曰：「我雖無堪，忝當大任，被卿以為黃頷小兒。

translations.literal: Lin came to court to give thanks; Wenxiang was still angry: "Though I am unworthy, I shamefully bear great duty — you took me for a yellow-chinned boy."
translations.idiomatic: Lin came to give thanks; Wenxiang still raged, "Though unworthy I bear great duty — you called me a yellow-chinned boy."

sentences.zh: 金石可銷，此言難滅！」

translations.literal: " Metal and stone may wear away — this speech is hard to extinguish!"
translations.idiomatic: Metal and stone may wear away — this speech will not die!"

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，除侍中，監起居。

translations.literal: At the start of Qi Tianbao he was made Attendant and supervised the imperial diary.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi Tianbao's start he was Attendant and supervised the diary.

sentences.zh: 以禪代之際，參掌儀禮，別封新豐縣男，回授第九弟子約。

translations.literal: At the change of dynasties he took part in ritual; he was separately enfeoffed Baron of Xinfeng and transferred the title to his ninth younger brother Yue.
translations.idiomatic: At the dynastic change he shaped ritual, was made Baron of Xinfeng, and passed the title to ninth brother Yue.

sentences.zh: 甗一門婚嫁，皆衣冠美族；

translations.literal: All marriages in Lin's house were with noble, cap-and-gown clans;
translations.idiomatic: Every marriage in Lin's house joined noble cap-and-gown clans;

sentences.zh: 吉凶儀範，為當時所稱。

translations.literal: rites of fortune and misfortune were praised in the age.
translations.idiomatic: rites of joy and mourning were models of the age.

sentences.zh: 婁太后為博陵王納甗妹為妃，敕其使曰：「好作法用，勿使崔家笑人。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Lou had Prince of Boling take Lin's sister as consort and charged the envoy: "Make proper ritual — do not let the Cui house laugh at us."
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Lou had Prince of Boling wed Lin's sister and told the envoy, "Rite it properly — do not let the Cui house laugh."

sentences.zh: 」婚夕，文宣帝舉酒祝曰：「新婦宜男，孝順富貴。

translations.literal: On the wedding night Emperor Wenxuan raised his cup and prayed: "May the new bride bear sons, be filial and rich."
translations.idiomatic: On the wedding night Wenxuan raised his cup: "May the bride bear sons — filial and rich."

sentences.zh: 」甗跪對：「孝順乃自臣門，富貴恩由陛下。

translations.literal: " Lin knelt and answered: "Filial piety is of my house; wealth and honor are grace from Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Lin knelt: "Filial piety is our house's gift; wealth and honor are Your Majesty's grace."

sentences.zh: 」五年，為東兗州刺史，復攜馮氏之部。

translations.literal: " In the fifth year he was Inspector of Eastern Yan and again brought Lady Feng's household troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was Inspector of Eastern Yan and again brought Feng's household troops.

sentences.zh: 為馮氏厭蠱，頗失精爽，尋遇偏風。

translations.literal: Because of Lady Feng's sorcery he lost much clarity of mind; soon he suffered hemiplegia.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's sorcery cost him his wits; soon hemiplegia struck.

sentences.zh: 馮氏受納狼籍，為御史劾，與甗俱召，詔付廷尉。

translations.literal: Lady Feng's bribes lay in heaps; the censorate impeached her — she and Lin were both summoned and handed to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Feng's bribes heaped up; the censorate impeached — both were handed to the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 諸囚多奸焉，獄中致競。

translations.literal: Many prisoners lay with her; in the prison they vied for her favor.
translations.idiomatic: Many prisoners lay with her; in prison they fought for her.

sentences.zh: 尋別詔斬馮氏於都市，支解為九段。

translations.literal: Soon a separate edict beheaded Lady Feng in the market and cut her corpse into nine parts.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict beheaded Feng in the market and cut her into nine.

sentences.zh: 甗以疾卒獄中。

translations.literal: Lin died of illness in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Lin died of illness in prison.

sentences.zh: 甗曆覽群書，兼有辭藻。

translations.literal: Lin had read widely and also had literary ornament.
translations.idiomatic: Lin read widely and wrote with ornament.

sentences.zh: 自中興迄于孝武，詔誥表檄多甗所為。

translations.literal: From the Zhongxing era to Xiaowu, most edicts, mandates, memorials, and proclamations were Lin's work.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhongxing to Xiaowu most edicts and proclamations were Lin's.

sentences.zh: 然性侈，耽財色，于諸弟不能盡雍穆之美，世論以此譏之。

translations.literal: Yet he was extravagant, addicted to wealth and women, and among his brothers did not fully keep harmonious kinship — the age criticized him for it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was extravagant, greedy for wealth and women, and not fully kind among brothers — the age faulted him.

sentences.zh: 素與魏收不協，收後專典國史，甗恐被惡言，乃悅之曰：「昔有班固，今則魏子。

translations.literal: He had long been at odds with Wei Shou; when Shou later monopolized the national history, Lin feared slander and therefore pleased him: "In the past there was Ban Gu; today there is Master Wei."
translations.idiomatic: Long at odds with Wei Shou, when Shou took the national history Lin feared slander and flattered him: "Once Ban Gu — today Master Wei."

sentences.zh: 」收鼻笑之，憾不釋。

translations.literal: Shou snorted through his nose; the resentment did not lift.
translations.idiomatic: Shou snorted; the grudge did not lift.

sentences.zh: 甗子贍。

translations.literal: Lin's son Zhan.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's son was Zhan.

sentences.zh: 贍字彥通，潔白，善容止，神彩嶷然，言不妄發，才學風流為後來之秀。

translations.literal: Zhan, styled Yantong, was pure and white, fine in bearing, spirit and color lofty; he did not speak rashly — in talent and grace he was the finest of the younger generation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan, styled Yantong, was pure, fine in bearing, spirit lofty, speech careful — the finest of the younger generation.

sentences.zh: 初，潁川荀濟自江南入洛，贍學於濟，故得經史有師法。

translations.literal: At first Xun Ji of Yingchuan came from the south into Luoyang; Zhan studied under Ji and therefore had classics and histories with proper masters.
translations.idiomatic: At first Xun Ji of Yingchuan came from the south; Zhan studied under him and gained proper masters in the classics.

sentences.zh: 侍中李神俊雅有風譽，晚年無子，見贍，歎謂邢邵曰：「昨見崔甗兒，便為後生第一。

translations.literal: Attendant Li Shenjun had elegant repute; in his later years without a son, seeing Zhan, he sighed to Xing Shao: "Yesterday I saw Cui Lin's son — at once first among the rising generation."
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Li Shenjun, childless in old age, saw Zhan and sighed to Xing Shao, "Yesterday I saw Lin's son — first among the rising generation."

sentences.zh: 我遂無此物，見此使人傷懷！」

translations.literal: " I have no such thing; seeing this wounds the heart!"
translations.idiomatic: I have no such son — the sight wounds the heart!"

sentences.zh: 年十五，刺史高昂召署主簿，清河公高嶽避為開府西閣祭酒。

translations.literal: At fifteen Inspector Gao Ang summoned him as Chief Clerk; Prince of Qinghe Gao Yue declined him as Sacrificer of the Western Pavilion of the Opening Office.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen Inspector Gao Ang made him Chief Clerk; Prince Gao Yue of Qinghe declined him as Western Pavilion Sacrificer.

sentences.zh: 博陵崔暹為中尉，啟除侍御史。

translations.literal: Cui Xuan of Boling as Commandant of Justice memorialized him as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xuan of Boling as Commandant memorialized him Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 以父與暹隙，俄而去官。

translations.literal: Because his father and Xuan were at odds, he soon left office.
translations.idiomatic: Father and Xuan were at odds; he soon left office.

sentences.zh: 神武召與北海王晞俱為諸子賓友，仍為相府中兵參軍，轉主簿。

translations.literal: Shenwu summoned him with Prince of Beihai Xi as companions to the princes, then made him Middle Army Officer of the Chancellor's Office and Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu made him and Prince Xi companions to the princes, then Middle Army Officer and Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 文襄崩，秘未發喪，文宣命贍兼相府司馬，使鄴。

translations.literal: When Wenxiang died the death was kept secret; Wenxuan ordered Zhan Acting Chief Clerk of the Chancellor's Office and sent him to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxiang died with the news sealed; Wenxuan made Zhan Acting Chief Clerk and sent him to Ye.

sentences.zh: 魏孝靜帝以人日登雲龍門。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei on the Human Day ascended the Cloud Dragon Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Emperor Xiaojing on the Human Day climbed the Cloud Dragon Gate.

sentences.zh: 與其父甗俱侍宴為詩。

translations.literal: With his father Lin he attended the feast and composed verse.
translations.idiomatic: He and father Lin attended the feast and made verse.

sentences.zh: 詔問邢邵等曰：「令贍此詩何如其父？

translations.literal: An edict asked Xing Shao and others: "How does young Zhan's poem compare with his father's?"
translations.idiomatic: An edict asked Xing Shao and others how young Zhan's poem compared with his father's.

sentences.zh: 」咸曰：「甗博雅弘麗，贍氣調清新，並詩人之冠冕。

translations.literal: " All said: "Lin is broad, elegant, and grand; Zhan's tone is fresh — both are crowns among poets."
translations.idiomatic: All said, "Lin is broad and grand; Zhan's tone is fresh — both crown poets."

sentences.zh: 」宴罷，咸共嗟賞之，云：「今日之宴，並為崔贍父子。

translations.literal: " When the feast ended all sighed in praise, saying: "Today's banquet is wholly for father and son Zhan of Cui."
translations.idiomatic: When the feast ended all sighed, "Today's banquet is wholly for the Cui father and son."

sentences.zh: 」楊愔欲引贍為中書侍，時盧思道直中書省，愔問其文藻優劣，思道曰：「崔贍文詞之美，實有可稱，但舉世重其風流，所以才華見沒。

translations.literal: " Yang Yin wished to bring Zhan into the Secretariat; Lu Sidao then served in the Secretariat — Yin asked the relative merit of their literary craft; Sidao said: "Cui Zhan's literary beauty truly deserves praise, but the age values his grace, and therefore his talent is buried."
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin wished Zhan for the Secretariat; Lu Sidao served there; Yin asked their merit; Sidao said, "Zhan's beauty deserves praise, but the age values his grace and buries his talent."

sentences.zh: 」愔云：「此言有理。

translations.literal: " Yin said: "This speech has reason."
translations.idiomatic: Yin said, "That has reason."

sentences.zh: 」其日奏用之。

translations.literal: " That day he memorialized for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: That day he was memorialized for appointment.

sentences.zh: 愔又曰：「昔裴瓚晉世為中書郎，神情高邁，每於禁門出入，宿衛者皆肅然動容。

translations.literal: Yin also said: "In Jin times Pei Zan was Secretariat Attendant — spirit lofty; each time he passed the forbidden gate the guards were solemnly moved."
translations.idiomatic: Yin also said, "In Jin Pei Zan was Secretariat Attendant — spirit lofty; passing the forbidden gate guards stirred."

sentences.zh: 崔生堂堂，亦當無愧裴子乎？」

translations.literal: " Cui Sheng is likewise grand — he should not shame Master Pei?"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Sheng is likewise grand — he should not shame Master Pei?"

sentences.zh: 皇建元年，除給事黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangjian he was made Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangjian's first year he was Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 與趙郡李概為莫逆之友。

translations.literal: With Li Gai of Zhao he was a sworn friend.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Gai of Zhao he was sworn friend.

sentences.zh: 概將東還，贍遺之書曰：「仗氣使酒，我之常弊，詆訶指切，在卿尤甚。

translations.literal: When Gai was to return east, Zhan sent him a letter: "Blowing off steam with wine is my constant fault; railing and cutting to the quick is especially yours."
translations.idiomatic: When Gai returned east Zhan wrote, "Wine and swagger are my fault; railing and cutting are especially yours."

sentences.zh: 足下告歸，吾于何聞過也？

translations.literal: " You go home — where shall I hear my faults?"
translations.idiomatic: You go home — where shall I hear my faults?"

sentences.zh: 」贍患氣，兼性遲重，雖居二省，竟不堪敷奏。

translations.literal: " Zhan suffered from qi blockage and was by nature slow and heavy; though he held posts in both secretariats, he could not bear to memorialize at court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan suffered blocked qi and was slow by nature; though in both secretariats he could not bear to memorialize.

sentences.zh: 孝昭踐阼，皇太子就傅受業，除太子中庶子，征赴晉陽。

translations.literal: When Xiaozhao took the throne the heir apparent took his tutor; Zhan was made Junior Mentor to the Heir Apparent and summoned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozhao reigned the heir took tutors; Zhan was Junior Mentor and summoned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 敕曰：「東宮弱年，未陶訓義。

translations.literal: The edict said: "The Eastern Palace is young and not yet steeped in teaching."
translations.idiomatic: The edict said, "The Eastern Palace is young and not steeped in teaching."

sentences.zh: 卿儀形風德，人之師表，故勞卿朝夕游處，開發幼蒙。

translations.literal: " Your bearing and wind are a man's model; therefore I trouble you to dwell day and night, opening the young mind."
translations.idiomatic: Your bearing is a man's model; dwell day and night and open the young mind."

sentences.zh: 一物三善，皆以相寄。

translations.literal: " One thing, three goods — all are entrusted to you."
translations.idiomatic: One thing, three goods — all entrusted to you."

sentences.zh: 」贍專在東宮，調護講讀及進退禮度，皆歸委焉。

translations.literal: " Zhan devoted himself to the Eastern Palace; nurture, lecturing, and the etiquette of coming and going were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan devoted himself to the Eastern Palace — nurture, lecture, and ritual of coming and going.

sentences.zh: 太子納妃斛律氏，敕贍與鴻臚崔勵撰訂婚禮儀注，主司以為後式。

translations.literal: When the heir took Lady Hulu as consort, an edict ordered Zhan and Grand Herald Cui Li to draft the marriage rites and notes — the supervising offices took them as later models.
translations.idiomatic: When the heir wed Lady Hulu, Zhan and Grand Herald Cui Li drafted marriage rites — offices took them as models.

sentences.zh: 時詔議三恪之禮，太子少傅魏收為一議，朝士莫不雷同。

translations.literal: At the time an edict debated the rites of the Three Revered; the Heir Apparent's Junior Tutor Wei Shou made one opinion — courtiers none failed to echo it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict debated the Three Revered; Junior Tutor Wei Shou made one opinion — courtiers echoed.

sentences.zh: 贍別立異議，收讀訖笑而不言。

translations.literal: Zhan set out a separate opinion; when Shou finished reading he laughed and said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan set a separate opinion; Shou read, laughed, and was silent.

sentences.zh: 贍正色曰：「聖上詔群臣議國家大典，少傅名位不輕，贍議若是，須贊其所長；

translations.literal: Zhan said with stern face: "The Sage has charged the ministers to debate the great canon of state; the Junior Tutor's name and standing are not light — if Zhan's opinion stands, praise what is strong;
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said sternly, "The Sage charged us to debate the state canon; the Junior Tutor is not light — if my opinion stands, praise what is strong;

sentences.zh: 若非，須詰其不允。

translations.literal: if not, probe what is wanting."
translations.idiomatic: if not, probe what fails."

sentences.zh: 何容讀國士議文，直此冷笑？

translations.literal: How may one read a fellow countryman's proposed text and only laugh coldly?"
translations.idiomatic: How may one read a countryman's text and only laugh coldly?"

sentences.zh: 崔贍居聖朝顯職，尚不免見疵，草萊諸生，欲云何自進！

translations.literal: " Cui Zhan holds a lofty post in the holy court and still is not free of fault — how may plain scholars hope to advance!"
translations.idiomatic: Cui Zhan in a lofty post still is faulted — how may plain scholars advance!"

sentences.zh: 」贍容貌方嚴，詞旨雄辯；

translations.literal: " Zhan's countenance was square and stern, his words heroic in debate;
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's countenance was square and stern, his words heroic;

sentences.zh: 收慚遽，竟無一言。

translations.literal: Shou flushed and hastened away — in the end not a word.
translations.idiomatic: Shou flushed and fled — not a word.

sentences.zh: 贍性簡傲，以才地自矜，所與周旋，皆一時名望。

translations.literal: Zhan was simple and proud, proud of talent and standing; those he associated with were all famous in the age.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was simple and proud of talent; his circle were all names of the age.

sentences.zh: 在御史臺，恆宅中送食，備盡珍羞；

translations.literal: At the Censorate he always had food sent from home, with every delicacy;
translations.idiomatic: At the Censorate food came from home with every delicacy;

sentences.zh: 別室獨餐，處之自若。

translations.literal: in a separate room he ate alone — at ease as if it were natural.
translations.idiomatic: in a separate room he ate alone — easy as nature.

sentences.zh: 有一河東人士姓裴，亦為御史，伺贍食，便往造焉。

translations.literal: A man of Hedong surnamed Pei was also a censor; watching Zhan eat, he went to visit.
translations.idiomatic: A Hedong man surnamed Pei was also censor; watching Zhan eat, he visited.

sentences.zh: 贍不與交言，又不命匕箸。

translations.literal: Zhan did not speak with him and did not offer spoon or chopsticks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan did not speak and offered no spoon or chopsticks.

sentences.zh: 裴坐觀贍食罷而退。

translations.literal: Pei sat watching until Zhan finished eating and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Pei sat watching until Zhan finished and left.

sentences.zh: 明日，自攜匕箸，恣情飲啖。

translations.literal: The next day he brought his own spoon and chopsticks and ate freely.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he brought his own utensils and ate freely.

sentences.zh: 贍謂曰：「我初不喚君食，亦不共君語，遂能不拘小節。

translations.literal: Zhan said: "At first I did not call you to eat, nor speak with you — yet you were not bound by small niceties."
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said, "I did not call you to eat nor speak — yet you were not bound by small niceties."

sentences.zh: 昔劉毅在京口冒請鵝炙，豈亦異是？

translations.literal: " In the past Liu Yi at Jingkou boldly asked for goose roasted — is this not the same?"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yi at Jingkou boldly asked for roast goose — is this not the same?"

sentences.zh: 君定名士。

translations.literal: You are surely a famed gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: You are surely a famed gentleman."

sentences.zh: 」於是每與之同食。

translations.literal: " Thereafter he always ate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter they always ate together.

sentences.zh: 性方重，好讀書，酒後清言，聞者莫不傾耳。

translations.literal: By nature he was square and weighty, loved reading; after wine his pure talk — none who heard but bent the ear.
translations.idiomatic: Square and weighty, he loved books; after wine his pure talk bent every ear.

sentences.zh: 自天保以後，重吏事，謂容止醖籍者為潦倒，而贍終不改焉。

translations.literal: From Tianbao onward clerical work was prized; those with cultivated bearing were called fallen — Zhan never changed.
translations.idiomatic: From Tianbao clerical work was prized; cultivated bearing was called fallen — Zhan never changed.

sentences.zh: 常見選曹以劉逖為縣令，謂之曰：「官長正應子琮輩，乃復屈名人！

translations.literal: He once saw the Selection Office make Liu Di a magistrate and said to them: "A district head should be Zicong's sort — yet you bend a famed man!"
translations.idiomatic: He saw Selection make Liu Di magistrate and said, "A magistrate should be Zicong's sort — yet you bend a famed man!"

sentences.zh: 」馮子琮聞之大怒。

translations.literal: " Feng Zicong heard and was greatly angry.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Zicong heard and raged.

sentences.zh: 及其用事，幾敗焉。

translations.literal: When he came to power, Zhan nearly came to ruin.
translations.idiomatic: When Zicong took power Zhan nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 有集二十卷。

translations.literal: He had a collection in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a collection in twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 甗弟仲文，有文學。

translations.literal: Lin's younger brother Zhongwen had literature.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's brother Zhongwen had letters.

sentences.zh: 太和中，為丞相掾。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era he was an aide to the Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe he was Chancellor's aide.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之敗，仲文持馬尾度河，波中乍沒乍出。

translations.literal: At the defeat at Shaye, Zhongwen gripped a horse's tail to cross the river — in the waves now submerged, now surfaced.
translations.idiomatic: At Shaye's defeat Zhongwen gripped a horse's tail to cross — now under the wave, now above.

sentences.zh: 神武望見，曰：「崔掾也。

translations.literal: Shenwu saw from afar and said: "Aide Cui."
translations.idiomatic: Shenwu saw afar and said, "Aide Cui."

sentences.zh: 」遽遣船赴接。

translations.literal: " He hastily sent a boat to fetch him.
translations.idiomatic: He sent a boat at once.

sentences.zh: 及至，謂曰：「卿為君為親，不顧萬死，可謂家之孝子，國之忠臣也。

translations.literal: When he arrived he said: "You for lord and kin did not spare ten thousand deaths — you may be called the house's filial son and the state's loyal minister."
translations.idiomatic: Arrived, he said, "For lord and kin you did not spare ten thousand deaths — filial son of the house, loyal minister of the state."

sentences.zh: 」後文襄欲使行青州，聞其多醉，乃止。

translations.literal: Later Wenxiang wished to send him to Qingzhou; hearing he drank much, he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Later Wenxiang wished to send him to Qing — hearing he drank much, he stopped.

sentences.zh: 天保初，甗為侍中，仲文為銀青光祿大夫，同日受拜，時雲兩鳳連飛。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao, Lin was Attendant and Zhongwen Silver-Glory Grand Master for Splendid Happiness — the same day they received appointment; clouds showed two phoenixes flying linked.
translations.idiomatic: At Tianbao's start Lin was Attendant and Zhongwen Silver-Glory Grand Master — same day appointed; clouds showed two linked phoenixes.

sentences.zh: 嘗被敕召，宿酲未解。

translations.literal: He was once summoned by edict with overnight wine not yet cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Once summoned by edict with overnight wine uncleared.

sentences.zh: 文宣怒，將罰之。

translations.literal: Wenxuan was angry and was about to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan raged and was about to punish him.

sentences.zh: 試使為觀射詩十韻，操筆立成，乃原之。

translations.literal: He was tested with a ten-rhyme poem on viewing the archery contest — brush in hand, it was finished at once — and he was forgiven.
translations.idiomatic: He was tested with ten rhymes on the archery contest — brush in hand, done at once — and forgiven.

sentences.zh: 拜散騎常侍、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子偃，太子洗馬、尚書郎。

translations.literal: His son Yan was Groom of the Heir Apparent and Secretariat Officer.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yan was Groom of the Heir Apparent and Secretariat Officer.

sentences.zh: 偃弟儦。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Biao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's brother was Biao.

sentences.zh: 儦字岐叔。

translations.literal: Biao, styled Qishu.
translations.idiomatic: Biao, styled Qishu.

sentences.zh: 少與范陽盧思道、隴西辛德源同志友善。

translations.literal: In youth with Lu Sidao of Fanyang and Xin Deyuan of Longxi he shared purpose and friendship.
translations.idiomatic: In youth with Lu Sidao of Fanyang and Xin Deyuan of Longxi he was sworn friend.

sentences.zh: 每以讀書為務，負恃才地，大署其戶曰：「不讀五千卷者，無得入此室」初舉秀才，為員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: He always made reading his task, trusting talent and standing, and wrote large on his door: "Whoever has not read five thousand juan may not enter this room." On first recommendation as cultivated talent he was Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He made reading his task, trusted talent and rank, and wrote large on his door, "Who has not read five thousand juan may not enter." First recommended as cultivated talent he was Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 與熊安生、馬敬德等議五禮，兼修律令。

translations.literal: With Xiong Ansheng, Ma Jingde, and others he debated the Five Rites and also revised statutes.
translations.idiomatic: With Xiong Ansheng and Ma Jingde he debated the Five Rites and revised statutes.

sentences.zh: 尋兼散騎侍郎，使陳。

translations.literal: Soon he was also Regular Attendant and envoy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Soon also Regular Attendant and envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 還，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: On return he waited for edicts at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: On return he waited for edicts at the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 曆尚書郎。

translations.literal: He successively was Secretariat Officer.
translations.idiomatic: He was in turn Secretariat Officer.

sentences.zh: 與頓丘李若俱見稱重，時人語曰：「京師灼灼，崔儦、李若。

translations.literal: With Li Ruo of Dunqiu he was alike praised; men of the time said: "In the capital, blazing bright — Cui Biao and Li Ruo."
translations.idiomatic: With Li Ruo of Dunqiu he was alike praised; the age said, "In the capital blazing bright — Cui Biao and Li Ruo."

sentences.zh: 」若每謂其子曰：「盧思道、崔儦，杳然崖岸，吾所重也，汝其師之。

translations.literal: " Ruo often told his sons: "Lu Sidao and Cui Biao are cliffs far and sheer — they are whom I honor; take them as masters."
translations.idiomatic: Ruo told his sons, "Lu Sidao and Cui Biao are sheer cliffs — honor them; be their pupils."

sentences.zh: 」思道與儦嘗酒後相調，儦曰：「偃邈無聞。

translations.literal: " Sidao and Biao once bantered after wine; Biao said: "Yan is distant and unheard-of."
translations.idiomatic: Sidao and Biao bantered after wine; Biao said, "Yan is distant and unheard."

sentences.zh: 」思道譏儦云：「高曾官薄。

translations.literal: " Sidao mocked Biao: "High ancestors' offices were thin."
translations.idiomatic: Sidao mocked Biao, "High ancestors' offices were thin."

sentences.zh: 」齊亡，歸鄉。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he returned home.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he went home.

sentences.zh: 仕郡為功曹，補主簿。

translations.literal: He served the commandery as Merit Officer and was made Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: He served the commandery as Merit Officer and Chief Clerk.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇四年，征授給事郎，兼內史舍人。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Sui Kaihuang he was summoned as Gentleman of the Secretariat and concurrently Palace Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In Sui Kaihuang's fourth year he was summoned Gentleman of the Secretariat and Palace Drafter.

sentences.zh: 後兼通直散騎侍郎，聘陳。

translations.literal: Later he was also Direct Attendant and Regular Attendant and went on embassy to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Later also Direct Attendant and Regular Attendant on embassy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 還，授員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: On return he was made Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was Supernumerary Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 以聾，常得無事，一醉輒八日。

translations.literal: Being deaf, he usually had nothing required of him; once he took to drink he would stay drunk for eight days.
translations.idiomatic: Deaf as he was, he was left largely alone; a single bout of drinking could last eight days.

sentences.zh: 越國公楊素時方貴幸，重儦門地，為子玄縱娶其女為妻，娉禮甚厚。

translations.literal: The Duke of Yue, Yang Su, was then at the height of favor; he valued Biao's family standing and had his daughter marry Biao's son Xuanzong, with a bride-price very generous indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, Duke of Yue, then stood at the summit of imperial favor; he prized Biao's pedigree and married his daughter to Biao's son Xuanzong with lavish betrothal gifts.

sentences.zh: 親迎之始，公卿滿坐，素令騎迎之。

translations.literal: At the start of the wedding procession the hall was full of dukes and ministers; Su ordered them to ride out and meet the groom.
translations.idiomatic: When the groom was to be escorted home, the seats were packed with nobles; Su sent them out on horseback to receive him.

sentences.zh: 儦弊衣冠騎驢而至。

translations.literal: Biao came in worn cap and robes, riding a donkey.
translations.idiomatic: Biao arrived in shabby dress, on a donkey.

sentences.zh: 素推令上坐，儦禮甚倨，言又不遜，素忿然拂衣而起，竟罷坐。

translations.literal: Su pushed him to the seat of honor; Biao's courtesy was very arrogant and his words insolent; Su angrily brushed his robe and rose, and the feast was broken up.
translations.idiomatic: Su pressed him to the place of honor, but Biao was haughty in ritual and rude in speech; Su flung his sleeve and left, and the banquet ended in ruin.

sentences.zh: 後數日，儦方來謝，素待之如初。

translations.literal: Several days later Biao came to apologize; Su treated him as before.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Biao came to make amends; Su received him as though nothing had happened.

sentences.zh: 詔授易州刺史，或言其未合，乃追停。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Governor of Yizhou; someone said he was unfit, and the appointment was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to be Governor of Yizhou, but when some said he was not suited to the post the appointment was halted.

sentences.zh: 鹿語人曰：「易州刺史何必勝道義。

translations.literal: Biao told people, "Why must the Governor of Yizhou surpass Dao Yi?"
translations.idiomatic: Biao said to others, "Why should a Governor of Yizhou have to outshine Dao Yi?"

sentences.zh: 」仁壽中，卒于京師。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he died in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the capital during Renshou.

sentences.zh: 子世濟。

translations.literal: His son Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Shiji.

sentences.zh: 仲文弟叔仁，輕俠重衿期。

translations.literal: Zhongwen's younger brother Shuren was light and chivalrous and set great store by pledged friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwen's younger brother Shuren was a swaggering knight who honored sworn bonds.

sentences.zh: 仕魏為潁州刺史。

translations.literal: He served Wei as Governor of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei he became Governor of Ying.

sentences.zh: 以貪污，為御史中丞高仲密劾，賜死於宅。

translations.literal: For corruption he was impeached by Censor-in-chief Gao Zhongmi and ordered to die at home.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhongmi, Censor-in-chief, impeached him for graft and he was granted death in his own house.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，賦詩五絕，與諸弟訣別。

translations.literal: Facing execution he composed five quatrains to take leave of his brothers.
translations.idiomatic: At the block he wrote five quatrains bidding his brothers farewell.

sentences.zh: 不及其兄甗，以其不甚營救也。

translations.literal: He did not reach his brother Yan—because Yan had not exerted himself much to save him.
translations.idiomatic: He never saw his brother Yan again—Yan, he felt, had not tried hard enough to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 子彥武，有識用。

translations.literal: His son Yanwu had judgment and ability.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yanwu was a man of insight and capacity.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，位魏州刺史。

translations.literal: At the opening of Sui's Kaihuang he held the post of Governor of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: In the first years of Sui's Kaihuang he was Governor of Wei.

sentences.zh: 叔仁弟叔義，魏孝莊時為尚書庫部郎。

translations.literal: Shuren's younger brother Shuyi, in Emperor Xiaozhuang's time, was Director of the Storehouse in the Ministry.
translations.idiomatic: Shuren's younger brother Shuyi, under Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei, was Director of the Storehouse in the Ministry.

sentences.zh: 初，叔義父休為青州刺史，放盜魁，令出其黨，遂以為門客。

translations.literal: At first Shuyi's father Xiu, as Governor of Qing, had released a bandit chieftain and ordered him to bring out his gang, and thus made them household retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Shuyi's father Xiu was Governor of Qing, he freed a bandit leader and had him deliver his band—men Xiu then kept as retainers.

sentences.zh: 在洛陽，與兄叔仁鑄錢。

translations.literal: In Luoyang he and his elder brother Shuren cast coin.
translations.idiomatic: In Luoyang he and his elder brother Shuren counterfeited coin.

sentences.zh: 事發，闔家逃逸，叔義見執。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light the whole family fled; Shuyi was seized.
translations.idiomatic: When the crime was exposed the household fled together, but Shuyi was caught.

sentences.zh: 時城陽王徽為司州牧，臨淮王彧以非其身罪，驟為致言。

translations.literal: The Prince of Chengyang, Hui, was Governor of Si; the Prince of Huaihuai, Yu, because the guilt was not Shuyi's own person, urgently spoke on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Chengyang Hui held Si Province; Prince of Huaihuai Yu, holding that the fault was not Shuyi's alone, pleaded for him at once.

sentences.zh: 徽以求婚不得，遂停赦書而殺之。

translations.literal: Hui, because a marriage proposal had been refused, then withheld the pardon and had him executed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, whose offer of marriage had been spurned, held back the amnesty and put him to death.

sentences.zh: 叔義弟子侃，以寄名從軍竊級為中書郎。

translations.literal: Shuyi's nephew's son Kan, by a false name, followed the army and stole rank as an officer of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shuyi's nephew's son Kan enlisted under a borrowed name and by fraud won a post in the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 為尚書左丞和子嶽彈糾，失官。

translations.literal: He was impeached by Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing He Ziyue and lost his office.
translations.idiomatic: He Ziyue, Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing, impeached him and he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 性兼使氣。

translations.literal: By nature he was also given to bravado.
translations.idiomatic: He was swaggering by temperament as well.

sentences.zh: 從自修改，閉門讀書，當時稱為博洽。

translations.literal: From then on he reformed himself, shut his door and read books, and at the time was called broadly learned.
translations.idiomatic: He afterward mended his ways, closed his doors to study, and men of the day called him encyclopedic.

sentences.zh: 後兼通直散騎常侍，使梁，為陽斐副。

translations.literal: Later he was also Token Attendant Cavalier and envoy to Liang, serving as Yang Fei's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Token Attendant Cavalier on a mission to Liang, as deputy to Yang Fei.

sentences.zh: 恥居斐下，自負才地，呼斐為陽子，語輒折之。

translations.literal: Ashamed to rank below Fei and arrogant of his talent and standing, he called Fei "Master Yang," and his words always cut him down.
translations.idiomatic: Loath to stand beneath Fei and proud of his own gifts and pedigree, he called Fei "Master Yang" and needled him at every turn.
