sentences.zh: 還，卒于路。

translations.literal: On his return he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the homeward journey.

sentences.zh: 子拯，位太子僕、武德郡守。

translations.literal: His son Zheng held the posts of Palace Steward and Governor of Wude commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zheng was Palace Steward and Governor of Wude.

sentences.zh: 子侃弟子植，位冀州別駕。

translations.literal: Kan's brother's son Zhi was Aide of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Kan's brother's son Zhi was Aide of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 走馬從禽，發掛木而死。

translations.literal: Galloping in the chase, his hair caught in a tree and he died.
translations.idiomatic: Riding hard after game, his hair caught in a branch and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 子珪。

translations.literal: His son Gui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Gui.

sentences.zh: 子植弟子聿，位東莞太守。

translations.literal: Zhi's brother's son Yu was Governor of Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's brother's son Yu was Governor of Dongguan.

sentences.zh: 子聿弟子約。

translations.literal: Yu's brother's son Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Yu's brother's son was Yue.

sentences.zh: 五歲喪父，不肯食肉。

translations.literal: At five he lost his father and would not eat meat.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at five and refused meat thereafter.

sentences.zh: 後喪母，居喪哀毀骨立。

translations.literal: Later, when his mother died, his mourning wore him to the bone.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died later, grief left him skin on bone.

sentences.zh: 人云：「崔九作孝，風吹即倒。

translations.literal: People said, "Cui Nine plays at filial piety—wind blows and he topples."
translations.idiomatic: People said, "Cui Nine performs filial piety: a gust of wind and he falls over."

sentences.zh: 」禫月，兄子度死，又百日不入房。

translations.literal: After the month of mourning ended, his elder brother's son Du died, and for another hundred days he did not enter his chamber.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning month ended his elder brother's son Du died, and for another hundred days he would not go indoors.

sentences.zh: 長八尺餘，姿神俊異，潛觀梁使劉孝儀，賓從見者駭目。

translations.literal: Over eight feet tall, with a bearing handsome and strange; he once watched the Liang envoy Liu Xiaoyi in secret, and those among the guests who saw him were startled.
translations.idiomatic: He stood more than eight feet, his presence striking and otherworldly; he once stole a look at the Liang envoy Liu Xiaoyi, and even the retinue who noticed were shaken.

sentences.zh: 武定中，為平原公開府祭酒。

translations.literal: In the Wuding era he was Sacrifice Wine on the staff of the Prince of Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wuding he was Sacrifice Wine on the Prince of Pingyuan's staff.

sentences.zh: 與兄子贍俱詣晉陽，寄居佛寺。

translations.literal: He and his elder brother's son Zhan both went to Jinyang and lodged in a Buddhist monastery.
translations.idiomatic: He and his elder brother's son Zhan went together to Jinyang and stayed in a temple.

sentences.zh: 贍長於子約二歲，每退朝久立，子約馮幾對之，儀望俱華，儼然相映。

translations.literal: Zhan was two years older than Yue; after court each would stand long while the other leaned on an armrest facing him—both splendid in bearing, like paired reflections.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan was two years Yue's senior; after audience they would stand facing each other, one leaning on a couch—both radiant, like mirrors of one another.

sentences.zh: 諸沙門竊窺之，以為二天人也。

translations.literal: The monks peeked at them and thought them two beings from heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Monks who spied on them whispered that two immortals had descended.

sentences.zh: 乾明中，為考功郎。

translations.literal: In the Qianming era he was Director of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianming he was Director of Merit.

sentences.zh: 病且卒，謂贍曰：「自諸兄歿，而門業頹替，居家大唯吾與爾。

translations.literal: Sick and near death, he told Zhan, "Since the brothers died the house line has declined; at home there are only you and me."
translations.idiomatic: Ill and dying, he said to Zhan, "Since our kinsmen died the line has crumbled; in this house only you and I remain."

sentences.zh: 命之修短，曾何足悲。

translations.literal: "Whether life is long or short—how is that worth grief?"
translations.idiomatic: "Life's span—what is there to mourn?"

sentences.zh: 汝能免之，吾不餒矣。」

translations.literal: "If you can escape this fate, I shall not die hungry."
translations.idiomatic: "If you can survive what comes, I will not starve in the grave."

sentences.zh: 休弟夤，字敬禮，位太子舍人。

translations.literal: Xiu's younger brother Yin, courtesy name Jingli, was Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu's younger brother Yin, style Jingli, was Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈樂安太守。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Le'an.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Governor of Le'an.

sentences.zh: 妻，樂安王長女晉甯公主也，貞烈有德行。

translations.literal: His wife was Princess Jinning, eldest daughter of the Prince of Le'an—chaste and of fine conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His wife was Princess Jinning, eldest daughter of the Prince of Le'an, famed for steadfast virtue.

sentences.zh: 子湣，字長謙，幼聰敏。

translations.literal: His son Min, courtesy name Changqian, was clever in boyhood.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min, style Changqian, was precocious as a child.

sentences.zh: 濟州刺史盧尚之欲以長女妻之，休子甗為長謙求尚之次女，曰：「家道多由婦人，欲令姊妹為妯娌。

translations.literal: The Governor of Jizhou, Lu Shangzhi, wished to give his eldest daughter to him; Yan sought Shangzhi's second daughter for Changqian, saying, "A household's way is ruled largely by its women; I wish the sisters to be sisters-in-law."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shangzhi, Governor of Jizhou, meant to marry his eldest daughter to him; Yan asked instead for Shangzhi's second daughter for Changqian, saying, "A house turns on its women—I want the girls to be sisters-in-law."

sentences.zh: 」尚之感其義，於是同日成婚。

translations.literal: Shangzhi was moved by the righteousness of it, and on the same day the weddings were held.
translations.idiomatic: Moved by the sentiment, Shangzhi married both daughters on the same day.

sentences.zh: 休誡諸子曰：「汝等宜皆一體，勿作同堂意。

translations.literal: Xiu warned his sons, "You should all be one body; do not act as though you were only cousins under one roof."
translations.idiomatic: Xiu admonished his sons, "Be one kin, not merely cousins sharing a hall."

sentences.zh: 若不用吾言，鬼神不享汝祭祀。

translations.literal: "If you do not heed my words, the spirits will not accept your sacrifices."
translations.idiomatic: "Ignore me, and the ancestors will refuse your offerings."

sentences.zh: 」休亡，枕中有書，如平生所誡，諸子奉焉。

translations.literal: When Xiu died, writings were found in his pillow like the admonitions he had given in life, and the sons obeyed them.
translations.idiomatic: After Xiu's death a text was found in his pillow, word for word his living counsel, and the sons followed it.

sentences.zh: 長謙與休第二子仲文同年而月長，其家謂之大二、小二。

translations.literal: Changqian and Xiu's second son Zhongwen were born in the same year, but Changqian was older by a month; the family called them Big Two and Little Two.
translations.idiomatic: Changqian and Zhongwen were born in the same year, Changqian a month ahead; the clan nicknamed them Big Two and Little Two.

sentences.zh: 長謙少與太原王延業俱為著作佐郎，監典校書。

translations.literal: In youth he and Wang Yanji of Taiyuan were both Editorial Assistants, supervising the collation of books.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he and Wang Yanji of Taiyuan served together as Editorial Assistants overseeing the collation of texts.

sentences.zh: 後為青州司馬。

translations.literal: Later he was Sima of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Sima of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 賊圍城二百日，長謙書不廢，凡咨手抄八千餘紙，天文、律曆、醫方、卜相、風角、鳥言，靡不開解。

translations.literal: When rebels besieged the city for two hundred days Changqian never laid down his brush; in all consultations he copied more than eight thousand sheets—astronomy, calendars, medicine, divination, wind horns, bird speech—there was nothing he did not master.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels held the city two hundred days; Changqian never stopped writing, copying eight thousand sheets by hand in counsel—astronomy, calendrics, medicine, omens, wind lore, bird calls, all of it open to him.

sentences.zh: 晚頗以酒為損。

translations.literal: In his later years he was somewhat harmed by wine.
translations.idiomatic: In later years wine took its toll.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒諮議，修起居注，加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was moved to Counsellor of the Masters of Writing, edited the Imperial Diary, and was given the added title Grand Master of Splendorous Light.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Counsellor of the Masters of Writing, kept the Imperial Diary, and was given the Splendorous Light grade.

sentences.zh: 後兼散騎常侍，使梁。

translations.literal: Later he was also Token Attendant Cavalier on a mission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Token Attendant Cavalier on an embassy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 將行，謂人曰：「我厄在吳國，忌在酉年，今恐不免。

translations.literal: Before leaving he told people, "My calamity lies in Wu lands; my taboo is the you year—I fear I shall not escape."
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out he said, "My doom is in Wu country; my unlucky year is you—I may not return."

sentences.zh: 」及還，未入境，卒。

translations.literal: On his return, before he had crossed the border, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died on the homeward road before he re-entered the realm.

sentences.zh: 年二十八。

translations.literal: He was twenty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was twenty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈南青州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Governor of Southern Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Governor of Southern Qing.

sentences.zh: 逞兄遹。

translations.literal: Cheng's elder brother Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's elder brother was Yuan.

sentences.zh: 遹字甯祖，亦有名于時。

translations.literal: Yuan, courtesy name Ningzu, was also famed in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, style Ningzu, was likewise celebrated in his day.

sentences.zh: 為慕容垂尚書左丞、范陽昌黎二郡太守。

translations.literal: He was Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing under Murong Chui and Governor of Fan Yang and Changli.
translations.idiomatic: Under Murong Chui he was Left Vice Minister of the Masters of Writing and Governor of Fan Yang and Changli.

sentences.zh: 遹曾孫延壽，冀州主簿。

translations.literal: Yuan's great-grandson Yanshou was chief clerk of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's great-grandson Yanshou was chief clerk of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 輕財好施，甚收鄉曲譽。

translations.literal: Light with wealth and fond of giving, he won great praise in his district.
translations.idiomatic: He spent freely and gave freely, and his neighborhood spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 延壽子隆宗，簡率友悌，居喪以孝聞。

translations.literal: Yanshou's son Longzong was plain and brotherly; his mourning was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou's son Longzong was open and devoted to his brothers; his filial mourning was widely praised.

sentences.zh: 位蘭陵、燕二郡太守。

translations.literal: He held the governorships of Lanling and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Lanling and Yan.

sentences.zh: 仁信待物，檢慎至誠，故見重于時。

translations.literal: He treated others with humaneness and trust, and was cautious to the point of sincerity; therefore he was valued in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Humane and trustworthy, scrupulous to sincerity itself, he was held in esteem.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈齊州刺史，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Governor of Qi, with the posthumous name Filial.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously Governor of Qi, posthumous name Filial.

sentences.zh: 子敬保，冀州儀同府從事中郎。

translations.literal: His son Jingbao was Attendant in the Yitong office of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingbao was Attendant in the Jizhou Yitong office.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Ji.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Governor of Ji.

sentences.zh: 敬保子子恆，位魯郡太守，早卒。

translations.literal: Jingbao's son Ziheng was Governor of Lu and died young.
translations.idiomatic: Jingbao's son Ziheng was Governor of Lu and died early.

sentences.zh: 子恆弟子安、子升，武定中，連元瑾事伏法。

translations.literal: Ziheng's brother's sons Zi'an and Zisheng, in the Wuding era, were executed in connection with the affair of Lian Yuanjin.
translations.idiomatic: Ziheng's brother's sons Zi'an and Zisheng were put to death in the Wuding era in the Lian Yuanjin affair.

sentences.zh: 逞宗人模，字思范，琰兄霸之後也。

translations.literal: A clansman of Cheng's, Mo, courtesy name Sifan, was descended from Yan's elder brother Ba.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng's kinsman Mo, style Sifan, came down from Yan's elder brother Ba.

sentences.zh: 父遵，慕容垂少府卿。

translations.literal: His father Zun was Chamberlain for the Household under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zun had been Chamberlain for the Household under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 模仕宋為榮陽太守。

translations.literal: Mo served Song as Governor of Rongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Mo served the Song as Governor of Rongyang.

sentences.zh: 神抅中，平滑台，歸降，後賜爵武城男。

translations.literal: In the Shenjuan era he pacified Pingtai and surrendered; afterward he was granted the barony of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Shenjuan he pacified Pingtai and submitted; later he was enfeoffed as Baron of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 模長者篤厚，不營榮利，雖為崔浩輕侮，而不為浩屈。

translations.literal: Mo was an elder of grave and sincere bearing who did not pursue glory or profit; though Cui Hao slighted him, he would not bend to Hao.
translations.idiomatic: Mo was a man of weight and integrity who shunned advancement; Cui Hao despised him, yet he would not yield.

sentences.zh: 與崔頤相親，往來如一家。

translations.literal: He was close to Cui Yi and they came and went like one family.
translations.idiomatic: He and Cui Yi were intimate, their households like one.

sentences.zh: 始模在南，妻張氏有二子，仲智、季柔。

translations.literal: At first, while Mo was in the south, his wife Lady Zhang had two sons, Zhongzhi and Jirou.
translations.idiomatic: When Mo was still in the south, Lady Zhang bore him Zhongzhi and Jirou.

sentences.zh: 模至京師，賜妻金氏，生子幼度。

translations.literal: When Mo reached the capital he was given Lady Jin as wife, and she bore Youdu.
translations.idiomatic: At the capital he was given Lady Jin, who bore Youdu.

sentences.zh: 仲智等以父隔遠，乃聚貨規贖歸之。

translations.literal: Zhongzhi and the others, because their father was far away, gathered goods and plotted to ransom him home.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzhi and his brothers, their father lost in the north, pooled wealth to buy his return.

sentences.zh: 其母張曰：「汝父志懷無決，必不能來。

translations.literal: Their mother Zhang said, "Your father's mind is irresolute in its aims—he surely cannot come."
translations.idiomatic: Lady Zhang said, "Your father's resolve is weak—he will never come back."

sentences.zh: 」行人以賄至都，模果顧念幼度等，指謂行人曰：「何忍舍此輩，致為刑辱。

translations.literal: When the travelers brought the bribe to the capital, Mo indeed thought of Youdu and the others, and pointing to the travelers said, "How can I bear to abandon these children and let them suffer punishment?"
translations.idiomatic: The envoys reached the capital with their price; Mo's heart turned to Youdu and the rest, and he told them, "How could I leave these boys to face torment?"

sentences.zh: 當為爾取一人，使名位不減我。

translations.literal: "I shall obtain one man for you so that his name and rank do not fall below mine."
translations.idiomatic: "I will give you a man whose standing will not dim mine."

sentences.zh: 」乃授以申謨，宋東郡太守也。

translations.literal: He then handed over Shen Mo, who was Governor of Dongjun in Song.
translations.idiomatic: And he surrendered Shen Mo, Governor of Dongjun under Song.

sentences.zh: 神。

translations.literal: In the Shen
translations.idiomatic: In the Shen

sentences.zh: 抅中被執，賜妻，生子靈度。

translations.literal: juan era he was seized, given a wife, and had a son, Lingdu.
translations.idiomatic: juan period he was taken, given a wife, and fathered Lingdu.

sentences.zh: 申謨聞此，乃棄妻子走還江外。

translations.literal: When Shen Mo heard of this he abandoned wife and children and fled back beyond the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Mo, hearing of it, cast off wife and children and fled south of the river.

sentences.zh: 靈度刑為閽人。

translations.literal: Lingdu was punished and made a gate eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: Lingdu was sentenced and castrated as a palace gatekeeper.

sentences.zh: 初，直君末，模兄協子邪利為宋魯郡太守，以郡降。

translations.literal: At first, in the last years of Zhijun, Mo's elder brother Xie's son Xieli was Governor of Lu in Song and surrendered the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, at the end of Zhijun, Mo's elder brother Xie's son Xieli, Governor of Lu under Song, surrendered his commandery.

sentences.zh: 賜爵臨淄子，拜廣甯太守，卒。

translations.literal: He was granted the viscounty of Linzi and made Governor of Guangning, then died.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Viscount of Linzi, appointed Governor of Guangning, and died.

sentences.zh: 邪利二子，懷順、次恩，仍居宋青州。

translations.literal: Xieli had two sons, Huaishun and Cien, who still lived in Qingzhou of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xieli left two sons, Huaishun and Cien, who remained in Song's Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷順以父入魏，故不仕。

translations.literal: Huaishun, because his father had entered Wei, did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Huaishun, his father now in Wei, declined office.

sentences.zh: 及魏克青州，懷順迎邪利喪還青州云。

translations.literal: When Wei conquered Qingzhou, Huaishun brought Xieli's coffin back to Qingzhou—or so it is said.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei took Qingzhou, Huaishun bore Xieli's remains home, or so the tale runs.

sentences.zh: 崇弟嶷，字道長。

translations.literal: Chong's younger brother Ni, courtesy name Daochang.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's younger brother Ni, style Daochang.

sentences.zh: 孝文初，為南部尚書，在任十四年。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign he was Director of the Southern Ministry and held the post fourteen years.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiaowen's early reign he headed the Southern Ministry for fourteen years.

sentences.zh: 時南州多事，訟者填門。

translations.literal: The southern provinces were then full of troubles, and litigants filled his gate.
translations.idiomatic: The south seethed with lawsuits; suitors packed his doorway.

sentences.zh: 嶷性儒緩不斷，終日昏睡。

translations.literal: Ni was scholarly, slow, and unable to decide; he slept in a daze all day.
translations.idiomatic: Ni was learned, hesitant, and incurably drowsy—he dozed the day away.

sentences.zh: 李䐶、鄧宗慶等，號為明察，而二人終見誅戮。

translations.literal: Li Kan, Deng Zongqing, and others were called sharp and discerning, yet in the end both were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Kan, Deng Zongqing, and the like were famed for keen judgment—and both were killed.

sentences.zh: 餘十數人或出或免，唯嶷卒得自保。

translations.literal: Of the remaining dozen or so, some were dismissed and some spared; only Ni in the end preserved himself.
translations.idiomatic: A dozen others were driven out or spared; Ni alone kept his skin.

sentences.zh: 時人語曰：「實癡實昏，終得保存。

translations.literal: People said at the time, "Truly dull, truly dim—and in the end he was saved."
translations.idiomatic: A saying ran, "Thick-headed, half asleep—and yet he survived."

sentences.zh: 」後封華山公，入為內都大官，卒。

translations.literal: Later he was enfeoffed as Duke of Huashan, entered court as Grand Inner Steward, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Duke of Huashan, rose to Grand Inner Steward, and died.

sentences.zh: 子祖念襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Zunian inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zunian succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 祖念弟雲，字羅漢，頗有風尚，位南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Zunian's younger brother Yun, courtesy name Luohan, had considerable refinement and held the post of Governor of Southern Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zunian's brother Yun, style Luohan, was a man of taste and became Governor of Southern Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 坐受所部荊山戍主杜虔財，又取官絹，因染遂有割易，御史糾劾。

translations.literal: He was impeached for taking bribes from Du Qian, commandant of the Jingshan garrison in his province, and for seizing official silk, then dyeing and substituting it—there was fraud in the exchange.
translations.idiomatic: He took gifts from Du Qian, his Jingshan garrison chief, and official silk he recolored and swapped—censors brought charges.

sentences.zh: 會赦免。

translations.literal: He was spared when an amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: An amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 卒官，贈豫州刺史，諡文昭。

translations.literal: He died in office and was posthumously made Governor of Yu, with the posthumous name Literary and Illustrious.
translations.idiomatic: He died in post and was posthumously Governor of Yu, styled Literary and Illustrious.

sentences.zh: 長子昕。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Xin.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Xin.

sentences.zh: 昕字元景，少篤學，能誦書，日以中疊舉手極上為率。

translations.literal: Xin, courtesy name Yuanjing, in youth was devoted to study and could recite books; each day he used the height to which he could raise his hand above a stacked set of volumes as his measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xin, style Yuanjing, studied relentlessly and knew books by heart; daily he gauged progress by how high his hand reached over a stack of texts.

sentences.zh: 與太原王延業俱詣魏安豐王延明。

translations.literal: Together with Wang Yanji of Taiyuan he visited the Prince of Anfeng, Yanming.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wang Yanji of Taiyuan called on Prince of Anfeng Yanming.

sentences.zh: 延明歎美之。

translations.literal: Yanming sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Yanming marveled at them.

sentences.zh: 太尉、汝南王悅辟為騎兵參軍。

translations.literal: The Grand Guardian, the Prince of Runan, Yue, engaged him as Riding Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Guardian Prince of Runan Yue took him on as Riding Attendant.

sentences.zh: 舊事，王出則騎兵武服持刀陪從。

translations.literal: By old custom, when a prince went out the riding attendants wore martial dress and carried blades in attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Custom required that when a prince rode forth his attendants follow in martial dress with blades.

sentences.zh: 昕恥之，未嘗肯依行列。

translations.literal: Xin was ashamed of this and would never stand in the procession.
translations.idiomatic: Xin found it shameful and refused to fall into line.

sentences.zh: 悅好逸遊，或馳騁信宿，昕輒棄還。

translations.literal: Yue loved roaming and would sometimes gallop through the night; Xin would abandon him and return.
translations.idiomatic: Yue loved reckless travel and might ride all night; Xin would leave him and go home.

sentences.zh: 悅乃令騎兵在前，手為驅策。

translations.literal: Yue then ordered the cavalry to ride ahead and personally drove them on.
translations.idiomatic: Yue set the horsemen before him and lashed them forward himself.

sentences.zh: 昕舍轡高拱，任馬所之，左右言其誕慢。

translations.literal: Xin dropped the reins and sat with hands clasped high, letting the horse go where it would; those beside him said he was mad and arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Xin let the reins hang and sat with folded hands, wherever the horse pleased; attendants called him insolent and unhinged.

sentences.zh: 悅曰：「府望唯在此賢，不可責也。

translations.literal: Yue said, "My house's hope rests on this worthy alone—he cannot be blamed."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "The honor of my house is this man—leave him be."

sentences.zh: 」悅數散錢於地，令諸佐爭拾之，昕獨不拾。

translations.literal: Yue several times scattered coins on the ground and ordered his staff to scramble for them; Xin alone did not pick any up.
translations.idiomatic: Yue would fling coins for his men to snatch; Xin never stooped.

sentences.zh: 悅又散銀錢以目昕，乃取其一。

translations.literal: Yue again scattered silver coins with his eyes on Xin, and then Xin took one.
translations.idiomatic: Yue tossed silver pieces and watched Xin—at last Xin took one.

sentences.zh: 悅與府寮飲酒，起自移床，人爭進手，昕獨執板卻立。

translations.literal: When Yue drank with his staff he would rise and move his own couch; everyone rushed to help, but Xin alone held his tablet and stood back.
translations.idiomatic: At wine Yue would shift his own seat; all rushed to assist, but Xin clasped his board and stood apart.

sentences.zh: 悅作色曰：「我帝孫，帝子，帝弟，帝叔，今親起輿床，卿何偃蹇？

translations.literal: Yue darkened his face and said, "I am the emperor's grandson, son, brother, and uncle—now I rise to move my couch myself; why this arrogance?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue's color changed: "I am imperial grandson, son, brother, uncle—and I lift my own couch; why do you lounge?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「元景位望微劣，不足使殿下式瞻儀形，安敢以親王僚采，從廝養之役。

translations.literal: He replied, "Yuanjing's rank and standing are slight and low—not enough to make Your Highness bow and view ritual form; how dare I, as a prince's staff member, follow a groom's labor?"
translations.idiomatic: He answered, "Yuanjing is too small a man for Your Highness to bend ritual toward; shall a prince's officer play stable boy?"

sentences.zh: 」悅謝焉。

translations.literal: Yue apologized to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yue begged his pardon.

sentences.zh: 坐上皆引滿酣暢；

translations.literal: Everyone at the table drank deep in high spirits;
translations.idiomatic: The company drank themselves merry;

sentences.zh: 昕先起，臥於閑室，頻召不至。

translations.literal: Xin rose first and lay down in a side room; though summoned repeatedly he would not come.
translations.idiomatic: Xin left early and stretched out in a side chamber; calls could not fetch him.

sentences.zh: 悅乃自詣呼之，曰：「懷其才而忽府主，可謂仁乎？

translations.literal: Yue then went in person to summon him and said, "You cherish your talent yet neglect your lord of the house—can that be called humane?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue sought him out: "You prize your gifts and scorn your host—is that humanity?"

sentences.zh: 」昕曰：「商辛沈湎，其亡也忽諸。

translations.literal: Xin said, "King Zhou of Shang sank in debauchery; his fall came all at once."
translations.idiomatic: Xin said, "King Zhou drowned in pleasure; his end arrived in a blink."

sentences.zh: 府主自忽傲，寮佐敢任其咎？

translations.literal: "The lord of the house is arrogant by his own neglect—how should his staff bear the blame?"
translations.idiomatic: "When the host forgets himself, why should the staff answer for it?"

sentences.zh: 」悅大笑而去。

translations.literal: Yue laughed loudly and left.
translations.idiomatic: Yue laughed and walked away.

sentences.zh: 後除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Later he was made Editorial Assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Editorial Assistant.

sentences.zh: 以兵亂漸起，將避地海隅。

translations.literal: As warfare gradually rose he meant to flee to the sea's edge.
translations.idiomatic: War spread; he planned to escape to the coast.

sentences.zh: 侍中李琰之、黃門侍郎王遵業惜其名士，不容外任，奏除尚書右外兵郎中。

translations.literal: The Attendant-in-chief Li Yanzhi and the Yellow Gate Gentleman Wang Zunye, cherishing so noted a man, would not allow an outer appointment and had him made Right Outer Troops Attendant in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yanzhi and Wang Zunye, unwilling to lose a luminary to the provinces, secured him a post as Right Outer Troops Attendant in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 出為光州長史，故免河陰之難。

translations.literal: He went out as chief administrator of Guang province and thus escaped the disaster at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: As chief administrator of Guang he missed the slaughter at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 遷東萊太守。

translations.literal: He was moved to Governor of Donglai.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Donglai.

sentences.zh: 于時年凶，人多相食，昕勤恤人隱，多所全濟。

translations.literal: In those years famine was severe and many ate one another; Xin worked hard to relieve hidden suffering and saved many.
translations.idiomatic: Famine turned men to cannibalism; Xin labored in secret charity and kept multitudes alive.

sentences.zh: 昕少時與河間邢邵俱為元羅賓友，及守東萊，邵舉室就之。

translations.literal: In youth Xin and Xing Shao of Hejian had both been guests of Yuan Luo; when Xin governed Donglai, Shao brought his whole household to him.
translations.idiomatic: Young Xin and Xing Shao of Hejian had shared Yuan Luo's table; when Xin held Donglai, Shao came with all his kin.

sentences.zh: 郡人以邵是邢杲從弟，會兵將執之。

translations.literal: The people of the commandery, because Shao was a cousin of Xing Gao, were about to seize him with armed men.
translations.idiomatic: Locals, knowing Shao was cousin to the rebel Xing Gao, meant to take him by force.

sentences.zh: 昕以身蔽伏其上，呼曰：「欲執子才，當先執我。

translations.literal: Xin shielded him with his own body and cried, "If you want Zicai, take me first!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin threw himself over Shao and shouted, "Want Zicai? Take me first!"

sentences.zh: 」邵乃免。

translations.literal: Shao was thus spared.
translations.idiomatic: Shao was saved.

sentences.zh: 昕雅好清言，詞無淺俗。

translations.literal: Xin was fond of pure talk; his words were never shallow or vulgar.
translations.idiomatic: Xin loved refined discourse and never spoke cheaply.

sentences.zh: 在東萊時，獲殺其同行侶者，詰之未服。

translations.literal: In Donglai he captured a man who had killed his traveling companion; questioned, the man would not confess.
translations.idiomatic: In Donglai he caught a murderer of his fellow traveler who would not confess under interrogation.

sentences.zh: 昕謂曰：「彼物故不歸，卿無恙而反，何以自明？

translations.literal: Xin said to him, "That man did not return—yet you came back unharmed; how will you clear yourself?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin told him, "Your companion never came home—you walked back whole; how do you prove innocence?"

sentences.zh: 」邢邵後見文襄，說此言以為笑樂。

translations.literal: When Xing Shao later saw Wen Xiang, he repeated the line for amusement.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shao told Wen Xiang the quip for a laugh.

sentences.zh: 昕聞之，詣邵曰：「卿不識造化。

translations.literal: When Xin heard of it he went to Shao and said, "You do not understand creation."
translations.idiomatic: Xin heard and confronted Shao: "You do not know fate."

sentences.zh: 」還謂人曰：「子才應死，我罵之極深。

translations.literal: Returning, he told others, "Zicai ought to die—I cursed him to the bone."
translations.idiomatic: He told others, "Zicai deserves death; I damned him to the marrow."

sentences.zh: 」頃之，以被謗，左遷陽平太守。

translations.literal: Before long, slandered, he was demoted to Governor of Yangping.
translations.idiomatic: Soon slander banished him to Governor of Yangping.

sentences.zh: 在郡有稱績。

translations.literal: In the commandery he won a name for achievement.
translations.idiomatic: There he earned repute for his work.

sentences.zh: 文襄謂人曰：「王元景殊獲我力，由吾數戲之，其在吏事，遂為良二千石。」

translations.literal: Wen Xiang told others, "Wang Yuanjing owes me much strength—because I teased him so often, in official business he has become a fine governor of two thousand households."
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang said, "Yuanjing thrives on my jests—hounded into office, he became a true governor."

sentences.zh: 齊文宣踐阼，拜七兵尚書。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenxuan of Qi took the throne, Xin was made Minister of the Seven Armies.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi Wenxuan's accession Xin became Minister of the Seven Armies.

sentences.zh: 以參議禮，封宜君縣男。

translations.literal: For participating in deliberations on ritual he was enfeoffed as Baron of Yijun.
translations.idiomatic: He helped shape ritual and was made Baron of Yijun.

sentences.zh: 嘗有鮮卑聚語，崔昂戲問昕曰：「頗解此不？

translations.literal: Once there was a cluster speaking Xianbei; Cui Ang playfully asked Xin, "Do you understand any of this?"
translations.idiomatic: A knot of men spoke Xianbei; Cui Ang teased, "Do you follow any of it?"

sentences.zh: 」昕曰：「樓羅，樓羅，實自難解。

translations.literal: Xin said, "Louluo, louluo—it is truly hard to grasp.
translations.idiomatic: Xin said, "Louluo, louluo—beyond me entirely.

sentences.zh: 時唱染於，似道我輩。」

translations.literal: What they sing now, ran-dyed, seems to mean our sort."
translations.idiomatic: Their current chant, ran-dyed, sounds like 'us fellows.'"

sentences.zh: 文宣以昕疏誕，非濟世才，罵：「好門戶，惡人身！

translations.literal: Wenxuan, because Xin was loose and eccentric and not talent for ordering the age, cursed, "Fine house, vile man!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan judged Xin frivolous, no statesman, and snarled, "Noble gate, wretched body!"

sentences.zh: 」又有讒之者，云：「王元景每嗟水運不應遂絕。

translations.literal: Others also slandered him, saying, "Wang Yuanjing constantly sighs that the water transport ought not to have been cut off."
translations.idiomatic: Slander added that Yuanjing lamented the end of the canal.

sentences.zh: 」帝愈怒，乃下詔曰：「元景本自庸才，素無勳行，早沾纓紱，遂履清途。

translations.literal: The emperor grew angrier still and issued an edict: "Yuanjing was by nature a mediocrity, without merit from the first, yet early girded with office and so walked the clear path.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's rage peaked; the edict read, "Yuanjing was always mediocrity, never meritorious, yet early robed and on the high road.

sentences.zh: 發自畿邦，超居詹事。

translations.literal: Starting from the capital region he leapt to Junior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: From the inner provinces he vaulted to Junior Tutor.

sentences.zh: 俄佩龍文之劍，仍啟帶礪之書。

translations.literal: Soon he wore the dragon-pattern sword and opened the book of belt and whetstone.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he bore the dragon sword and the covenant stone.

sentences.zh: 語其器分，何因到此？

translations.literal: Speaking of his measure of capacity—how did he reach here?
translations.idiomatic: By what measure did he climb so high?

sentences.zh: 誠宜清心勵己，少酬萬一。

translations.literal: He ought to have cleared his heart and striven in himself, repaying the throne one part in ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He should have purified himself and repaid the throne in the smallest measure.

sentences.zh: 尚書百揆之本，庶務攸歸。

translations.literal: The Masters of Writing are the root of the hundred offices; all affairs return there.
translations.idiomatic: The Masters of Writing anchor the bureaucracy; all business flows there.

sentences.zh: 元景與奪任情，威福在己。

translations.literal: Yuanjing judged arbitrarily as he pleased; authority and favor rested in himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjing judged capriciously; power and grace were his alone.

sentences.zh: 能使直而為枉，曲反成弦。

translations.literal: He could make the straight crooked and the bent like a bowstring.
translations.idiomatic: He bent straight lines and strung curves.

sentences.zh: 害政損公，名義安在？

translations.literal: He harmed government and injured the public—where was honor's name?
translations.idiomatic: He wounded the state—where was righteousness?

sentences.zh: 偽賞賓郎之味，好詠輕薄之篇。

translations.literal: He feigned the taste of a guest officer and loved to chant frivolous verses.
translations.idiomatic: He played at salon wit and dabbled in light verse.

sentences.zh: 自謂模擬傖楚，曲盡風制。

translations.literal: He called himself imitating the barbarian Chu and claimed to exhaust their airs and styles.
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself a mimic of northern song and boasted mastery of its tones.

sentences.zh: 推此為長，余何足取。

translations.literal: Taking that as his strength—what else is worth taking?
translations.idiomatic: That was his gift—what else had he?

sentences.zh: 此而不繩，後將焉肅？

translations.literal: If this is not disciplined, how will the future be made reverent?
translations.idiomatic: If this goes unpunished, what discipline remains?

sentences.zh: 在身官爵，宜從削奪。

translations.literal: His titles and ranks in life should be stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Strip his living ranks.

sentences.zh: 」於是徙幽州為百姓。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was moved to Youzhou as a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: He was exiled to Youzhou as a commoner.

sentences.zh: 昕任運窮通，不改其操。

translations.literal: Xin accepted fortune and misfortune without changing his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Through fortune and ruin Xin did not bend.

sentences.zh: 未幾，征還，奉敕送蕭莊于梁為主。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled and, by imperial order, escorted Xiao Zhuang to Liang to be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned back to conduct Xiao Zhuang to Liang as king.

sentences.zh: 除銀青光祿大夫，判祠部尚書。

translations.literal: He was made Grand Master of Splendorous Light and acting Minister of the Imperial Ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: He was given Splendorous Light rank and acting charge of the Imperial Ancestors.

sentences.zh: 帝怒臨漳令嵇曄及舍人李文師，以曄賜薛豐洛，文師賜崔士順為奴。

translations.literal: The emperor, enraged at Linzhang Magistrate Ji Ye and Gentleman of the Palace Interior Li Wenshi, gave Ye to Xue Fengluo and Wenshi to Cui Shishun as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan, furious at Ji Ye of Linzhang and Li Wenshi, gave Ye to Xue Fengluo and Wenshi to Cui Shishun as bondsmen.

sentences.zh: 鄭子默私誘昕曰：「自古無朝士作奴。

translations.literal: Zheng Zimo privately urged Xin, "Since antiquity no court gentleman has been made a slave."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zimo whispered to Xin, "Never in history was a courtier enslaved."

sentences.zh: 」昕曰：「箕子為之奴，何言無也？

translations.literal: Xin said, "Jizi became a slave—how can you say there was none?"
translations.idiomatic: Xin answered, "Jizi was enslaved—how say never?"

sentences.zh: 」子默遂以昕言啟文宣，仍曰：「王元景比陛下于紂。

translations.literal: Zimo then reported Xin's words to Wenxuan, adding, "Wang Yuanjing compares Your Majesty to King Zhou of Shang."
translations.idiomatic: Zimo told Wenxuan, adding, "Yuanjing likens Your Majesty to King Zhou."

sentences.zh: 」楊愔微為解之。

translations.literal: Yang Yin lightly excused him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin softened the matter.

sentences.zh: 帝謂愔曰：「王元景是爾博士，爾語皆元景所教。

translations.literal: The emperor told Yin, "Wang Yuanjing is your doctoral teacher—your every word is Yuanjing's teaching."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Yin, "Yuanjing is your teacher; all you say is his lesson."

sentences.zh: 」帝后與朝臣酣飲，昕稱疾不至。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor drank deep with the court, Xin pleaded illness and did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at a court revel, Xin claimed sickness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 帝遣騎執之，見其方搖膝吟詠，遂斬於御前，投屍漳水。

translations.literal: The emperor sent riders to seize him; they found him swaying on his knees, chanting poetry, and he was beheaded before the throne; the corpse was cast into the Zhang waters.
translations.idiomatic: Riders seized him—he was rocking on his knees, reciting verse—and he was cut down before the throne and thrown into the Zhang.

sentences.zh: 天統末，追贈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the end of Tiantong he was posthumously made Minister of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: In late Tiantong he was posthumously Minister of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in twenty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran twenty juan.

sentences.zh: 子顗嗣。

translations.literal: His son Yan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 卒于燕郡太守。

translations.literal: He died as Governor of Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Governor of Yan.

sentences.zh: 昕母清河崔氏，學識有風訓。

translations.literal: Xin's mother was of the Cui clan of Qinghe, learned and with cultured instruction.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was Lady Cui of Qinghe, scholarly and strict in nurture.

sentences.zh: 生九子，皆風流醖籍，世號王氏九龍。

translations.literal: She bore nine sons, all refined and accomplished; the age called them the Nine Dragons of the Wang house.
translations.idiomatic: Nine sons, each polished; the world called them the Nine Dragons of Wang.

sentences.zh: 昕弟暉、昭、晞、皓最知名。

translations.literal: Xin's younger brothers Hui, Zhao, Xi, and Hao were the most famed.
translations.idiomatic: His brothers Hui, Zhao, Xi, and Hao were best known.

sentences.zh: 暉字元旭，少與昕齊名，兼多術藝。

translations.literal: Hui, courtesy name Yuanxu, in youth was as famed as Xin and was also skilled in many arts.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, style Yuanxu, rivaled Xin in youth and mastered many arts besides.

sentences.zh: 卒于中書舍人，贈兗州刺史。

translations.literal: He died as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and was posthumously made Governor of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat and was posthumously Governor of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭字仲亮，少好儒術，又頗以武藝自許。

translations.literal: Zhao, courtesy name Zhongliang, in youth loved Confucian studies and also prided himself somewhat on martial skill.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao, style Zhongliang, cherished the classics and fancied himself no mean hand with arms.

sentences.zh: 性敦篤，以友悌知名。

translations.literal: By nature he was sincere and thick and was famed for brotherly affection.
translations.idiomatic: He was warm and steadfast, renowned for devotion to his brothers.

sentences.zh: 卒于考功郎中。

translations.literal: He died as Director of Merit.
translations.idiomatic: He died as Director of Merit.

sentences.zh: 晞字叔朗，小名沙彌。

translations.literal: Xi, courtesy name Shulang, childhood name Shamini.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, style Shulang, childhood name Shamini.

sentences.zh: 幼而孝謹，淹雅有器度。

translations.literal: From childhood he was filial and careful, refined and of great capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Even as a boy he was filial, careful, elegant, and far-seeing.

sentences.zh: 好學不倦。

translations.literal: He loved learning and never wearied.
translations.idiomatic: He studied without tiring.

sentences.zh: 美容儀，有風則。

translations.literal: His appearance was beautiful and he had bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome and carried himself with grace.

sentences.zh: 魏末，隨母兄東適海隅，與邢子良遊處。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei he followed his mother and elder brother east to the sea's edge and associated with Xing Ziliang.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei foundered he went east with his mother and brother and kept company with Xing Ziliang.

sentences.zh: 子良愛其清悟，與其在洛兩兄書曰：「賢弟彌郎，意識深遠，曠達不羈。

translations.literal: Ziliang loved his clarity and, writing to Xi's two elder brothers in Luoyang, said, "Your worthy younger brother Milang's mind is deep and his reach far; he is free and unbound.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang prized his clarity and wrote to the brothers in Luoyang, "Milang's mind runs deep and wide; he is untrammeled.

sentences.zh: 簡於造次，言必詣理。

translations.literal: Brief in haste, his words always hit principle.
translations.idiomatic: Even rushed, his speech struck truth.

sentences.zh: 吟詠情性，麗絕當時。

translations.literal: When he chants feeling and nature, he is the finest of his age.
translations.idiomatic: In poetry of the heart he has no peer.

sentences.zh: 恐足下方難為兄，不暇慮其不進也。」

translations.literal: I fear you below will find it hard to be elder brothers and will have no leisure to worry that he does not advance."
translations.idiomatic: You may struggle to play elder brother—you will not need to fret that he fails to rise."

sentences.zh: 魏永安初，第二兄暉聘梁，啟晞釋褐，除員外散騎侍郎，征署廣平王開府功曹史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yong'an of Wei, his second elder brother Hui was betrothed in Liang; he had Xi released from common dress and made him Token Attendant Cavalier outside the regular rolls, and he was summoned to the staff of the Prince of Guangping as Recorder.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Yong'an's first year, when Hui was betrothed in Liang, Xi was given Token Attendant Cavalier and summoned to the Prince of Guangping's staff as Recorder.

sentences.zh: 晞願養母，竟不受署。

translations.literal: Xi wished to nurse his mother and in the end did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Xi wanted to care for his mother and declined.

sentences.zh: 母終後，仍屬遷鄴，遨遊鞏、洛，悅其山水。

translations.literal: After his mother died, as the court moved to Ye, he wandered between Gong and Luoyang, delighting in their hills and waters.
translations.idiomatic: After her death, when the court shifted to Ye, he roamed between Gong and Luoyang, in love with landscape.

sentences.zh: 與范陽盧元明、钜鹿魏季景結侶同契，往天陵山，浩然有終焉之志。

translations.literal: He joined Lu Yuanming of Fanyang and Wei Jijing of Julu in sworn friendship and went to Tianling Mountain, with a vast longing to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: With Lu Yuanming of Fanyang and Wei Jijing of Julu he swore fellowship and climbed Tianling, resolved to finish life there.

sentences.zh: 及西魏將獨孤信入洛，署為開府記室。

translations.literal: When the Western Wei general Dugu Xin entered Luoyang, Xi was appointed Recorder on his staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Dugu Xin of Western Wei took Luoyang, Xi was named Recorder on his staff.

sentences.zh: 晞稱先被犬傷，困篤，不赴。

translations.literal: Xi claimed he had earlier been bitten by a dog and was gravely ill, and did not attend.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said an old dog bite had laid him low, and he did not go.

sentences.zh: 有故人疑其所傷非猘，書勸令赴。

translations.literal: An old friend doubted the wound was not rabid and wrote urging him to come.
translations.idiomatic: A friend doubted it was mad-dog fever and wrote urging him to report.

sentences.zh: 晞復書曰：「辱告存念，見令起疾。

translations.literal: Xi replied, "I am shamed by your care in asking me to rise from illness.
translations.idiomatic: Xi answered, "Your concern shames me—you bid me rise though ill.

sentences.zh: 循復眷旨，似疑吾所傷未必是猘。

translations.literal: Following through on your gracious intent, it seems you doubt that my wound may not be rabies.
translations.idiomatic: Reading your kindness, you seem unsure this is rabies at all.

sentences.zh: 吾豈願其必猘？

translations.literal: Do I wish it must be rabies?
translations.idiomatic: Do I want it to be rabies?

sentences.zh: 但理契無疑耳。

translations.literal: But reason and circumstance leave no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Reason leaves none.

sentences.zh: 就足下疑之，亦有過說。

translations.literal: As for your doubt, there is also excess in it.
translations.idiomatic: Your doubt overshoots.

sentences.zh: 足下既疑其非猘，亦可疑其是猘，其疑半矣。

translations.literal: Since you doubt it is not rabies, you may also doubt it is rabies—the doubt is already half.
translations.idiomatic: Doubt it is not, and you may doubt it is—your doubt is already half the whole.

sentences.zh: 若疑其是猘而營護，雖非猘亦無損。

translations.literal: If you doubt it is rabies and still nurse it, though it is not rabies there is no harm.
translations.idiomatic: If you fear rabies and treat it, no harm comes when it is not.

sentences.zh: 疑非猘而不療，儻是猘則難救。

translations.literal: If you doubt it is not rabies and do not treat it, perchance it is rabies and then it cannot be saved.
translations.idiomatic: If you deem it harmless and withhold care, and it is rabies, nothing will save you.

sentences.zh: 然則過療則致萬全，過不療或至於死。

translations.literal: Thus overtreatment brings ten thousand certainties of safety; overt neglect may lead to death.
translations.idiomatic: Over-care buys perfect safety; under-care buys death.

sentences.zh: 若王晞無可惜也，則不足取；

translations.literal: If Wang Xi were not worth keeping, then he is not worth taking;
translations.idiomatic: If Wang Xi is worthless, do not take him;

sentences.zh: 既取之，便是可惜。

translations.literal: since you have taken him, he is worth keeping.
translations.idiomatic: having taken him, he is worth keeping.

sentences.zh: 奈何奪其萬全，任其或死！

translations.literal: How can you rob him of perfect safety and leave him to possible death!
translations.idiomatic: Why steal his safety and risk his death!

sentences.zh: 且將軍威德所被飆飛霧襲，方掩八紘，豈在一介？

translations.literal: Moreover the general's authority and virtue sweep like storm and mist, about to cover the eight directions—how much less one man!
translations.idiomatic: Your general's might rolls like wind and fog over the realm—what is one man!

sentences.zh: 若必從隗始，先須濟其生靈。

translations.literal: If you must begin with Kuai, first you must save the living.
translations.idiomatic: If service starts with the lowly, save lives first.

sentences.zh: 足下何不從容為將軍言也？

translations.literal: Why will you not speak to the general at ease on his behalf?"
translations.idiomatic: Will you not plead for him, gently, to the general?"

sentences.zh: 」於是方得見寬。

translations.literal: Only then was he granted leniency.
translations.idiomatic: Leniency followed.

sentences.zh: 俄而信返，晞遂歸鄴。

translations.literal: Before long Xin returned, and Xi went back to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xin withdrew, and Xi returned to Ye.

sentences.zh: 齊神武訪朝廷子弟忠孝謹密者，令與諸子遊。

translations.literal: Gao Huan sought court youths who were loyal, filial, and careful to roam with his sons.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Huan sought young men of loyalty and filial care to companion his sons.

sentences.zh: 晞與清河崔贍、頓丘李度、范陽盧正通首應此選。

translations.literal: Xi, together with Cui Zhan of Qinghe, Li Du of Dunqiu, and Lu Zhengtong of Fanyang, were the first chosen.
translations.idiomatic: Xi, with Cui Zhan, Li Du, and Lu Zhengtong, were first picked.

sentences.zh: 文襄時為大將軍，握晞等手曰：「我弟並向成長，志識未定，近善狎惡，不能不移。

translations.literal: When Wen Xiang was Grand General he took Xi's hand and said, "My younger brothers are still growing; their wills are unsettled—near goodness or near evil, they cannot but be shifted.
translations.idiomatic: Wen Xiang as Grand General clasped their hands: "My brothers are still forming; good and ill companions will move them.

sentences.zh: 吾弟不負義方，卿祿位常亞召弟；

translations.literal: You do not fail righteousness; your rank and stipend shall always stand below my brothers'—
translations.idiomatic: Hold to righteousness; your honors shall stay beneath my brothers'—

sentences.zh: 若苟使回邪，致相詿誤，罪及門族，非止一身。

translations.literal: but if you knowingly lead them astray and bring mutual ruin, the guilt reaches your clan, not you alone."
translations.idiomatic: yet if you bend them to evil, the house pays, not you alone."

sentences.zh: 」晞隨神武到晉陽，補中外府功曹參軍，帶常山公演友。

translations.literal: Xi followed Shenwu to Jinyang and was made Staff Officer in the inner and outer offices, attending Prince of Changshan Yan as friend.
translations.idiomatic: Xi followed Shenwu to Jinyang as staff officer, companion to Prince of Changshan Yan.

sentences.zh: 齊天保初，行太原郡事。

translations.literal: At the opening of Qi Tianbao he acted for Taiyuan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: At Qi Tianbao's start he governed Taiyuan in commission.

sentences.zh: 及文宣昏逸，常山王數諫。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan grew dissolute, the Prince of Changshan remonstrated repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan turned reckless, Prince Yan remonstrated again and again.

sentences.zh: 帝疑王假辭於晞，欲加大辟。

translations.literal: The emperor suspected the prince borrowed words from Xi and meant to impose the death penalty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought Yan spoke through Xi and prepared capital punishment.

sentences.zh: 王私謂晞曰：「博士，明日當作一條事，為欲相活，亦圖自全，宜深體勿怪。

translations.literal: The prince told Xi privately, "Doctor, tomorrow you must do one thing—for I mean to keep you alive and also save myself; understand deeply and do not resent it."
translations.idiomatic: Yan whispered to Xi, "Doctor, tomorrow do a thing—to save you and me; do not blame me."

sentences.zh: 」乃於眾中杖晞二十。

translations.literal: Then before the assembly he beat Xi twenty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Before the court he had Xi thrashed twenty blows.

sentences.zh: 帝尋發怒，聞晞得杖，以故不殺，髡鞭鉗配甲坊。

translations.literal: The emperor soon raged again; hearing Xi had been beaten, for that reason he did not kill him, but shaved his head, flogged him, fettered him, and sent him to the armor workshop.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan raged anew; learning Xi had been beaten, he spared his life but shaved, lashed, chained, and sent him to the armory.

sentences.zh: 居三年，王又固諫爭，大被毆撻，閉口不食。

translations.literal: After three years the prince again remonstrated fiercely, was himself beaten savagely, closed his mouth and would not eat.
translations.idiomatic: Three years on, Yan remonstrated once more, was thrashed himself, and fasted.

sentences.zh: 太后極憂之。

translations.literal: The empress dowager was deeply grieved.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager grieved.

sentences.zh: 帝謂左右曰：「儻小兒死，奈我老母何！

translations.literal: The emperor told those beside him, "If the boy dies, what of my old mother!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor muttered, "If the boy dies, what becomes of my mother?"

sentences.zh: 」於是每問王疾，謂曰：「努力強食，當以王晞還汝。

translations.literal: Thereafter he often inquired after the prince's illness and said, "Force yourself to eat—I will give Wang Xi back to you."
translations.idiomatic: He asked after Yan's health and said, "Eat—I will return Wang Xi."

sentences.zh: 」乃釋晞令往。

translations.literal: Then he released Xi and sent him to the prince.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was freed and sent to Yan.

sentences.zh: 王抱晞曰；

translations.literal: The prince embraced Xi and said;
translations.idiomatic: Yan embraced Xi and said:

sentences.zh: 「吾氣息惙然，恐不復相見！

translations.literal: "My breath is faint—I fear we shall not meet again!"
translations.idiomatic: "I can barely breathe—we may not meet again!"

sentences.zh: 」晞流涕曰：「天道神明，豈令殿下遂斃此舍。

translations.literal: Xi wept and said, "Heaven's way and the spirits—how could they let Your Highness die in this house!"
translations.idiomatic: Xi wept, "Heaven would not let Your Highness perish here!"

sentences.zh: 至尊親為人兄，尊為人主，安可與計？

translations.literal: "The Supreme One is elder brother to men and lord to the realm—how can one reckon with him?"
translations.idiomatic: "The Son of Heaven is brother and sovereign—do not measure him as an equal."

sentences.zh: 殿下不食，太后亦不食，殿下縱不自惜，不惜太后乎？

translations.literal: "If Your Highness will not eat, the empress dowager also will not eat; if Your Highness does not cherish yourself, will you not cherish her?"
translations.idiomatic: "If you refuse food, your mother refuses it too; spare yourself for her sake."

sentences.zh: 」言未卒，王強坐而飯。

translations.literal: Before he finished speaking the prince forced himself to sit and eat.
translations.idiomatic: Yan sat up and ate before Xi finished.

sentences.zh: 晞由是得免徒，還為王友。

translations.literal: Xi was thus spared penal service and returned as the prince's friend.
translations.idiomatic: Xi was freed from labor and again Yan's companion.

sentences.zh: 王復錄尚書事。

translations.literal: The prince again held charge of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Yan again directed the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 新除官者必詣王謝職，去必辭。

translations.literal: Newly appointed officers had to visit the prince to thank him for office and take leave when departing.
translations.idiomatic: Every new appointee thanked Yan in person on taking and leaving office.

sentences.zh: 晞言于王曰：「受爵天朝，拜恩私第，自古以為幹紀。

translations.literal: Xi said to the prince, "To receive rank from the court and bow in thanks at a private house has always been reckoned a breach of discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Xi told him, "Rank from the throne, thanks in a private house—that has always been corruption.

sentences.zh: 朝廷文武，出入辭謝，宜一約絕。

translations.literal: Court civil and military, coming and going with farewells of thanks—let it all be stopped at once.
translations.idiomatic: Let every officer's comings and goings end with one rule.

sentences.zh: 主上顒顒，賴殿下扶翼。

translations.literal: The sovereign is stern in bearing; he relies on Your Highness to support him."
translations.idiomatic: The throne stands uneasy; it leans on you."

sentences.zh: 」王深納焉。

translations.literal: The prince took it deeply to heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yan took the counsel to heart.

sentences.zh: 常從容謂晞曰：「主上起居不恆，卿耳目所具，吾豈可以前逢一怒，遂爾結舌。

translations.literal: He often said calmly to Xi, "The sovereign's conduct is inconstant; what your eyes and ears have gathered—can I fall silent after one burst of anger?"
translations.idiomatic: He often told Xi, "The emperor's ways shift—what you've seen—shall I bite my tongue after one rage?"

sentences.zh: 卿宜為撰諫草，吾當伺便極諫。

translations.literal: "You should draft remonstrances; I shall seize a moment to speak to the limit."
translations.idiomatic: "Draft protests; I'll speak when the moment comes."

sentences.zh: 」晞遂條十餘事以呈，因切諫王曰：「今朝廷乃爾，欲學介子匹夫，輕一朝之命，狂藥令人不自覺，刀箭豈復識親疏？

translations.literal: Xi then set out more than ten items and presented them, and urgently admonished the prince, "The court is now thus—do you wish to imitate Jie Zi's common man and lightly throw away a morning's life? Madness makes a man unaware of himself; do blades and arrows know kinship?
translations.idiomatic: Xi listed ten points and warned, "The court is mad—will you mimic Jie Zi and toss one dawn's life away? Drunken rage forgets kin; steel knows no family.

sentences.zh: 一旦禍出理外，將奈殿下家業何！

translations.literal: Once calamity comes outside reason, what of Your Highness's house?
translations.idiomatic: When disaster strikes beyond sense, what of your line?

sentences.zh: 奈皇太后何！

translations.literal: What of the empress dowager?
translations.idiomatic: What of your mother?

sentences.zh: 乞且將順，日慎一日。

translations.literal: I beg you for now to yield and be cautious day by day."
translations.idiomatic: Yield now; guard each day."

sentences.zh: 」王歔欷不自勝，曰：「乃至是乎！

translations.literal: The prince sobbed uncontrollably and said, "It has come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: Yan wept, "So far gone!"

sentences.zh: 」明日見晞，曰：「吾長夜九思，今便息意。

translations.literal: The next day he saw Xi and said, "I brooded nine nights—now my mind rests."
translations.idiomatic: Next day he said, "Nine nights I thought—now I am at peace."

sentences.zh: 」便命火對晞焚之。

translations.literal: He ordered a fire and burned the drafts before Xi.
translations.idiomatic: He burned the drafts before Xi.

sentences.zh: 後王承間苦諫，遂致忤旨。

translations.literal: Later the prince seized chances to remonstrate bitterly and thus offended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yan remonstrated hard and provoked wrath.

sentences.zh: 帝使力士反接伏，白刃注頸，罵曰：「小子何知，欲以吏才非我！

translations.literal: The emperor had brawny men twist his arms behind him, set a white blade at his throat, and curse, "Boy, what do you know—do you mean to judge me with clerk's talent?
translations.idiomatic: Brawlers bent his arms back, a blade at his throat: "Pup, what do you know—measuring me with clerk's skill?

sentences.zh: 是誰教汝？

translations.literal: Who taught you?"
translations.idiomatic: Who taught you?"

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「天下噤口，除臣誰敢有言？

translations.literal: The prince said, "The realm is mute—apart from me, who dares speak?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "All China is silent—who but me?"

sentences.zh: 」帝催遣捶楚，亂杖數十。

translations.literal: The emperor pressed for beating; he was clubbed dozens of times in confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Wenxuan ordered blows; dozens of strokes fell at random.

sentences.zh: 會醉臥得解。

translations.literal: He was spared when the emperor fell drunk asleep.
translations.idiomatic: Drunken sleep ended it.

sentences.zh: 爾後褻黷之好，遍于宗戚，所往留連，俾畫作夜；

translations.literal: Afterward licentious pleasures spread through the imperial kin; wherever he lingered, he turned night into day;
translations.idiomatic: Then debauchery ran through the clan; wherever he stayed, night became day;

sentences.zh: 唯常山邸多無適而去。

translations.literal: only at the Prince of Changshan's residence did he mostly find nothing to his liking and leave.
translations.idiomatic: only Changshan's hall rarely pleased him long.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩，濟南嗣立。

translations.literal: When the emperor died, Jinan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: At Wenxuan's death Jinan reigned.

sentences.zh: 王謂晞曰：「一人垂拱，吾曹亦保優閑。

translations.literal: The prince told Xi, "One man holds his hands in his sleeves—we too shall keep ease and leisure."
translations.idiomatic: Yan told Xi, "One man reigns at ease—we too may rest."

sentences.zh: 」因言：「朝廷寬仁慈恕，真守文良主。

translations.literal: He also said, "The court is broad, benevolent, and forgiving—a true ruler who guards the laws."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "The throne is mild and forgiving—a keeper of the old ways."

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「天保享詐，東宮委一胡人。

translations.literal: Xi said, "Tianbao enjoyed the mandate, yet the eastern palace was left to a barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Tianbao held heaven's trust, yet the heir was a barbarian.

sentences.zh: 今卒覽萬機，駕馭雄傑。

translations.literal: Now he suddenly holds the myriad reins and drives fierce heroes.
translations.idiomatic: Now he grips every rein and rides fierce men.

sentences.zh: 如聖德幼沖，未堪雙難，而使他姓出納詔命，必權有所歸。

translations.literal: If sagely virtue is still young and cannot bear twin burdens, yet another surname handles edicts in and out, power must settle somewhere.
translations.idiomatic: If the sage is young and cannot bear double weight, yet aliens issue orders, power will find a seat.

sentences.zh: 殿下雖欲守籓職，其可得也？

translations.literal: Though Your Highness wishes to keep only your fief, is that possible?
translations.idiomatic: Though you mean to keep your fief alone, can you?

sentences.zh: 假令得遂沖退，自審家祚得保靈長不？

translations.literal: Even if you could truly yield and withdraw, do you judge that your house could long keep its fortune?
translations.idiomatic: Even yielding, do you think your line would endure?"

sentences.zh: 」王默然，思念久之，曰：「何以處我？

translations.literal: The prince was silent, brooded long, and said, "What is to be done with me?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan was silent, then said, "What am I to do?"

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「周公抱成王朝諸侯，攝政七年，然後復子明辟。

translations.literal: Xi said, "The Duke of Zhou held King Cheng and faced the feudal lords, ruled as regent seven years, then returned the bright mandate to the son.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "The Duke of Zhou held the boy-king, ruled seven years, then returned the realm.

sentences.zh: 幸有故事，惟殿下慮之。

translations.literal: Fortunately there is this precedent—only Your Highness must ponder it."
translations.idiomatic: The precedent exists—ponder it."

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「我安敢自擬周公？

translations.literal: The prince said, "How would I dare compare myself to the Duke of Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Yan said, "How dare I match the Duke of Zhou?"

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「殿下今日地望，欲避周公得邪？

translations.literal: Xi said, "With Your Highness's standing today, do you think you can avoid the Duke of Zhou?"
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "At your height today, can you avoid him?"

sentences.zh: 」王不答。

translations.literal: The prince did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said nothing.

sentences.zh: 帝臨發，敕王從駕，除晞并州長史。

translations.literal: When the emperor set out, he ordered the prince to follow the carriage and made Xi chief administrator of Bing.
translations.idiomatic: On the emperor's departure he commanded Yan to accompany him and made Xi chief administrator of Bing.

sentences.zh: 及王至鄴，誅楊、燕等。

translations.literal: When the King reached Ye, he executed Yang, Yan, and the others.
translations.idiomatic: When the King reached Ye, he put Yang, Yan, and their faction to death.

sentences.zh: 詔以王為大丞相、都督中外諸軍事，督攝文武還并州。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him Grand Chancellor and Commander-in-Chief of all armies at home and abroad, with authority over civil and military affairs, and he returned to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made him Grand Chancellor and supreme commander of all forces, civil and military, and he went back to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 及至，延晞謂曰：「不早用卿言，使群小弄權，幾至傾覆。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Yan Xi said to him: "Had you taken my counsel earlier, those petty men would not have seized power and we would nearly have been overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: On his arrival Yan Xi said, "Had you heeded me sooner, petty men would never have held the reins and we would almost have been ruined.

sentences.zh: 今君側雖獲暫清，終當何以處我？

translations.literal: Those beside the throne are cleared for the moment—but in the end how will you deal with me?"
translations.idiomatic: The court is clean for now—but what will you do with me in the end?"

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「殿下將往時地位，猶可以名教出處。

translations.literal: Xi replied: "Your Highness's former standing still allowed you to take office or leave it under the teaching of moral names.
translations.idiomatic: Xi answered, "Your Highness's old rank still let you enter or leave office by the norms of moral teaching.

sentences.zh: 今日事勢，遂關天時，非復人理所及。

translations.literal: Today's situation turns on Heaven's timing; it is no longer within what human reason can reach."
translations.idiomatic: Today's turn of affairs hangs on Heaven's hour; it is past what men can argue."

sentences.zh: 」有頃，奏趙郡王睿為左長史，晞為司馬。

translations.literal: Before long it was memorialized to appoint Prince of Zhao Commandery Rui as Left Chief Steward; Xi was made Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Soon a memorial named Prince Rui of Zhao commandery Left Chief Steward and made Xi his Administrator.

sentences.zh: 每夜載入，晝則不與語，以晞儒緩，恐不允武將之意。

translations.literal: Each night he was brought in by carriage; by day they did not speak with him, because Xi was scholarly and slow and they feared he would not satisfy the military men's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: He was carted in every night yet not spoken to by day—Xi was too bookish and mild to please the generals.

sentences.zh: 後進晞密室，曰：「比王侯諸貴每見煎迫，言我違天不祥，恐當或有變起，吾正欲以正法繩之。

translations.literal: Later the King entered Xi's private room and said: "Lately the nobles press me hard, saying I go against Heaven and court ill fortune, and I fear some uprising may come; I mean to bind them by the proper law."
translations.idiomatic: Later the King came to Xi's chamber and said, "The great families hound me, calling my course unlucky and heaven-defying. I fear trouble and mean to punish them by law."

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「朝廷比者疏遠親戚，甯思骨血之重。

translations.literal: Xi said: "The court of late has kept kin at a distance and scarcely remembers the weight of flesh and bone.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "The court has lately estranged its kin and forgotten the weight of blood."

sentences.zh: 殿下倉卒所行，非復人臣之事。

translations.literal: What Your Highness has done in haste is no longer the conduct of a subject.
translations.idiomatic: What you have done in haste is no longer how a subject should act.

sentences.zh: 芒刺在背，交戟入頸，上下相疑，何由可久？

translations.literal: A thorn in the back, crossed halberds at the throat—superior and inferior doubting each other—how can that long endure?
translations.idiomatic: Dagger at your back, blades at your neck—ruler and ruled doubting one another—how can that last?

sentences.zh: 且天道不恆，虧盈迭至，神機變化，肸蠻斯集。

translations.literal: Moreover Heaven's way is not constant; loss and gain take turns; divine calculation shifts, and omens gather.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's way is not fixed; waxing and waning alternate; omens shift and spirits stir.

sentences.zh: 雖執謙挹，粃糠神器。

translations.literal: Though you hold humility in check, you treat the sacred vessel as chaff.
translations.idiomatic: Though you feign humility, you treat the throne as chaff.

sentences.zh: 便是違上玄之意，墜先人之基。

translations.literal: That is to go against the Supreme Mystery and topple your forefathers' foundation."
translations.idiomatic: That defies Heaven above and casts down your fathers' house."

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「卿何敢鬚髮非所宜言！

translations.literal: The King said: "How dare you speak what your beard should not say!
translations.idiomatic: The King cried, "How dare you say what no beard should utter!

sentences.zh: 須致卿於法。

translations.literal: I must bring you to law."
translations.idiomatic: I will have you punished by law."

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「竊謂天時人事，同無異揆。

translations.literal: Xi said: "I take it that Heaven's timing and human affairs follow one measure.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Heaven's hour and men's affairs, I believe, share one rule.

sentences.zh: 是以冒犯雷霆，不憚斧鉞。

translations.literal: Therefore I offend the thunderbolt and do not fear axe and halberd.
translations.idiomatic: So I brave the thunderbolt and do not fear the axe.

sentences.zh: 今日得披肝膽，抑亦神明攸贊。

translations.literal: Today I may lay bare liver and gall; perhaps the spirits too approve."
translations.idiomatic: Today I lay my heart bare—and perhaps the spirits approve."

sentences.zh: 」王曰：「拯難匡時，方俟聖哲，吾何敢私議，幸勿多言。

translations.literal: The King said: "To rescue peril and set the age right still awaits a sage; how dare I debate in private? Pray speak no more."
translations.idiomatic: The King said, "To save the age still wants a sage—how dare I plot in private? Say no more."

sentences.zh: 」尋有詔，以丞相任重，普進府寮一班，晞以司馬領吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Soon an edict came: because the Chancellor's burden was heavy, all staff in his bureau were promoted one grade; Xi as Administrator also held the post of Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict, citing the Chancellor's heavy load, raised every man in his bureau one grade; Xi as Administrator also headed a personnel desk.

sentences.zh: 丞相從事中郎陸杳將出使，臨別，握晞手曰：「相王功格區宇，天下樂推，歌謠滿道，物無異望。

translations.literal: Lu Yao, Attendant Gentleman in the Chancellor's service, was about to go on a mission; at parting he grasped Xi's hand and said: "The Chancellor's merit fills the realm; the world gladly pushes him forward; songs fill the roads and nothing else is desired.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Yao of the Chancellor's staff was leaving on a mission; at farewell he seized Xi's hand. "The Chancellor's merit fills the realm; all men push him forward; songs crowd the roads and every heart looks one way.

sentences.zh: 杳等伏隸，願披赤心。

translations.literal: We lie prostrate and wish to lay bare our loyal hearts.
translations.idiomatic: We lie prostrate and would bare our hearts.

sentences.zh: 而忽奉外使，無由面盡短誠，寸心謹以仰白。

translations.literal: Yet suddenly I am sent abroad and cannot speak my short plea face to face; my inch of heart I respectfully raise to you."
translations.idiomatic: Yet I am sent away and cannot speak face to face; this inch of heart I raise to you."

sentences.zh: 」晞尋述杳言。

translations.literal: Xi soon repeated Yao's words.
translations.idiomatic: Xi soon repeated Yao's words to the King.

sentences.zh: 王曰：「若內外咸有異望，趙彥深朝夕左右，何因都無所論？

translations.literal: The King said: "If inside and outside alike harbor such hopes, Zhao Yanshen is at my side morning and night—why has he never said a word?
translations.idiomatic: The King said, "If court and camp share this wish, Zhao Yanshen is with me day and night—why has he never spoken?

sentences.zh: 自以卿意試密與言之。

translations.literal: Try in secret what you think and speak with him."
translations.idiomatic: Sound him out in secret as you think best."

sentences.zh: 」晞以事隙問彥深。

translations.literal: Xi took an opening to ask Yanshen.
translations.idiomatic: Xi found a moment to ask Yanshen.

sentences.zh: 曰：「我比亦驚此音謠，每欲陳聞，則口噤心戰。

translations.literal: He said: "I too have been startled by these songs; each time I wished to report it my mouth froze and my heart trembled.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshen said, "These songs startled me too; each time I meant to speak my mouth froze and my heart shook.

sentences.zh: 弟既發論，吾亦欲昧死一披肝膽。

translations.literal: Since you have broached the matter, I too will risk death and lay bare liver and gall once."
translations.idiomatic: Now that you have opened the matter, I too will risk death and lay my heart bare."

sentences.zh: 」因亦同勸。

translations.literal: He likewise urged the same course.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the same course as the others.

sentences.zh: 是時諸王公將相日敦請，四方岳牧表陳符命。

translations.literal: At that time the kings, dukes, ministers, and generals daily pressed the plea; governors and prefects from the four quarters tabled memorials with portents of mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Kings, dukes, ministers, and generals pressed daily; governors from the four quarters tabled portents of the mandate.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年八月，昭帝踐阼。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the first year of Qianming, Emperor Zhao ascended the throne.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Qianming 1, Emperor Zhao took the throne.

sentences.zh: 九月，除晞散騎常侍，仍領兼吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the ninth month Xi was made Regular Attendant and continued to hold the concurrent post of Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Xi was made Regular Attendant and still held his personnel post.

sentences.zh: 後因奏事罷，帝從容曰：「比日何為自同外客，略不可見？

translations.literal: Later, when a memorial audience ended, the Emperor said at ease: "Lately why have you made yourself like an outsider I can scarcely see?
translations.idiomatic: After an audience the Emperor said gently, "Why lately do you act like a stranger I can hardly see?

sentences.zh: 自今假非局司，但有所懷，隨宜作一牒，候少隙即徑進也。

translations.literal: From now on, unless it is your bureau's business, whenever you have something in mind write a note as you please and, when a brief gap appears, bring it straight in."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, unless it is bureau business, write whatever is on your mind and bring it in the first spare moment."

sentences.zh: 」因敕尚書陽休之、鴻臚卿崔勵等三人，每日本職務罷，併入東廊。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered Yang Xiuzhi of the Ministry of Personnel, Cui Li of the Court for Diplomatic Reception, and two others—three men in all—each day when their regular duties ended to enter together the east corridor.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Yang Xiuzhi, Cui Li, and one other—three men—to join the east corridor after daily duties.

sentences.zh: 共舉錄歷代廢禮墜樂，職司廢置，朝饗異同，輿服增損，或道德高俊久在沈淪，或巧言眩俗，妖邪害政，爰及田市舟車、徵稅通塞、婚葬儀軌、貴賤等衰，有不便於時而古今行用不已者，或自古利用而當今毀棄者，悉令詳思，以漸條奏。

translations.literal: Together they were to record rites and music abandoned through the ages, offices abolished, differences in court sacrifice, changes in carriage and dress, or men of lofty virtue long sunk in obscurity, or clever words that dazzle the vulgar and evil that harms government, reaching to markets, taxes, marriage and burial, noble and base—whatever was inconvenient to the times yet still used from past to present, or useful in antiquity yet cast away today—and think through all in detail and report item by item.
translations.idiomatic: Together they were to catalogue lost rites and music, abolished offices, changes in sacrifice and dress, worthy men long buried in obscurity, flashy words and harmful cults, markets, taxes, marriage and burial, rank and mean—whatever ill fit the age yet lingered, or what antiquity used and today threw away—and report step by step.

sentences.zh: 未待頓備，遇憶續聞。

translations.literal: They need not wait until all was ready; whenever something came to mind they might continue to report.
translations.idiomatic: They need not finish all at once; whenever memory stirred they could report again.

sentences.zh: 朝晡給典禦食，畢景聽還。

translations.literal: Morning and evening they were given imperial pantry food; at day's end they were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Morning and evening they ate from the imperial pantry; at dusk they went home.

sentences.zh: 時百官請建東宮，敕未許，每令晞就東堂監視太子冠服，導引趨拜。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials asked to establish an Eastern Palace, the edict was not granted; each time Xi was sent to the east hall to oversee the crown prince's cap and robes and guide his steps in obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: When officials asked for an Heir Apparent's establishment, the throne refused; Xi was sent to the east hall to watch the crown prince's dress and guide his bows.

sentences.zh: 尋拜為太子太傅。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 晞以局司奉璽授皇太子。

translations.literal: Xi in his bureau duty presented the seal to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In bureau duty Xi presented the seal to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 太子釋奠，又兼中庶子。

translations.literal: At the crown prince's sacrifice to the sage he also served as Junior Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: At the crown prince's school sacrifice he also served as Junior Mentor.

sentences.zh: 帝謂曰：「今既當劇職，不得尋常舒慢也。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said to him: "Now that you hold heavy office, you must not be at ease and slack as before."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor told him, "Now that your post is weighty, you must not lounge as before."

sentences.zh: 帝將北征，敕問：「比何所聞？

translations.literal: When the Emperor was about to campaign north he ordered and asked: "What have you heard lately?"
translations.idiomatic: Before a northern campaign the Emperor asked, "What have you heard lately?"

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「道路傳言，車駕將行。

translations.literal: Xi said: "On the roads they say the imperial carriage will set out."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "The roads say the carriage will march."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「庫莫奚南侵，我未經親戎，因此聊欲習武。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "The Kumo Xi raid the south; I have not yet led troops myself and therefore wish a little to drill in arms."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "The Kumo Xi raid south; I have never led an army and wish to learn war on the march."

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「鑾駕巡狩，為復何爾？

translations.literal: Xi said: "The imperial carriage on tour—what is the need?
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "The sacred carriage on tour—to what end?

sentences.zh: 若輕有征戰，恐天下失望。

translations.literal: If you lightly take the field, I fear the realm will lose heart."
translations.idiomatic: If you lightly go to war, the realm will lose heart."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「此懦夫常慮，吾自當臨時斟酌。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "That is the coward's constant worry; I myself will weigh matters when the time comes."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "That is a coward's fret; I will judge when the hour comes."

sentences.zh: 」帝使齋帥裴澤、主書蔡暉伺察群下，好相誣枉，朝士呼為裴、蔡。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent the fast-officer Pei Ze and the chief clerk Cai Hui to spy on the court below, fond of false accusations; courtiers called them Pei and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Pei Ze and Cai Hui to spy on officials, given to slander; men called them Pei and Cai.

sentences.zh: 時二人奏：「車駕北征後，陽休之、王晞數與諸人遊宴，不以公事在懷。

translations.literal: At that time the two reported: "After the northern campaign Yang Xiuzhi and Wang Xi several times feasted and roamed with others and did not keep public business in mind."
translations.idiomatic: They reported, "After the northern march Yang Xiuzhi and Wang Xi feasted and wandered and neglected office."

sentences.zh: 」帝杖休之、晞脛各四十。

translations.literal: The Emperor had Xiuzhi and Xi flogged forty strokes on the shins.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had both men flogged forty strokes on the shins.

sentences.zh: 帝斬人於前，問晞曰：「此人合死不？

translations.literal: The Emperor executed a man before him and asked Xi: "Does this man deserve death?"
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded a man before Xi and asked, "Did this man deserve death?"

sentences.zh: 」晞曰：「罪實合死，但恨其不得死地。

translations.literal: Xi said: "His crime indeed deserved death, but I regret that he did not die in the proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "His crime deserved death, but not here.

sentences.zh: 臣聞刑人於市，與眾棄之；

translations.literal: I have heard that punishment is carried out in the market and the multitude casts the body away;
translations.idiomatic: I have heard punishment belongs in the market, where the people cast the body away;

sentences.zh: 殿廷非殺戮之所。

translations.literal: the palace hall is not a place for killing."
translations.idiomatic: the palace is no place to kill."

sentences.zh: 」帝改容曰：「自今當為王公改之。」

translations.literal: The Emperor changed expression and said: "From now on I shall change this for the kings and dukes."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor's face changed. "From now on I shall change this—for kings and dukes alike."

sentences.zh: 帝欲以晞為侍中，苦辭不受。
