translations.literal: The Emperor wished to make Xi Attendant-in-Ordinary; he firmly declined and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor wished to make him Attendant-in-Ordinary; Xi firmly refused.

sentences.zh: 或勸晞勿自疏，晞曰：「我少年以來，閱要人多矣。

translations.literal: Some urged Xi not to distance himself; Xi said: "From my youth I have seen many men in high favor.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him not to stand apart; Xi said, "Since youth I have watched many favorites.

sentences.zh: 充詘少時，鮮不敗績。

translations.literal: Filled to satiety in their brief hour, few did not end in ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Sated for a moment, few escaped ruin.

sentences.zh: 且性實疏緩，不堪時務。

translations.literal: Moreover my nature is truly loose and slow; I cannot bear the affairs of the time.
translations.idiomatic: My nature is loose and slow; I cannot bear the times.

sentences.zh: 人主恩私，何由可保？

translations.literal: A ruler's private favor—how can it be kept?
translations.idiomatic: A ruler's private grace—how can it be kept?

sentences.zh: 萬一披猖，求追無地。

translations.literal: If by chance things turn wild, there will be nowhere to seek recall.
translations.idiomatic: If fortune turns, there is nowhere to flee.

sentences.zh: 非不愛作熱官，但思之爛熟耳。

translations.literal: It is not that I do not love a hot office; I have only thought it through to the core."
translations.idiomatic: I do not dislike a glittering post; I have only chewed the thought to the bone."

sentences.zh: 」百官嘗賜射，晞中的，當得絹，為不書箭，有司不與。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials were granted an archery contest, Xi hit the target and should have received silk, but because he did not mark his arrow the office would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: At an archery grant Xi hit the mark and should have won silk, but he did not mark his arrow and the office refused payment.

sentences.zh: 晞陶陶然曰：「我今段可謂武有餘文不足矣。

translations.literal: Xi said cheerfully: "This time I may be called strong in war and weak in letters."
translations.idiomatic: Xi laughed, "This time I may be called war-strong and letter-weak."

sentences.zh: 」晞無子，帝將賜之妾。

translations.literal: Xi had no son; the Emperor was about to give him a concubine.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had no son; the Emperor meant to give him a concubine.

sentences.zh: 使小黃門就宅宣旨，皇后相聞晞妻。

translations.literal: He sent a junior yellow gate to his house to proclaim the intent; the empress sent word to Xi's wife.
translations.idiomatic: A junior eunuch proclaimed the intent at his house; the empress sent word to his wife.

sentences.zh: 晞令妻答，妻終不言，晞以手撩胸而退。

translations.literal: Xi had his wife answer; his wife never spoke; Xi brushed his chest with his hand and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xi had his wife answer; she said nothing; Xi touched his chest and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之笑。

translations.literal: When the Emperor heard it he laughed.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed when he heard.

sentences.zh: 孝昭崩，晞哀慕殆不自勝，因以羸敗。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, Xi's grief was such that he nearly could not survive; because of this he fell into emaciation and decline.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhao died, Xi grieved until he nearly perished and wasted away.

sentences.zh: 武成本忿其儒緩，由是彌嫌之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his scholarly slowness and therefore disliked him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wucheng had long resented his bookish slowness and disliked him the more.

sentences.zh: 因奏事，大被訶叱，而雅步晏然。

translations.literal: When he reported on business he was greatly berated, yet he walked at ease with his elegant step.
translations.idiomatic: Reporting to court he was savagely scolded, yet walked at ease with his elegant step.

sentences.zh: 曆東徐州刺史、秘書監。

translations.literal: He served as Inspector of East Xuzhou and Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Inspector of East Xuzhou and Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武平初，遷大鴻臚，加儀同三司，監修起居注，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wuping he was moved to Grand Herald, with the added title Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes, supervised the drafting of the imperial diary, and attended at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wuping he became Grand Herald with honors equal to the Three Dukes, supervised the imperial diary, and attended at the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 性閑淡寡欲，雖王事鞅掌，而雅操不移。

translations.literal: His nature was leisurely and he desired little; though kingly business pressed thick, his refined conduct did not shift.
translations.idiomatic: He was leisurely and desired little; though royal business pressed thick, his refined conduct never shifted.

sentences.zh: 在并州，雖戎馬填閭，未嘗以世務為累。

translations.literal: In Bingzhou, though war-horses filled the lanes, he never took worldly affairs as a burden.
translations.idiomatic: In Bingzhou, though war-horses filled the lanes, he never let the world weigh on him.

sentences.zh: 良辰美景，嘯詠遨遊，登臨山水，以談宴為事，人士謂之「方外司馬。

translations.literal: On fine days and fair scenes he would chant and roam, climb hills and waters, and make talk and feasting his business; gentlemen called him "the Grand Administrator beyond the world."
translations.idiomatic: On fair days he chanted and roamed, climbed hills and streams, and made feasting his trade; men called him the Grand Administrator beyond the world.

sentences.zh: 」詣晉祠，賦詩曰：「日落應歸去，魚鳥見留連。

translations.literal: Visiting the Jin Shrine he composed a poem: "The sun sets—I should return; fish and birds seem to detain me."
translations.idiomatic: At the Jin Shrine he wrote, "The sun sets and I should go home; fish and birds seem to hold me back."

sentences.zh: 」忽有相王使召，晞不時至。

translations.literal: Suddenly a messenger of the King summoned him; Xi did not come at once.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the King's messenger called; Xi did not come at once.

sentences.zh: 明日，丞相西閣祭酒盧思道謂晞曰：「昨被召已硃顏，得無以魚鳥致怪？

translations.literal: The next day Lu Sidao, Libationer of the Chancellor's western pavilion, said to Xi: "Yesterday's summons already flushed your face—can fish and birds have brought blame?"
translations.idiomatic: Next day Lu Sidao said, "Yesterday's summons flushed you red—did fish and birds bring the blame?"

sentences.zh: 」晞緩笑曰：「昨晚陶然，頗以酒漿被責。

translations.literal: Xi smiled slowly: "Last night I was merry and was rather fined in wine.
translations.idiomatic: Xi smiled, "Last night I was merry and was fined in wine.

sentences.zh: 卿輩亦是留連之一物，豈直在魚鳥而已？

translations.literal: You fellows too are things that detain one—not only fish and birds."
translations.idiomatic: You too are things that detain—not only fish and birds."

sentences.zh: 」及晉陽陷敗，與同志避周兵東北走。

translations.literal: When Jinyang fell in defeat he fled northeast with like-minded men to escape Zhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Jinyang fell he fled northeast with friends to escape Zhou troops.

sentences.zh: 山路險迥，懼有土賊，而晞溫酒服膏，曾不一廢。

translations.literal: The mountain road was perilous and steep; they feared bandits, yet Xi warmed wine and took unguent and never once stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain road was steep and bandits feared, yet Xi warmed wine and took salve and never once stopped.

sentences.zh: 每不肯疾去，行侶尤之。

translations.literal: Each time he would not hurry away and his companions especially blamed him.
translations.idiomatic: He would not hurry and his companions blamed him.

sentences.zh: 晞曰：「莫尤我，我行事若不悔，久作三公矣。」

translations.literal: Xi said: "Do not blame me—if I acted without regret I would long since have been one of the Three Dukes."
translations.idiomatic: Xi said, "Blame me not—had I never regretted my way I would long since have been a Three Duke."

sentences.zh: 皓字季高，少立名行，為士友所稱。

translations.literal: Hao, styled Jigao, from youth established name and conduct and was praised by scholar-friends.
translations.idiomatic: Hao, styled Jigao, won name and conduct early and was praised by friends.

sentences.zh: 遭母憂，居喪有至性。

translations.literal: When his mother died he mourned with utmost filial feeling.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he mourned with utmost filial feeling.

sentences.zh: 儒緩亦同諸兄。

translations.literal: His scholarly slowness was the same as his elder brothers'.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarly slowness matched his brothers'.

sentences.zh: 嘗從文宣北征，乘赤馬，旦蒙霜氣，遂不復識。

translations.literal: Once he followed Emperor Wenxuan on a northern campaign, riding a red horse; at dawn it was covered with frost and he could no longer recognize it.
translations.idiomatic: Once on Emperor Wenxuan's northern campaign he rode a red horse; at dawn frost covered it and he did not know it.

sentences.zh: 自言失馬，虞候為求覓不得。

translations.literal: He said he had lost his horse; the camp guards searched but could not find it.
translations.idiomatic: He said his horse was lost; guards searched in vain.

sentences.zh: 須臾日出，馬體霜盡，系在幕前，方云：「我馬尚在。

translations.literal: In a moment the sun rose, the frost on the horse's body melted away, and it was tied before the tent; then he said: "My horse is still here."
translations.idiomatic: The sun rose, the frost melted, and the horse stood before the tent; he said, "My horse is still here."

sentences.zh: 」為司徒掾，在府聽午鼓，蹀躞待去。

translations.literal: As a clerk in the Secretariat he listened for the noon drum at court, pacing in small steps waiting to leave.
translations.idiomatic: As Secretariat clerk he listened for the noon drum, pacing small steps to leave.

sentences.zh: 群寮嘲之曰：「王七思歸何太疾？

translations.literal: The assembled clerks mocked him: "Wang the Seventh, why such haste to go home?"
translations.idiomatic: Clerks mocked him, "Wang the Seventh, why such haste home?"

sentences.zh: 」季高曰：「大鵬始欲舉，燕雀何啾唧？

translations.literal: Jigao said: "The great peng is just about to rise—why do swallows and sparrows chirp so?"
translations.idiomatic: Jigao said, "The great peng is about to rise—why do sparrows chirp?"

sentences.zh: 」嘲者曰：「誰家屋當頭，鋪首浪遊逸。

translations.literal: The mockers said: "Whose house is dead ahead—the door-boss roams in idle sport."
translations.idiomatic: The mockers said, "Whose house stands ahead—the door-knob roams in idle sport."

sentences.zh: 」於是喧笑，季高不復得言。

translations.literal: "At that there was loud laughter and Jigao could speak no more.
translations.idiomatic: At that they laughed aloud and Jigao could say no more.

sentences.zh: 大寧初，兼散騎常侍、聘陳使主。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daning he also served as Regular Attendant and chief envoy on the mission to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Daning he also served as Regular Attendant and chief envoy to Chen.

sentences.zh: 天統末，修國史。

translations.literal: At the end of Tiantong he revised the national history.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Tiantong he revised the national history.

sentences.zh: 尋除通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Unimpeded Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Unimpeded Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈郢州刺史。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 子伯，奉朝請，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: His son Bo held court appointment and attended at the Forest of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bo held court appointment and attended at the Forest of Literature.

sentences.zh: 皓弟曄，字季炎，卒于滄州司馬。

translations.literal: Hao's younger brother Ye, styled Jiyan, died as Administrator of Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hao's younger brother Ye, styled Jiyan, died as Administrator of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 封懿，字處德，勃海蓚人也。

translations.literal: Feng Yi, styled Chude, was a man of Mao in Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Yi, styled Chude, was from Mao in Bohai.

sentences.zh: 曾祖釋，晉東夷校尉。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Shi was Jin Colonel for the Eastern Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Shi was Jin Colonel for the Eastern Yi.

sentences.zh: 父放，慕容痈吏部尚書。

translations.literal: His father Fang was Minister of Personnel under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Fang was Minister of Personnel under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 兄孚，慕容超太尉。

translations.literal: His elder brother Fu was Grand Marshal under Murong Chao.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Fu was Grand Marshal under Murong Chao.

sentences.zh: 懿有才器，能屬文，與孚雖器行有長短，而名位略齊。

translations.literal: Yi had talent and capacity and could compose writing; though Fu and he differed in conduct and length of service, their fame and rank were roughly equal.
translations.idiomatic: Yi had talent and could write; Fu differed in conduct and tenure, yet their fame and rank were much the same.

sentences.zh: 仕慕容寶，位中書令、戶部尚書。

translations.literal: He served Murong Bao as Central Secretariat Director and Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: He served Murong Bao as Secretariat Director and Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 寶敗，歸魏，除給事黃門侍郎、都坐大官、章安子。

translations.literal: When Bao was defeated he returned to Wei and was made Gentlemen Attendant at the Yellow Gate, Grand Master for the Imperial Commissariat, and Viscount of Zhang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Bao fell he entered Wei as Gentlemen Attendant at the Yellow Gate, Grand Master of the Imperial Commissariat, and Viscount of Zhang'an.

sentences.zh: 道武引見，問以慕容舊事，懿應對疏慢，廢黜還家。

translations.literal: Emperor Daowu received him in audience and asked about old Yan affairs; Yi answered with negligence and was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Daowu asked about old Yan affairs; Yi answered with negligence, was dismissed, and sent home.

sentences.zh: 明元初，復徵拜都坐大官，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingyuan he was again summoned and appointed Grand Master for the Imperial Commissariat; his noble rank was raised to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Mingyuan he was summoned again as Grand Master of the Commissariat and raised to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 卒官。

translations.literal: He died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office.

sentences.zh: 懿撰《燕書》，頗行於世。

translations.literal: Yi compiled the "Book of Yan," which circulated quite widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Yi compiled the Book of Yan, which circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 子玄之，坐與司馬國璠、溫楷等謀亂，伏誅。

translations.literal: His son Xuanzhi was executed for plotting disorder with Sima Guofan, Wen Kai, and others.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanzhi was executed for plotting with Sima Guofan, Wen Kai, and others.

sentences.zh: 臨刑，明元謂曰：「終不令絕汝種也，將宥汝一子。

translations.literal: At execution Emperor Mingyuan said to him: "In the end I will not let your line be cut off; I shall spare one of your sons."
translations.idiomatic: At execution Emperor Mingyuan said, "I will not end your line; I spare one son."

sentences.zh: 」玄之以弟虔之子磨奴字君明早孤，乞全其命。

translations.literal: Xuanzhi, because his younger brother Qian's son Monu, styled Junming, had been orphaned early, begged to spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzhi begged life for his nephew Monu, styled Junming, Qian's orphaned son.

sentences.zh: 乃殺玄之四子，赦磨奴，刑為宦人。

translations.literal: They therefore killed Xuanzhi's four sons and pardoned Monu, who was punished by castration as a eunuch.
translations.idiomatic: They killed Xuanzhi's four sons, pardoned Monu, and castrated him as a eunuch.

sentences.zh: 崔浩之誅也，太武謂磨奴曰：「汝本應全，所以致刑者，由浩也。

translations.literal: At Cui Hao's execution Emperor Taiwu said to Monu: "You should have been spared entirely; the reason you suffered punishment was Hao."
translations.idiomatic: At Cui Hao's fall Emperor Taiwu told Monu, "You should have been spared; Hao brought your punishment."

sentences.zh: 」後為中曹監，使張掖，賜爵富城子。

translations.literal: Later he was Director of the Middle Palace Attendants, sent to Zhangye, and granted the noble rank Viscount of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Director of Palace Attendants, sent to Zhangye, and made Viscount of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 卒于懷州刺史，贈勃海公，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He died as Inspector of Huaizhou; posthumously he was made Duke of Bohai with the posthumous title Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He died Inspector of Huaizhou and was posthumously Duke of Bohai, posthumous title Ding.

sentences.zh: 以族子叔念為後。

translations.literal: A clansman's son Shunian was made his heir.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman's son Shunian was made his heir.

sentences.zh: 回字叔念，孝文賜名焉，慕容痈太尉奕之後也。

translations.literal: Hui, styled Shunian—Emperor Xiaowen granted the name—was a descendant of Murong Chui's Grand Marshal Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Hui, styled Shunian—a name granted by Emperor Xiaowen—descended from Murong Chui's Grand Marshal Yi.

sentences.zh: 父鑒。

translations.literal: His father Jian.
translations.idiomatic: His father was Jian.

sentences.zh: 初，磨奴既以回為後，請于獻文。

translations.literal: At first, after Monu had taken Hui as heir, he requested it of Emperor Xianwen.
translations.idiomatic: When Monu took Hui as heir he petitioned Emperor Xianwen.

sentences.zh: 贈鑒甯遠將軍、滄水太守。

translations.literal: Jian was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Cangshui.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was posthumously General Who Pacifies the Distance and Administrator of Cangshui.

sentences.zh: 回襲靡奴爵富城子。

translations.literal: Hui inherited Monu's noble rank as Viscount of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Hui inherited Monu's rank as Viscount of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 宣武時，累遷安州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was repeatedly promoted to Inspector of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he rose to Inspector of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 山人願朴，父子賓旅同寢一室。

translations.literal: The mountain man Yuan Pu, father and son, lodged together and slept in one room.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain man Yuan Pu, father and son, lodged and slept in one room.

sentences.zh: 回下車，勒令別處，其俗遂改。

translations.literal: When Hui took office he ordered them to lodge separately and the custom there changed.
translations.idiomatic: Hui on taking office ordered separate lodging and the custom changed.

sentences.zh: 明帝時，為瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming he was Inspector of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming he was Inspector of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時大乘寇亂之後，加以水潦，表求振恤，免其兵調，州內賴之。

translations.literal: At that time, after the disorders of the Mahayana sect and in addition floods, he memorialized asking relief and exemption from military levies; the province relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: After Mahayana rebellion and floods he sought relief and exemption from levies; the province relied on him.

sentences.zh: 曆度支、都官二尚書、冀州大中正。

translations.literal: He served as Minister of Revenue, Minister of Justice, and Grand Rectifier of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Minister of Revenue, Minister of Justice, and Grand Rectifier of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 滎陽鄭雲諂事長秋卿劉騰，貨紫纈四百匹，得為安州刺史。

translations.literal: Zheng Yun of Xingyang curried favor with the Director of the Long Autumn Office Liu Teng and with four hundred bolts of purple gauze bought the post of Inspector of Anzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yun of Xingyang fawned on Liu Teng of the Long Autumn Office and bought Inspector of Anzhou with four hundred bolts of purple gauze.

sentences.zh: 除書旦出，晚往詣回，坐未定，問回：「安州興生，何事為便？

translations.literal: The appointment letter came out in the morning; in the evening he went to call on Hui, and before he had sat down he asked Hui: "In Anzhou, what line of business is most profitable?"
translations.idiomatic: The appointment came at dawn; that evening he called on Hui and, before sitting, asked what business paid best in Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 」回曰：「卿荷國寵靈，位至方伯，雖不能拔園葵，去織婦，宜思方略以濟百姓，如何見造問興生乎？

translations.literal: Hui said: "You bear the state's favor and have reached a frontier post; though you cannot uproot the mallow in your garden or send away the weaving woman, you ought to think of plans to aid the people—why come on your first visit to ask about business?"
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "You bear the state's grace and hold a frontier post; though you cannot uproot your mallows or send away your weaver, you should aid the people—why on your first visit ask about profit?"

sentences.zh: 封回不為商賈，何以相示？

translations.literal: Feng Hui is no merchant—why show me this?"
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui is no merchant—why show me this?"

sentences.zh: 」雲慚失色。

translations.literal: Yun flushed and lost color.
translations.idiomatic: Yun flushed pale.

sentences.zh: 轉七兵尚書，領御史中尉，劾奏尚書右僕射元欽與從兄麗妻崔氏奸通，時人稱之。

translations.literal: Transferred to Minister of the Seven Armies while holding the post of Imperial Censor; he impeached the Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat Yuan Qin for adultery with his cousin Li's wife Cui; men of the time praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Made Minister of the Seven Armies and Imperial Censor; he impeached Vice Minister Yuan Qin for adultery with his cousin's wife Cui, and men praised him.

sentences.zh: 後為殿中尚書、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Later he was Minister in the Palace, Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Palace Minister and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

sentences.zh: 莊帝初，遇害河陰。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Zhuang's reign he was killed at Heyin.

sentences.zh: 贈司空公，諡曰孝宣。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Duke of the Ministry of Works with the posthumous title Xiaoxuan.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was Duke of Works, posthumous title Xiaoxuan.

sentences.zh: 長子隆之。

translations.literal: His eldest son was Longzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son was Longzhi.

sentences.zh: 隆之字祖裔，小名皮，寬和有度量。

translations.literal: Longzhi, styled Zuyi, childhood name Pi, was generous and had measure.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi, styled Zuyi, childhood name Pi, was generous and measured.

sentences.zh: 延昌中，道人法慶作亂冀州，自號大乘，眾五萬人。

translations.literal: In the Yanchang era the monk Faqing made disorder in Jizhou, styled himself Mahayana, and had fifty thousand followers.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanchang the monk Faqing rebelled in Jizhou, styled himself Mahayana, and gathered fifty thousand men.

sentences.zh: 隆之以開府中兵參軍與大都督元遙討之。

translations.literal: Longzhi as Colonel of Army Affairs in the Opening Office joined the Grand Commander Yuan Yao in suppressing him.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi as Opening Office colonel joined Grand Commander Yuan Yao to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 獲法慶，賜爵武城子。

translations.literal: Faqing was captured and Longzhi was granted the noble rank Viscount of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Faqing was taken and Longzhi made Viscount of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 累遷河內太守。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Administrator of Henei.

sentences.zh: 未到郡，屬爾硃兆入洛，莊帝幽崩，隆之以父遇害，常懷報雪，因持節東歸，圖為義舉。

translations.literal: Before he reached the commandery, Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; Emperor Zhuang was imprisoned and died; Longzhi, because his father had been killed, constantly harbored revenge and, holding the staff of office, went east to plot a righteous rising.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took the post Erzhu Zhao entered Luoyang; Emperor Zhuang died in prison; Longzhi, his father slain, held the staff and went east to plot revenge.

sentences.zh: 遂與高乾等夜襲冀州，克之，乃推為刺史。

translations.literal: He joined Gao Gan and others in a night attack on Jizhou, took it, and was thereupon pushed as Inspector.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Gao Gan in a night attack on Jizhou, took it, and was pushed as Inspector.

sentences.zh: 及齊神武自晉陽東出，隆之遣子子繪隨高乾奉迎於滏口。

translations.literal: When Qi Prince Shenwu marched east from Jinyang, Longzhi sent his son Zihui with Gao Gan to welcome him at Fukou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Shenwu marched east from Jinyang, Longzhi sent Zihui with Gao Gan to welcome him at Fukou.

sentences.zh: 中興初，拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhongxing he was made Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhongxing he was Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 韓陵之役，留隆之鎮鄴城。

translations.literal: At the battle of Hanling he remained to guard Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At Hanling he stayed to guard Ye.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徵為侍中，封安德郡公。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed as Duke of Ande Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and enfeoffed Duke of Ande.

sentences.zh: 于時朝議以爾硃榮宜配食明帝廟庭。

translations.literal: At that time court opinion held that Erzhu Rong should receive sacrifice in Emperor Ming's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: Court opinion then held Erzhu Rong should share sacrifice in Emperor Ming's temple.

sentences.zh: 隆之議曰：「榮為人臣，親行殺逆，豈有害人之母而與子對食之理？

translations.literal: Longzhi argued: "Rong was a subject who personally carried out murder and treason—how can there be reason for a man who harmed another's mother to share food with her son?"
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi argued, "Rong was a subject who murdered his lord—how can a man who killed a mother dine with her son?"

sentences.zh: 」以參議麟趾閣新制，又贈其妻祖氏范陽郡君。

translations.literal: Because he took part in deliberating the new regulations of the Unicorn Toe Office, his wife's clan the Zu were also enfeoffed as Lady of Fanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberating new regulations at the Unicorn Toe Office, he also enfeoffed his wife's clan Zu as Lady of Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 隆之表以先爵富城子及武城子轉授弟子孝琬等，朝廷嘉而從之。

translations.literal: Longzhi memorialized to transfer his former ranks as Viscount of Fucheng and Viscount of Wucheng to his nephews Xiaowan and others; the court approved and followed his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi memorialized to transfer his ranks Fucheng and Wucheng to nephews Xiaowan and others; the court approved.

sentences.zh: 後為斛斯椿等所構，逃歸鄉里，齊神武召赴晉陽。

translations.literal: Later he was framed by Huasi Chun and others, fled to his home village, and Prince Shenwu summoned him to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huasi Chun framed him; he fled home and Prince Shenwu summoned him to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 魏孝靜立，除吏部尚書，尋加侍中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaojing of Wei was established he was made Minister of Personnel and soon added Attendant-in-Ordinary.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaojing was established he was Minister of Personnel and soon Attendant-in-Ordinary.

sentences.zh: 元象初，除冀州刺史，加開府，累遷尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanxiang he was made Inspector of Jizhou with the Opening Office; he was repeatedly promoted to Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanxiang 1 he was Inspector of Jizhou with Opening Office rank and rose to Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 及北豫州刺史高仲密將叛，陰招冀州豪望為內應。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhongmi, Northern Prefect of Yuzhou, was about to rebel he secretly won the great families of Jizhou as inside allies.
translations.idiomatic: When Northern Yuzhou Prefect Gao Zhongmi was about to rebel he secretly won Jizhou magnates as allies within.

sentences.zh: 詔隆之馳驛慰撫，遂得安靜。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Longzhi to gallop on post-horses to comfort and soothe them, and the region was thereby quieted.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Longzhi on post-horses to soothe them and the region quieted.

sentences.zh: 隆之首參神武經略，奇謀皆密以啟聞，手書削槁，罕知於外。

translations.literal: Longzhi from the first took part in Prince Shenwu's strategy; every subtle plan he reported in secret; he cut drafts by hand and few outside knew.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi had shared Prince Shenwu's strategy from the start; subtle plans he reported in secret, cutting drafts by hand that few outside knew.

sentences.zh: 卒于齊州刺史，贈司徒。

translations.literal: He died as Inspector of Qizhou; posthumously he was made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died Inspector of Qizhou and was posthumously Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 神武以追榮未盡，復啟贈太保，諡宣懿。

translations.literal: Prince Shenwu, because posthumous honor was not yet complete, again petitioned to grant Grand Tutor with the posthumous title Xuanyi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Shenwu, finding honor incomplete, petitioned again for Grand Tutor, posthumous title Xuanyi.

sentences.zh: 神武后至冀州北境，次交津，追憶隆之，顧冀州行事司馬子如，言其德美，為之流涕。

translations.literal: When the Prince later reached the northern border of Jizhou and stopped at Jiaojin Ford he recalled Longzhi, turned to the acting prefect Sima Ziru, spoke of his virtue, and wept for him.
translations.idiomatic: Later at Jizhou's northern border, Jiaojin Ford, the Prince recalled Longzhi, told Sima Ziru of his virtue, and wept.

sentences.zh: 令乙太牢就祭。

translations.literal: He ordered a second grand sacrifice sent to offer sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a grand second sacrifice sent.

sentences.zh: 隆之曆事五帝，以謹素見知。

translations.literal: Longzhi served five emperors and was known for cautious plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi served five emperors and was known for plain caution.

sentences.zh: 凡四為侍中，再為吏部尚書，一為僕射，四為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In all he was Attendant-in-Ordinary four times, Minister of Personnel twice, Vice Minister once, and Inspector of Jizhou four times.
translations.idiomatic: Four times Attendant-in-Ordinary, twice Minister of Personnel, once Vice Minister, four times Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 每臨冀部，州中舊齒咸曰：「我封公復來。

translations.literal: Each time he came to Jizhou the old men of the province all said: "Our Lord Feng has come again."
translations.idiomatic: Each arrival in Jizhou the old men said, "Our Lord Feng has come again."

sentences.zh: 」其得物情如此。

translations.literal: Such was the hold he had on men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the hold he had on hearts.

sentences.zh: 子子繪嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zihui inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zihui inherited.

sentences.zh: 子繪字仲藻，小名搔。

translations.literal: Zihui, styled Zhongzao, childhood name Sao.
translations.idiomatic: Zihui, styled Zhongzao, childhood name Sao.

sentences.zh: 性和理，有器局。

translations.literal: His nature was harmonious and principled and he had capacity and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: He was harmonious, principled, and had capacity.

sentences.zh: 釋褐秘書郎，累遷平陽太守，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Leaving the purple he was Secretariat Clerk and was repeatedly promoted to Administrator of Pingyang with the added title Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Secretariat Clerk, rose to Administrator of Pingyang with Regular Attendant rank.

sentences.zh: 晉州北界霍山舊號千里徑者，山阪高峻，每大軍往來，士馬勞苦。

translations.literal: On Jinzhou's northern border Mount Huo was oldly called the Thousand-Li Path; the mountain slopes were high and steep and whenever a great army passed, men and horses were worn with labor.
translations.idiomatic: On Jinzhou's north Mount Huo was called the Thousand-Li Path; slopes were steep and every great army wore men and horses down.

sentences.zh: 子繪請於舊徑東穀別開一路。

translations.literal: Zihui asked to open a separate road east of the valley of the old path.
translations.idiomatic: Zihui asked to open a new road east of the old valley path.

sentences.zh: 神武從之，仍令子繪修開，旬日而就。

translations.literal: The Prince agreed and still ordered Zihui to open and repair it; in ten days it was done.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince agreed and ordered Zihui to open it; in ten days it was done.

sentences.zh: 征補大行台吏部郎中。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Director in the Ministry of Personnel of the Great Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Director in the Great Office Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 神武崩，秘未發喪，文襄以子繪為勃海太守。

translations.literal: When the Prince died the secret was not yet announced; Wenxiang made Zihui Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince died the death was not yet announced; Wenxiang made Zihui Administrator of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 執其手曰：「誠知未允勳臣官望，但須鎮撫。

translations.literal: He grasped his hand and said: "I truly know this does not match a meritorious minister's standing, but you must pacify and soothe.
translations.idiomatic: He took his hand and said, "I know this does not match your merit, but you must pacify the land.

sentences.zh: 且衣錦晝游，古人所貴，宜善加經略，不勞習常太守向州參也。

translations.literal: Moreover to clothe brocade and roam by day is what ancients prized; you should govern well and need not practice like an ordinary prefect going to the province for audience."
translations.idiomatic: To clothe brocade and roam by day ancients prized; govern well and need not act like a common prefect at provincial audience."

sentences.zh: 」仍聽收集部曲一千人。

translations.literal: He was still permitted to gather a thousand men of his household troops.
translations.idiomatic: He was still allowed to gather a thousand household troops.

sentences.zh: 大寧三年，為都官尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daning he was Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Daning 3 he was Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 高歸彥作逆，命子繪參贊軍事。

translations.literal: When Gao Guiyan rebelled he was ordered to take part in planning the military affair.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Guiyan rebelled he was ordered to plan the campaign.

sentences.zh: 賊平，敕子繪權行州事。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified he was ordered to act temporarily in provincial affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels were pacified he was ordered to act in provincial affairs.

sentences.zh: 徵拜儀同三司、尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Equal in Honor to the Three Dukes and Right Vice Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned Equal to the Three Dukes and Right Vice Minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: When he died his posthumous title was Jian.
translations.idiomatic: At death his posthumous title was Jian.

sentences.zh: 子寶蓋襲。

translations.literal: His son Baogai inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Baogai inherited.

sentences.zh: 子繪弟子繡，位霍州刺史。

translations.literal: Zihui's nephew Xiu held the post of Inspector of Huozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zihui's nephew Xiu was Inspector of Huozhou.

sentences.zh: 陳將吳明徹侵淮南，子繡城陷，送揚州。

translations.literal: When the Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Huainan, Xiu's city fell and he was sent to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen general Wu Mingche invaded Huainan, Xiu's city fell and he was sent to Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 齊亡後，逃歸。

translations.literal: After Qi perished he escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi's fall he escaped home.

sentences.zh: 終於通州刺史。

translations.literal: He ended as Inspector of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as Inspector of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 子繡外貌儒雅，而使氣難犯。

translations.literal: Xiu's outward appearance was refined and Confucian, yet his spirit was hard to offend.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu looked refined and Confucian, yet his spirit was hard to offend.

sentences.zh: 兄女婿司空婁定遠為瀛州刺史，子繡為勃海太守。

translations.literal: His elder sister's husband, Minister of Works Lou Dingyuan, was Inspector of Yingzhou; Xiu was Administrator of Bohai.
translations.idiomatic: His sister's husband, Minister Lou Dingyuan, was Inspector of Yingzhou; Xiu was Administrator of Bohai.

sentences.zh: 定遠過之，對妻及諸女宴集言戲，微有褻慢。

translations.literal: Dingyuan called on him and, facing his wife and daughters at a gathering, spoke in jest with slight impropriety.
translations.idiomatic: Dingyuan called and, feasting with his wife and daughters, jested with slight impropriety.

sentences.zh: 子繡鳴鼓集眾將攻之，定遠免冠拜謝，久之乃釋。

translations.literal: Xiu beat the drum, gathered the crowd, and was about to attack him; Dingyuan doffed his cap and bowed in apology and only after long time was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu beat the drum, gathered men to attack; Dingyuan doffed his cap and bowed long before he was released.

sentences.zh: 隆之弟興之，字祖胄。

translations.literal: Longzhi's younger brother Xingzhi, styled Zuyu.
translations.idiomatic: Longzhi's younger brother Xingzhi, styled Zuyu.

sentences.zh: 經明行修，恬素清靜。

translations.literal: He was versed in the classics and cultivated in conduct, plain and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: He was versed in classics and conduct, plain and quiet.

sentences.zh: 位瀛冀二州刺史、平北府長史。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Inspector of Ying and Ji and Chief Steward of the Pacify-the-North Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was Inspector of Ying and Ji and Chief Steward of the Pacify-the-North Office.

sentences.zh: 所曆有當官譽。

translations.literal: In every post he held he had the reputation of a proper official.
translations.idiomatic: Every post won him repute as a proper official.

sentences.zh: 卒，以隆之佐命功，贈殿中尚書、雍州刺史，諡曰文。

translations.literal: When he died, because of Longzhi's merit in aiding the founding, he was posthumously made Minister in the Palace and Inspector of Yongzhou with the posthumous title Wen.
translations.idiomatic: At death, for Longzhi's founding merit, he was posthumously Palace Minister and Inspector of Yongzhou, posthumous title Wen.

sentences.zh: 子孝琬，字士茜。

translations.literal: His son Xiaowan, styled Shiqian.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaowan, styled Shiqian.

sentences.zh: 七歲而孤，為隆之鞠養；

translations.literal: Orphaned at seven, he was reared by Longzhi;
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned at seven, Longzhi reared him;

sentences.zh: 慈愛甚篤，隆之啟以父爵富城子授焉。

translations.literal: his love was very deep, and Longzhi petitioned to grant him his father's noble rank as Viscount of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: his love was deep, and Longzhi petitioned to grant his father's rank Viscount of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 位東宮洗馬。

translations.literal: He held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: He was Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太府少卿。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Vice Minister of the Grand Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Vice Minister of the Grand Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 孝琬性恬靜，頗好文詠。

translations.literal: Xiaowan's nature was tranquil and he quite loved literary composition.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaowan was tranquil and loved literary composition.

sentences.zh: 太子少師邢邵、七兵尚書王昕並先達高才，與孝琬年位懸隔，晚相逢遇，分好遂深。

translations.literal: Xing Shao, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and Wang Xin, Minister of the Seven Armies, were both advanced men of high talent; with Xiaowan the gap in years and rank was wide, yet meeting late they became deeply fond.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shao and Wang Xin, both eminent talents, met Xiaowan late in life despite wide gaps in age and rank, and friendship grew deep.

sentences.zh: 孝琬靈櫬言歸，二人送於郊外，悲哭淒慟，有感路人。

translations.literal: When Xiaowan's coffin was to return home the two escorted him to the suburbs, weeping bitterly with grief that moved passers-by.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaowan's coffin went home both escorted him to the suburbs, weeping so bitterly passers-by were moved.

sentences.zh: 孝琬弟孝琰，字士光，少修飭，學尚有風儀。

translations.literal: Xiaowan's younger brother Xiaoyan, styled Shiguang, from youth cultivated himself; in learning he had bearing and elegance.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Xiaoyan, styled Shiguang, cultivated himself from youth; in learning he had elegant bearing.

sentences.zh: 位秘書丞、散騎常侍、聘陳使主，在道遙授中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Secretariat Assistant, Regular Attendant, and chief envoy on the mission to Chen; on the road he was remotely appointed Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was Secretariat Assistant, Regular Attendant, and chief envoy to Chen; on the road he was remotely made Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 還，坐受魏收囑，牒其門客從行事發，付南都獄，決鞭二百，除名。

translations.literal: On return he was punished for accepting Wei Shou's commission and issuing a warrant against his retainers' conduct on the journey; he was handed to the Southern Capital prison, sentenced to two hundred strokes of the whip, and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was punished for taking Wei Shou's commission and issuing warrants against his retainers; the Southern Capital prison gave him two hundred lashes and struck his name away.

sentences.zh: 後除並省吏部郎中、南陽王友，赴晉陽典機密。

translations.literal: Later he was made Director in the Joint Secretariat Ministry of Personnel and Friend to the Prince of Nanyang and went to Jinyang to handle secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was Joint Secretariat personnel director and Friend to the Prince of Nanyang and went to Jinyang for secret affairs.

sentences.zh: 和士開母喪，托附者咸往奔哭。

translations.literal: At He Shikai's mother's mourning all who had attached themselves went to wail.
translations.idiomatic: At He Shikai's mother's mourning all hangers-on went to wail.

sentences.zh: 鄴中富商丁鄒、嚴興等並為義孝，有一士人亦在哭限。

translations.literal: The wealthy merchants Ding Zou and Yan Xing of Ye all performed filial mourning; one scholar too was within the mourners.
translations.idiomatic: Ye merchants Ding Zou and Yan Xing all played filial mourners; one scholar too wailed among them.

sentences.zh: 孝琰入吊，出謂人曰：「嚴興之南，丁鄒之北，有一朝士，號叫甚哀。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan entered to condole and, coming out, said to others: "South of Yan Xing and north of Ding Zou there is one court gentleman wailing exceedingly bitterly."
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan condoled and, coming out, said, "South of Yan Xing, north of Ding Zou, one court gentleman wails exceedingly bitter."

sentences.zh: 」聞者傳之。

translations.literal: Those who heard passed it on.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing men passed it on.

sentences.zh: 士開知而大怒。

translations.literal: Shikai learned of it and was greatly enraged.
translations.idiomatic: Shikai learned and was greatly enraged.

sentences.zh: 其後會黃門郎李瑰奏南陽王綽驕恣，士開因譖之曰：「孝琰從綽出外，乘其副馬，舍離部伍，別行戲語。

translations.literal: Later, when Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Gui reported that the Prince of Nanyang Chuo was arrogant and willful, Shikai therefore slandered him saying: "Xiaoyan followed Chuo outside, rode his spare horse, left the unit's ranks, and went apart in playful talk."
translations.idiomatic: Later Yellow Gate Gentleman Li Gui reported Prince Chuo of Nanyang arrogant; Shikai slandered Xiaoyan for riding Chuo's spare horse, leaving ranks, and jesting apart.

sentences.zh: 」時孝琰女為范陽王妃，為禮事，因假入辭。

translations.literal: At that time Xiaoyan's daughter was consort to the Prince of Fanyang; for ritual reasons she therefore took leave to enter audience.
translations.idiomatic: Then Xiaoyan's daughter was consort to the Prince of Fanyang; for ritual she took leave to enter audience.

sentences.zh: 帝遂決馬鞭一百放出，又遣高阿那肱重決五十，幾死。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon had him beaten one hundred strokes with the horse whip and expelled; he also sent Gao Anagong to beat him again fifty strokes and he nearly died.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor had him horse-whipped one hundred strokes and expelled, and sent Gao Anagong for fifty more—he nearly died.

sentences.zh: 還鄴，在集書省上下。

translations.literal: Returning to Ye he went up and down in the Bureau for Collecting Writings.
translations.idiomatic: Back in Ye he kept to the Collecting Writings Bureau.

sentences.zh: 自此沈廢。

translations.literal: From this he sank into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: From this he sank into disuse.

sentences.zh: 士開死後，為通直散騎常侍。

translations.literal: After Shikai died he was made Unimpeded Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Shikai died he was Unimpeded Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後與周和好，以為聘周使副。

translations.literal: Later, when peace was made with Zhou, he was made deputy chief envoy on the mission to Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at peace with Zhou, he was deputy chief envoy to Zhou.

sentences.zh: 祖珽輔政，奏入文林館撰御覽。

translations.literal: When Zu Ting aided government he memorialized his entry into the Forest of Literature to compile the imperial overview.
translations.idiomatic: When Zu Ting aided government he entered the Forest of Literature to compile the imperial overview.

sentences.zh: 孝琰文筆不高，但以風流自立，善談戲，威儀閒雅，容止進退，人皆慕之。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan's literary brush was not high, but he stood on elegant bearing, was skilled in witty talk, and his majesty was leisurely and refined; in bearing and in advance and retreat all men admired him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan's brush was not high, yet he stood on elegant bearing, witty talk, leisurely majesty, and men admired his advance and retreat.

sentences.zh: 以祖珽好自矜大，佞之云：「是衣冠宰相，異于餘人。

translations.literal: Because Zu Ting liked to boast himself, he flattered him saying: "This is a minister in cap and gown, different from the rest."
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ting boasted; Xiaoyan flattered him, "This is a minister in cap and gown, unlike the rest."

sentences.zh: 」近習聞之，大以為恨。

translations.literal: Those close to the throne heard it and greatly resented it.
translations.idiomatic: Court intimates heard and greatly resented it.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼尚書右丞。

translations.literal: Soon with his original office he also held the concurrent post of Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he also held Right Assistant Minister with his original office.

sentences.zh: 其所彈射，多承意旨。

translations.literal: In his impeachments he mostly followed the ruler's intent.
translations.idiomatic: His impeachments mostly followed the ruler's intent.

sentences.zh: 時有道人曇獻者，為皇太后所幸，賞賜隆厚，車服過度。

translations.literal: At that time the monk Tanxian was favored by the Empress Dowager; rewards were thick and his carriage and dress exceeded measure.
translations.idiomatic: The monk Tanxian was favored by the Empress Dowager; rewards were thick and dress exceeded measure.

sentences.zh: 又乞為沙門統，後主意不許，但太后欲之，遂得居任。

translations.literal: He also begged to be Patriarch over the Buddhist clergy; the later ruler's heart did not consent, but the Empress Dowager wished it and he therefore obtained the post.
translations.idiomatic: He begged to be Patriarch over clergy; the later ruler refused but the Empress Dowager wished it and he obtained the post.

sentences.zh: 然後主常憾焉。

translations.literal: Yet the later ruler often resented this.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the later ruler often resented it.

sentences.zh: 因僧尼他事，訴者辭引曇獻，上令有司推劾。

translations.literal: Because of another matter involving monks and nuns, a plaintiff's words implicated Tanxian; the ruler ordered the relevant office to investigate and impeach.
translations.idiomatic: In another monks-and-nuns case a plaintiff implicated Tanxian; the ruler ordered investigation.

sentences.zh: 孝琰案其受賄，致於極法，其家珍異悉以沒官。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan tried his case for taking bribes and brought him to extreme punishment; the rare treasures of his house were all confiscated for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan tried his bribes and brought extreme punishment; rare treasures were confiscated.

sentences.zh: 由是正授左丞，仍奏門下事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was formally appointed Left Assistant Minister and still reported on Gate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he was formally Left Assistant Minister and still reported Gate affairs.

sentences.zh: 性頗簡傲，不諧時俗，意遇漸高，彌自矜誕，舉動舒遲，無所降屈，識者鄙之。

translations.literal: His nature was quite haughty and he did not harmonize with the customs of the time; as favor rose higher he was all the more self-conceited; his movements were slow and he bowed to none—men of insight despised him.
translations.idiomatic: He was haughty, ill-fit to custom, and as favor rose grew conceited; movements slow, bowing to none—men of insight despised him.

sentences.zh: 與崔季舒等以正諫同死。

translations.literal: He died with Cui Jishu and others for upright remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: He died with Cui Jishu and others for upright remonstrance.

sentences.zh: 子君確、君靜二人徙北邊，少子君嚴、君贊下蠶室。

translations.literal: His sons Junque and Junjing were both moved to the northern border; the younger sons Junyan and Junzan were sent to the silkworm chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Junque and Junjing were moved north; younger sons Junyan and Junzan to the silkworm chamber.

sentences.zh: 南安敗，君確等二人皆坐死。

translations.literal: When Nan'an was defeated Junque and the two others were both punished with death.
translations.idiomatic: When Nan'an fell Junque and the two others were executed.

sentences.zh: 興之弟延之，字祖業，少明辯，有世用。

translations.literal: Xingzhi's younger brother Yanzhi, styled Zuye, from youth was clear in debate and had worldly usefulness.
translations.idiomatic: Xingzhi's younger brother Yanzhi, styled Zuye, was clear in debate and useful in the world.

sentences.zh: 封郯城子，位青州刺史，多所受納。

translations.literal: Enfeoffed as Viscount of Tan, he was Inspector of Qingzhou and took many bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Enfeoffed Viscount of Tan, he was Inspector of Qingzhou and took many bribes.

sentences.zh: 後行晉州事。

translations.literal: Later he acted in Jinzhou affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later he acted in Jinzhou affairs.

sentences.zh: 沙苑之敗，延之棄州北走，以隆之故，免其死。

translations.literal: At the defeat at Shawei Yanzhi abandoned the province and fled north; because of Longzhi's relation he was spared death.
translations.idiomatic: At Shawei's defeat Yanzhi abandoned the province and fled north; Longzhi's name spared his life.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左僕射、司徒公，諡文恭。

translations.literal: When he died he was posthumously made Left Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Duke of the Ministry of Works with the posthumous title Wengong.
translations.idiomatic: At death he was posthumously Left Vice Minister and Duke of Works, posthumous title Wengong.

sentences.zh: 子纂嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zuan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zuan inherited.

sentences.zh: 鑒長子琳，字彥寶，位中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Jian's eldest son Lin, styled Yanbao, held the post of Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's eldest son Lin, styled Yanbao, was Vice Director of the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與侍中、南平王馮誕等議定律令，有識者稱之。

translations.literal: With Attendant-in-Ordinary and Prince of Nanping Feng Yan and others he deliberated on fixing the laws and orders; men of discernment praised it.
translations.idiomatic: With Attendant Feng Yan of Nanping and others he fixed laws and orders; discerning men praised it.

sentences.zh: 歷位太尉長史、司宗下大夫、南夏青二州刺史、光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He served as Chief Steward to the Grand Marshal, Junior Minister under the Minister of the Masses, Inspector of Nanxia and Qing, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: He was Chief Steward to the Grand Marshal, Junior Minister under the Minister of the Masses, Inspector of Nanxia and Qing, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue.

sentences.zh: 琳弟子肅。

translations.literal: Lin's younger brother's son Su.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's younger brother's son was Su.

sentences.zh: 肅字元邕，博涉經史。

translations.literal: Su, styled Yuanyong, was broadly versed in the classics and histories.
translations.idiomatic: Su, styled Yuanyong, was broadly versed in classics and histories.

sentences.zh: 太傅崔光見而賞焉。

translations.literal: Grand Tutor Cui Guang saw him and prized him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Cui Guang saw and prized him.

sentences.zh: 位尚書左中兵郎中。

translations.literal: He held the post of Director in the Left Section for Army Affairs of the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: He was Director in the Left Section for Army Affairs.

sentences.zh: 性恭儉，不妄交遊，唯與崔勵、勵從兄鴻尤相親善。

translations.literal: His nature was respectful and frugal; he did not make friends rashly—only with Cui Li and Li's cousin Hong was he especially close.
translations.idiomatic: He was respectful and frugal, friendless save Cui Li and Li's cousin Hong.

sentences.zh: 所制文章多亡失，存者十餘卷。

translations.literal: Most of the writings he composed are lost; a little more than ten scrolls remain.
translations.idiomatic: Most writings are lost; a little over ten scrolls remain.

sentences.zh: 懿從兄子愷，字思悌，奕之孫也。

translations.literal: Yi's cousin's son Kai, styled Siti, was Yi's grandson.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's cousin's son Kai, styled Siti, was Yi's grandson.

sentences.zh: 父勸，慕容垂侍中、太常卿。

translations.literal: His father Quan was Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Minister of Ceremonies under Murong Chui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Quan was Attendant-in-Ordinary and Grand Minister of Ceremonies under Murong Chui.

sentences.zh: 愷位給事黃門侍郎、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: Kai held the posts of Gentlemen Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Kai was Gentlemen Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 後入代都，名出懿子玄之右。

translations.literal: Later he entered the capital of Dai; his fame stood above Yi's son Xuanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Later he entered the Dai capital; his fame stood above Xuanzhi.

sentences.zh: 俱坐司馬氏事死。

translations.literal: Both were executed for the Sima affair.
translations.idiomatic: Both were executed for the Sima affair.

sentences.zh: 愷妻，盧玄女也。

translations.literal: Kai's wife was the daughter of Lu Xuan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's wife was Lu Xuan's daughter.

sentences.zh: 愷子伯達，棄母及妻李氏南奔河表，改婚房氏。

translations.literal: Kai's son Boda abandoned his mother and wife Lady Li and fled south of the river, changing marriage to the Fang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Kai's son Boda abandoned mother and wife Lady Li, fled south of the river, and remarried into the Fang clan.

sentences.zh: 獻文末，伯達子休傑內入。

translations.literal: At the end of Emperor Xianwen's reign Boda's son Xiujie entered within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xianwen Xiujie entered within the passes.

sentences.zh: 祖母盧猶存，垂百歲矣。

translations.literal: Grandmother Lu was still alive, nearly a hundred years old.
translations.idiomatic: Grandmother Lu still lived, nearly a hundred.

sentences.zh: 而李已死。

translations.literal: Yet Lady Li had already died.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Li was already dead.

sentences.zh: 休傑位冀州咸陽王府諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Xiujie held the post of Adviser to the Prince of Xianyang of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xiujie was Adviser to the Prince of Xianyang of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 回族叔軌，字廣度。

translations.literal: Returning to the clan, uncle Gui, styled Guangdu.
translations.idiomatic: Of the clan, uncle Gui, styled Guangdu.

sentences.zh: 好學，通覽經傳。

translations.literal: He loved learning and thoroughly mastered the classics and their traditions.
translations.idiomatic: He loved learning and mastered classics and traditions.

sentences.zh: 與光祿大夫武邑孫惠蔚同志友善。

translations.literal: With Grand Master of Splendid Virtue Sun Huiwei of Wuyi he shared purpose and were friendly.
translations.idiomatic: With Grand Master Sun Huiwei of Wuyi he shared purpose and friendship.

sentences.zh: 惠蔚每推軌曰：「封生之於經義，吾所弗如者多矣。

translations.literal: Huiwei often pushed Gui saying: "In classical meaning Feng Sheng surpasses me in more matters than I can count."
translations.idiomatic: Huiwei often said, "In classical meaning Feng Sheng surpasses me in more than I can count."

sentences.zh: 」頗自修潔，儀容甚偉。

translations.literal: He quite cultivated himself in purity; his bearing was very grand.
translations.idiomatic: He cultivated purity; his bearing was grand.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「學士不事修飾，此賢何獨如此？

translations.literal: Some said: "Scholars do not trouble with adornment—why is this worthy alone thus?"
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "Scholars do not dress up—why is this worthy alone so?"

sentences.zh: 」軌聞，笑曰：「君子整其衣冠，尊其瞻視，何必蓬頭垢面而後為賢。

translations.literal: Gui heard it and laughed: "The gentleman sets his cap and robes in order and honors what men see—why must one be unkempt and filthy before he is worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: Gui laughed, "The gentleman orders cap and robes and honors what men see—must one be filthy to be worthy?"

sentences.zh: 」言者慚退。

translations.literal: The speaker flushed and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The speaker flushed and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 以兼員外散騎常侍銜命高麗。

translations.literal: As Concurrent Regular Attendant he bore credentials to Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: As Concurrent Regular Attendant he bore credentials to Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 高麗王雲恃其偏遠，稱疾不親受詔。

translations.literal: King Yun of Goguryeo relied on his remote distance and claimed illness and would not personally receive the edict in audience.
translations.idiomatic: King Yun relied on distance, claimed illness, and would not receive the edict in person.

sentences.zh: 軌正色詰之，喻以大義，雲乃北面受旨。

translations.literal: Gui sternly questioned him and instructed him in the great meaning; Yun then turned north and received the decree.
translations.idiomatic: Gui sternly questioned him and taught the great meaning; Yun turned north and received the decree.

sentences.zh: 使還，轉考功郎中，除本郡中正。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he was transferred to Director in the Ministry for Evaluating Merit and made Rectifier of his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was Director for Evaluating Merit and Rectifier of his commandery.

sentences.zh: 勃海太守崔休入為吏部郎中，以兄考事幹軌。

translations.literal: Cui Xiu of Bohai entered office as Director in the Ministry of Personnel; because of his elder brother he handled Gui's evaluation.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Xiu of Bohai became personnel director and, for his elder brother, handled Gui's evaluation.

sentences.zh: 軌曰：「法者天下之事，不可以舊君故，虧之也。

translations.literal: Gui said: "Law is the business of the realm—it cannot be bent because of an old patron."
translations.idiomatic: Gui said, "Law is the realm's business—it cannot bend for an old patron."

sentences.zh: 」休歎其守正。

translations.literal: Xiu sighed at his upholding what was right.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu sighed at his rectitude.

sentences.zh: 軌在台中，稱為儒雅。

translations.literal: In the central offices Gui was called refined and Confucian.
translations.idiomatic: In central offices Gui was called refined and Confucian.

sentences.zh: 除國子博士，假通直散騎常侍，慰勞汾州山胡。

translations.literal: He was made Erudite of the National University, acting Unimpeded Regular Attendant, and sent to comfort the mountain Hu of Fenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was National University Erudite, acting Unimpeded Regular Attendant, comforting Fenzhou mountain Hu.

sentences.zh: 司空、清河王懌表修明堂、辟雍，詔百寮集議。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qinghe, Minister of Works, Yi, memorialized to repair the Bright Hall and the Imperial Academy; an edict ordered the hundred offices to assemble in deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Qinghe, Minister of Works, memorialized to repair Bright Hall and Imperial Academy; the hundred offices were ordered to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 軌議曰：

translations.literal: Gui argued:
translations.idiomatic: Gui argued:

sentences.zh: 《周官匠人》職云：夏後氏世室，殷人重屋，周人明堂，五室，九階，四戶，八窗。

translations.literal: The "Artificer" office in the Offices of Zhou says: the Hall of the Xia had the World Room, the Yin the Double Roof, the Zhou the Bright Hall—five chambers, nine steps, four doors, eight windows.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou Offices Artificer says: Xia's World Room, Yin's Double Roof, Zhou's Bright Hall—five chambers, nine steps, four doors, eight windows.

sentences.zh: 鄭玄曰：「或舉宗廟，或舉王寢，或舉明堂，互文以見同制。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan says: "Sometimes ancestral temple is named, sometimes royal sleeping quarters, sometimes Bright Hall—interlocking words to show one system."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan says, "Sometimes temple, sometimes royal chambers, sometimes Bright Hall—interlocking words for one system."

sentences.zh: 」然則三代明堂，其制一也。

translations.literal: Thus the Bright Halls of the Three Dynasties were one in system.
translations.idiomatic: Thus the Three Dynasties' Bright Halls shared one system.

sentences.zh: 案周與夏、殷，損益不同。

translations.literal: Considering Zhou with Xia and Yin, additions and subtractions differ.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou against Xia and Yin differs in additions and subtractions.

sentences.zh: 至於明堂，因而弗革，明五室之義，得天數矣。

translations.literal: As for the Bright Hall, they followed without change; clearly the meaning of five chambers obtained Heaven's number.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Bright Hall they followed unchanged—five chambers obtain Heaven's number.

sentences.zh: 是以鄭玄又曰：「五室者，象五行也。

translations.literal: Therefore Zheng Xuan also says: "Five chambers image the Five Phases."
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan also says, "Five chambers image the Five Phases."

sentences.zh: 」然則九階者法九土，四戶者達四時，八窗者通八風，誠不易之大范，有國之恆式。

translations.literal: Then nine steps image the Nine Regions; four doors reach the four seasons; eight windows penetrate the eight winds—truly an unchanging great model and the constant pattern of a state.
translations.idiomatic: Nine steps image the Nine Regions; four doors the four seasons; eight windows the eight winds—an unchanging great model and a state's constant pattern.

sentences.zh: 若其上圓下方以則天地，通水環宮以節觀者，茅蓋白盛為之質飾，赤綴白綴為之戶牖，皆典籍所載，制度之明義也。

translations.literal: If above round and below square to model Heaven and Earth, a water channel encircling the palace to regulate viewers, thatched cover and white hangings for substance and ornament, red tassels and white tassels for doors and windows—all are what the classics record and the clear meaning of institution.
translations.idiomatic: Round above, square below to model Heaven and Earth; water channel encircling the palace; thatched cover and white hangings; red and white tassels for doors and windows—all are what classics record and institution's clear meaning.

sentences.zh: 秦焚滅五典，非毀三代，變更先聖，不依舊憲。

translations.literal: Qin burned and extinguished the Five Canons, destroyed and overthrew the Three Dynasties, changed the former sages, and did not follow the old statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Qin burned the Five Canons, overthrew the Three Dynasties, changed the former sages, and abandoned old statutes.

sentences.zh: 故《呂氏月令》見九室之義，大戴之《禮》著十二堂之文。

translations.literal: Therefore the "Monthly Ordinances" of Master Lü shows the meaning of nine chambers; the "Rites" of Dai the Great sets forth the text of twelve halls.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Master Lü's Monthly Ordinances show nine chambers; Dai the Great's Rites set forth twelve halls.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦法，亦未能改，東西二京，俱為九室。

translations.literal: Han inherited Qin's law and likewise could not change it; the two capitals east and west were both nine chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Han inherited Qin law and could not change; both eastern and western capitals had nine chambers.

sentences.zh: 是以《黃圖》、《白武通》、蔡邕、應劭等咸稱九室以象九州，十二堂以象十二辰。

translations.literal: Thus the "Yellow Chart," "Comprehensive Meaning," Cai Yong, Ying Shao, and others all said nine chambers image the Nine Provinces and twelve halls image the twelve chronograms.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yellow Chart, Comprehensive Meaning, Cai Yong, Ying Shao, and others said nine chambers image the Nine Provinces and twelve halls the twelve chronograms.

sentences.zh: 夫室以祭天，堂以布政。

translations.literal: Chambers are for sacrificing to Heaven; halls are for spreading government.
translations.idiomatic: Chambers sacrifice to Heaven; halls spread government.

sentences.zh: 依行而祭，故室不過五；

translations.literal: According to conduct one sacrifices; therefore chambers do not exceed five;
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifice follows conduct; chambers do not exceed five;

sentences.zh: 依時布政，故堂不逾四。

translations.literal: according to seasons one spreads government; therefore halls do not exceed four.
translations.idiomatic: government follows seasons; halls do not exceed four.

sentences.zh: 州之與辰，非所可法。

translations.literal: Provinces and chronograms are not what may be taken as models.
translations.idiomatic: Provinces and chronograms are not models to follow.

sentences.zh: 九與十二，厥用安在？

translations.literal: What use have nine and twelve?
translations.idiomatic: What use are nine and twelve?

sentences.zh: 今聖朝欲尊道訓人，備禮化物，宜則五室，以為永制。

translations.literal: Now the sacred court wishes to honor the Way, instruct men, complete rites, and transform by rites—it should take five chambers as the everlasting institution.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sacred court wishes to honor the Way, instruct men, complete rites, and transform—all should take five chambers as everlasting institution.

sentences.zh: 至如廟學之嫌，台沼之雜，袁准之徒已論正矣。

translations.literal: As for the tangle of temple and school, the miscellany of terrace and pool—Yuan Zhun and others have already argued what is correct.
translations.idiomatic: As for temple-school tangles and terrace-pool miscellany—Yuan Zhun and others have already argued the right.

sentences.zh: 後卒于廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: Later he died as Vice Minister of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Later he died Vice Minister of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 贈濟州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made Inspector of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was Inspector of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 初，軌深為郭祚所知，祚堂謂子景尚曰：「封軌、高綽二人，並幹國之才，必應遠至。

translations.literal: At first Gui was deeply known by Guo Zuo; Zuo once told his son Jingshang in the hall: "Feng Gui and Gao Chuo—both are talents to steady the state and will surely reach far.
translations.idiomatic: At first Gui was deeply known by Guo Zuo; Zuo told his son Jingshang, "Feng Gui and Gao Chuo are talents to steady the state and will reach far.

sentences.zh: 吾平生不妄進舉，而每薦此二人，非直為國進賢，亦為汝等之津梁。

translations.literal: All my life I have not advanced men rashly, yet each time I recommend these two—not only to advance worthies for the state but also to make a bridge for you."
translations.idiomatic: All my life I have not advanced men rashly, yet each time I recommend these two—not only for the state but as a bridge for you."

sentences.zh: 」其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the weight in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the weight in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 軌既以方直自業，高綽亦以風概立名。

translations.literal: Gui because he took squareness and uprightness as his business and Gao Chuo likewise established his name on spirit and bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Gui took square uprightness as his business; Gao Chuo likewise stood on spirit and bearing.

sentences.zh: 高肇拜司徒，綽送迎往來，軌竟不詣。

translations.literal: When Gao Zhao was appointed Minister of Works, Chuo went back and forth on calls of courtesy; Gui in the end did not visit.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Zhao became Minister of Works, Chuo went back and forth on courtesy calls; Gui never visited.

sentences.zh: 綽顧不見軌，乃遽歸曰：「吾一生自謂無愆規矩，今日舉措不如封生遠矣。

translations.literal: Chuo, not seeing Gui, hurried home and said: "All my life I thought myself without breach of rule—today my conduct falls far short of Lord Feng."
translations.idiomatic: Chuo, not seeing Gui, hurried home and said, "All my life I thought myself without breach—today I fall far short of Lord Feng."

sentences.zh: 」軌以務德慎言，修身之本，奸回讒佞，世之巨害。

translations.literal: Gui, because cultivating virtue and cautious speech are the root of self-cultivation, while flattery and slander are the great harm of the age,
translations.idiomatic: Gui held that cultivating virtue and cautious speech root self-cultivation, while flattery and slander are the age's great harm,

sentences.zh: 乃為《務德》、《慎言》、《遠佞》、《防奸》四戒。

translations.literal: therefore made the "Four Admonitions": "Cultivate Virtue," "Cautious Speech," "Keep Distance from Flatterers," and "Guard against Villainy."
translations.idiomatic: and made the Four Admonitions: Cultivate Virtue, Cautious Speech, Keep Distance from Flatterers, Guard against Villainy.

sentences.zh: 文多不載。

translations.literal: The text is mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: The text is mostly not recorded.

sentences.zh: 長子偉伯，字君良，博學有才思。

translations.literal: His eldest son Weibo, styled Junliang, was broadly learned and had literary talent and thought.
translations.idiomatic: Eldest son Weibo, styled Junliang, was broadly learned with literary talent.

sentences.zh: 弱冠，除太學博士。

translations.literal: At twenty he was made Erudite of the Grand Academy.
translations.idiomatic: At twenty he was Grand Academy Erudite.

sentences.zh: 每朝廷大議，偉伯參焉。

translations.literal: Whenever the court held great deliberation Weibo took part.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court held great deliberation Weibo took part.

sentences.zh: 雅為太保崔光、僕射遊肇所知賞。

translations.literal: He was elegantly known to Grand Tutor Cui Guang and Vice Minister You Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Cui Guang and Vice Minister You Zhao knew and prized him.

sentences.zh: 太尉、清河王懌辟參軍事。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qinghe, Grand Marshal, Yi, recruited him as staff.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yi of Qinghe, Grand Marshal, recruited him.

sentences.zh: 懌親為《孝經解詁》，命偉伯為難例九條，皆發起隱漏。

translations.literal: Yi personally made a "Exegesis of the Classic of Filial Piety" and ordered Weibo nine difficult cases, all raising hidden flaws.
translations.idiomatic: Yi personally made an Exegesis of the Filial Classic and set Weibo nine hard cases, all raising hidden flaws.

sentences.zh: 偉伯又討論《禮》、《傳》、《詩》、《易》疑事數十條，儒者咸稱之。

translations.literal: Weibo also debated doubtful points in the "Rites," traditions, "Odes," and "Changes" in several tens of items; Confucians all praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo also debated doubtful points in Rites, traditions, Odes, and Changes in dozens of items; Confucians praised him.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷將經始明堂，廣集儒學，議其制度，九五之論，久而不定。

translations.literal: At that time the court was about to begin the Bright Hall and broadly gathered Confucian learning to deliberate its institution; debate on the nine-and-five theory long went unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The court was about to begin the Bright Hall and gathered Confucians; the nine-and-five debate long went unsettled.

sentences.zh: 偉伯乃搜檢經、緯，上《明堂圖說》六卷。

translations.literal: Weibo then searched the classics and their weft texts and submitted the "Explanation of the Bright Hall in Diagrams" in six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Weibo searched classics and weft texts and submitted Explanation of the Bright Hall in Diagrams in six scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又撰《封氏本錄》六卷。

translations.literal: He also compiled the "Feng Clan Original Record" in six scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Feng Clan Original Record in six scrolls.

sentences.zh: 正光末，尚書僕射蕭寶夤為關西行台，引為行台郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Zhengguang Vice Minister Xiao Baoyin was Western Expedition Commissioner for the Passes and recruited him as staff gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Zhengguang Vice Minister Xiao Baoyin was Western Expedition Commissioner and recruited him.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤為逆，偉伯與南平王固潛結關中豪右韋子粲等，謀舉義兵。

translations.literal: When Baoyin turned rebel Weibo secretly joined with Prince Nanping Gu and the great men of Guanzhong Wei Zican and others to plot raising righteous troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled Weibo secretly joined Prince Gu of Nanping and Guanzhong magnates Wei Zican and others to plot righteous troops.

sentences.zh: 事發，見殺。

translations.literal: The affair was exposed and he was killed.
translations.idiomatic: The affair was exposed and he was killed.

sentences.zh: 永安中，贈瀛州刺史，聽一子出身，無子，轉授弟翼。

translations.literal: In the Yong'an era he was posthumously made Inspector of Yingzhou; one son was permitted to enter service—with no son, the grant was transferred to his younger brother Yi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yong'an he was posthumously Inspector of Yingzhou; one son might enter service—with no son, the grant went to younger brother Yi.

sentences.zh: 翼弟述。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother was Shu.

sentences.zh: 述字君義，有幹用。

translations.literal: Shu, styled Junyi, had practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Shu, styled Junyi, had practical ability.

sentences.zh: 天平中，為三公郎中。

translations.literal: In the Tianping era he was Director for the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianping he was Director for the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 時增損舊事，為《麟趾新格》，其名法科條皆述所刪定。

translations.literal: At that time additions and subtractions to old affairs were made in the "New Regulations of the Unicorn Toe"; the titles of laws and articles were all cut and fixed by Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Additions and subtractions to old affairs became the Unicorn Toe New Regulations; law titles and articles were all cut and fixed by Shu.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，累遷大理卿。

translations.literal: When Qi received the mandate he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Court of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate he rose to Director of the Court of Justice.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，敕與錄尚書趙彥深、僕射魏收、尚書陽休之、國子祭酒馬敬德等議定律令。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing an edict ordered him with Recording Minister Zhao Yanshen, Vice Minister Wei Shou, Minister Yang Xiuzhi, National University Libationer Ma Jingde, and others to deliberate fixing laws and orders.
translations.idiomatic: In Heqing 3 an edict ordered him with Zhao Yanshen, Wei Shou, Yang Xiuzhi, Ma Jingde, and others to fix laws and orders.

sentences.zh: 歷位度支、五兵、殿中三尚書。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Minister of Revenue, Minister of the Five Armies, and Minister in the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was Minister of Revenue, Minister of the Five Armies, and Palace Minister.

sentences.zh: 述久為法官，明解律令，議斷平允，深為時人所稱。

translations.literal: Shu long served as a law officer, clearly understood statutes and ordinances, and in deliberation was even and fair; he was deeply praised by men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Shu long served as law officer, clearly knew statutes, deliberated evenly, and was deeply praised.

sentences.zh: 而厚積財產，一無分饋。

translations.literal: Yet he amassed wealth thickly and never gave a portion away.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he amassed wealth thickly and never gave away a portion.

sentences.zh: 雖至親密友，貧病困篤，亦絕於拯濟。

translations.literal: Even to close kin and intimate friends, when poor, ill, and in extremity, he also cut off relief.
translations.idiomatic: Even to close kin and intimate friends poor, ill, and dying he cut off relief.

sentences.zh: 朝野物論甚鄙之。

translations.literal: Public and private opinion of the time greatly despised him.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private opinion greatly despised him.

sentences.zh: 外貌方整，而不免請謁，回避進趣，頗致嗤駭。

translations.literal: Outwardly he was square and orderly, yet he could not avoid solicitation; in advancing and retreating to avoid he quite drew sneers.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly square and orderly, yet he could not avoid solicitation; dodging advance drew sneers.

sentences.zh: 前妻河內司馬氏。

translations.literal: His former wife was of the Sima clan of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: His former wife was of the Sima clan of Henei.

sentences.zh: 一息為娶隴西李士元女，大輸財聘。

translations.literal: For his son he took in marriage the daughter of Li Shiyuan of Longxi with a great bride-price.
translations.idiomatic: For his son he married Li Shiyuan's daughter of Longxi with a great bride-price.

sentences.zh: 及將成禮，猶競懸違。

translations.literal: When the rites were about to be completed they still competed in delay.
translations.idiomatic: When rites were about to be completed they still competed in delay.

sentences.zh: 述忽取所供養像，對士元打像為誓。

translations.literal: Shu suddenly took the image supplied for worship, faced Shiyuan, and struck the image to swear.
translations.idiomatic: Shu suddenly took the worship image, faced Shiyuan, and struck the image to swear.

sentences.zh: 士元笑曰：「封公何處常得應急像，須誓便用？

translations.literal: Shiyuan laughed and said: "Where does Lord Feng always get emergency images that he must swear at once?"
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan laughed, "Where does Lord Feng always get emergency images to swear at once?"

sentences.zh: 」一息娶范陽盧莊之女，述又經府訴云：「送騍乃嫌腳跛，評田則雲咸薄，銅器又嫌古廢。

translations.literal: For his son's marriage he took the daughter of Lu Zhuang of Fanyang; Shu again appealed to the office saying: "The presented horse was faulted as lame in the hoof; the assessed fields were said too thin; bronze vessels were faulted as old and cast off."
translations.idiomatic: For another son he took Lu Zhuang's daughter of Fanyang; Shu appealed, "The presented horse was faulted lame; fields too thin; bronze vessels old and cast off."

sentences.zh: 」皆為吝嗇所及，每致紛紜。

translations.literal: All were matters stinginess touched; each time it led to quarrels.
translations.idiomatic: All were touched by stinginess; each led to quarrels.

sentences.zh: 子元茜，位太子舍人。

translations.literal: His son Yuanqian held the post of Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Son Yuanqian was Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household.

sentences.zh: 述弟詢，字景文，窺涉經史，以清素自持。

translations.literal: Shu's younger brother Xun, styled Jingwen, ranged through the classics and histories and held himself by pure plainness.
translations.idiomatic: Younger brother Xun, styled Jingwen, ranged classics and histories and held himself by pure plainness.

sentences.zh: 位尚書左丞、濟南太守。

translations.literal: He held the posts of Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat and Administrator of Jinan.
translations.idiomatic: He was Left Assistant Minister and Administrator of Jinan.

sentences.zh: 曆官皆有幹局才具，臨郡甚著聲績。

translations.literal: In every office he had practical capacity and talent; in governing commanderies his reputation for achievement was quite marked.
translations.idiomatic: Every office showed practical talent; governing commanderies his achievement was marked.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Kaihuang era of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Sui's Kaihuang era.

sentences.zh: 論曰：崔逞文學器識，當年之俊，忽微慮遠，俱以為災。

translations.literal: Discussion: Cui Cheng's literary learning and discernment were the excellence of his age; suddenly reduced to insignificance though they thought far ahead—both met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Cui Cheng's learning and discernment crowned his age; suddenly made small, though they looked far ahead—both met calamity.

sentences.zh: 休立身有本，當官著稱。

translations.literal: Xiu in establishing himself had root; in holding office he bore repute.
translations.idiomatic: Xiu rooted himself in principle; in office he won repute.

sentences.zh: 長儒才望之美，禍因驕物，雖有周公之才，猶且為累。

translations.literal: Changru's beauty of talent and repute—disaster came through arrogant things; though he had the Duke of Zhou's talent, it still became a burden.
translations.idiomatic: Changru's talent and repute invited disaster through pride; though he had the Duke of Zhou's gifts, they still weighed him down.

sentences.zh: 況未足諭其高下，能無及乎？

translations.literal: How much less when one cannot discuss their higher and lower—can one not reach them?
translations.idiomatic: How much less for those who cannot be weighed against such men—who can reach them?

sentences.zh: 贍詞韻溫雅，風神秀髮，固人望也。

translations.literal: Zhan's phrasing was warm and elegant, his spirit brilliant in emergence—truly men's expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's diction was warm and elegant, his spirit bright in emergence—he was truly what men hoped for.

sentences.zh: 王憲名公之孫，老見優異。

translations.literal: Wang Xian, grandson of a famous lord, in old age was seen with exceptional favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xian, grandson of a famous minister, in old age was treated with exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 元景昆季履道，標映人倫，美哉！

translations.literal: Yuan Jing and his brothers walked the Way and shone in human relations—beautiful!
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan Jing brothers walked the Way and shone among men—beautiful!

sentences.zh: 封回克光家世，隆之勤勞霸業，子繪實隆堂構，可謂載德者矣。

translations.literal: Feng Hui could brighten his house's generations; Longzhi toiled in the hegemonic enterprise; Zihui truly raised the hall's timbers—one may call them men who bore virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui brightened his clan across generations; Longzhi toiled in the hegemonic work; Zihui truly raised the hall's frame—men who carried virtue.

sentences.zh: 君義聚斂嗇吝，無乃鄙哉！

translations.literal: Junyi amassed and was stingy and mean—perhaps contemptible!
translations.idiomatic: Junyi heaped wealth and clung to it—was that not contemptible?
